items.title: PCR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Strengthening Environmental Pathogen Surveillance and Public Health Preparedness Across United States Communities
items.summary: This review paper examines the role of PCR-based molecular diagnostic technologies in strengthening environmental pathogen surveillance and public health preparedness across the United States. The authors critically assess advances across multiple PCR platforms, including conventional, quantitative, digital, and multiplex approaches, as well as point-of-need diagnostic systems, evaluating their application to complex environmental matrices such as wastewater, surface water, air, and soil. The review addresses technical aspects including assay design, sample processing, quality assurance, and computational data interpretation, while also considering integration with national surveillance infrastructures such as wastewater-based epidemiology programs. The authors find that PCR technologies offer substantial advantages over conventional culture-based methods in terms of speed, sensitivity, and throughput, and have demonstrated clear utility for early outbreak detection, antimicrobial resistance monitoring, and evidence-based decision-making. The review concludes by identifying ongoing implementation challenges and highlighting opportunities to combine artificial intelligence with molecular diagnostics to further enhance environmental surveillance capacity and public health resilience.
items.venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
items.citation: Iyanuoluwa Oluwafemi. PCR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Strengthening Environmental Pathogen Surveillance and Public Health Preparedness Across United States Communities. International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews. 2026

items.title: Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques
items.summary: This review examines the full landscape of bacterial identification methods, motivated by the ongoing global burden of infectious diseases and the escalating challenge of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed techniques spanning classical approaches such as microscopy, culture, and biochemical testing through to immunological, proteomic, and spectroscopy-based methods, as well as molecular tools including various forms of PCR, sequencing, and metagenomics. They also assessed the role of artificial intelligence in enhancing analytical performance and considered emerging technologies such as CRISPR-based diagnostics and phage- and nanomaterial-based detection systems. The review concludes that integrating these diverse approaches can improve the accuracy, speed, and breadth of bacterial identification across clinical, veterinary, agricultural, and environmental contexts. However, the authors caution that standardization remains a critical priority, particularly regarding variability in bioinformatics frameworks that currently limits the routine implementation of whole-genome sequencing.
items.citation: Ina Gajić, Milos Jovicevic, Dušan Kekić et al.. Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive sequence analysis reveals the vast β-lactam resistome
items.summary: This study investigated the environmental distribution and diversity of β-lactamase resistance genes, which are widespread among bacteria but remain poorly characterized in terms of their full scope and ecological context. Using an integrated bioinformatics and experimental workflow applied to large-scale sequence data, the researchers constructed a comprehensive taxonomy-environment map of putative β-lactamase sequences across bacterial phyla and diverse ecosystems. They discovered a reservoir of putative β-lactamases spanning all four β-lactamase classes that far exceeds what is currently catalogued in existing antibiotic resistance gene databases, with these genes appearing at frequencies approaching that of a core housekeeping gene across environmental samples. Wastewater and plant-associated environments showed particular enrichment of putative β-lactamases, but terrestrial and aquatic settings also harbored close homologs of clinically relevant variants. The authors present a reusable mapping tool and workflow that reveals a largely unexplored β-lactamase resistome with substantial potential for mobilization into clinical pathogens.
items.citation: Sevan Gholipour, John Z. Chen, Dong‐Kyu Lee et al.. Comprehensive sequence analysis reveals the vast β-lactam resistome. Microbiome. 2026

items.title: Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host
items.summary: This study investigated whether wastewater-based surveillance can reliably reflect community-level antibiotic resistance patterns by examining how antibiotic resistance gene abundances in sewage relate to clinical antibiotic use. The researchers combined a multi-year record of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions with an intensive, year-long metagenomic sampling campaign at a single wastewater treatment plant to distinguish signals originating from human hosts versus those shaped by in-sewer microbial ecology. They found that resistance genes associated with Enterobacteriaceae tracked closely and contemporaneously with antibiotic usage patterns, while those linked to Pseudomonadaceae exhibited lagged correlations of one to three months, reflecting the distinct ecological behavior of these bacteria within sewer systems. Statistical modeling further confirmed that the dynamics of Pseudomonas populations in sewage were associated with delayed responses to specific antibiotic use after controlling for sewage characteristics and seasonality. The findings demonstrate that wastewater surveillance can meaningfully capture epidemiologically relevant antibiotic resistance trends, but only when the ecological factors governing different bacterial taxa in sewage are explicitly accounted for.
items.citation: Connor Brown, MA. Rumi, Lauren F. McDaniel et al.. Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
items.summary: This review paper examined the use of wastewater surveillance conducted on aircraft and at airports as a public health tool for detecting and monitoring infectious pathogens among traveling populations. The authors conducted a structured narrative review synthesizing current evidence on this approach, with particular attention to the methodological factors that influence the validity and interpretation of surveillance signals, including sampling design, nucleic acid extraction, molecular detection, sequencing, and quality assurance. The strongest evidence base comes from detection and variant monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in aircraft lavatory and airport terminal wastewater, though the authors emphasize that signal detectability is shaped by numerous variables such as pathogen shedding dynamics, flight duration, and assay sensitivity. The review cautions that wastewater signals are aggregate and matrix-dependent, meaning they cannot be interpreted as individual diagnoses, evidence of transmission, or definitive attribution to specific flights or populations. The authors conclude that extending this surveillance approach to multiple pathogens, including enteric and respiratory viruses, vaccine-preventable diseases, and antimicrobial resistance markers, will require pathogen-specific validation, and that the overall value of aviation wastewater surveillance depends on translating technical signals into scientifically interpretable public health evidence.
items.citation: Vaidya SR, Pandey PG, Giri S et al.. Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.
items.summary: This study examined how the structure of urban wastewater infrastructure influences the detection and interpretation of multiple respiratory virus signals in wastewater-based epidemiology. Conducted in Mumbai, where sewer networks are fragmented and partially connected, the researchers compared surveillance data from centralised sewage treatment plants and decentralised open drains, collecting samples across two monitoring periods and testing for SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus using RT-qPCR. Centralised treatment plants showed higher and more consistent viral detection rates, reflecting signal integration across larger populations, while open drains displayed greater temporal variability consistent with localised, short-term transmission dynamics. SARS-CoV-2 was reliably detected across both sampling node types, whereas influenza detection was more sporadic and suggested seasonal patterns, with co-circulation of influenza A and B observed in one monitoring period. The authors conclude that wastewater signal profiles reflect both pathogen-specific biology and the structural characteristics of the sampling network, and they advocate for integrated surveillance frameworks combining centralised and decentralised nodes alongside clinical validation to improve epidemiological inference.
items.citation: Shaikh A, Nikam S, Mistry N. Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.. Food and environmental virology. 2026

items.title: From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.
items.summary: Wastewater surveillance offers a population-level window into infectious disease transmission that can capture cases missed by clinical reporting, including asymptomatic infections. This study developed and validated methods for detecting Salmonella in wastewater, combining polyethylene glycol precipitation for sample concentration, magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction, and quantitative PCR targeting. These methods were deployed across Oklahoma over a two-year period to monitor Salmonella dynamics in the community. The surveillance system revealed seasonal transmission patterns, provided approximately one week of advance notice relative to clinical case reporting, and uncovered outbreak activity that passive surveillance had failed to detect. Despite limitations including low pathogen concentrations in wastewater and an inability to resolve Salmonella serovars, the approach demonstrates clear potential as an early warning and outbreak detection tool when used alongside traditional public health surveillance.
items.citation: Kuhn KG, Shelton K, Rimal B et al.. From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.). 2027

items.title: Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
items.summary: This study examined how a major international mass gathering sporting event influenced the infectious disease pathogen landscape in a host city by employing wastewater-based surveillance as a complementary public health monitoring tool. Researchers collected wastewater samples from three water reclamation facilities before, during, and after the relevant matches, testing them with multiplexed qualitative PCR panels covering a broad range of respiratory and gastrointestinal pathogens. The primary analysis found no statistically significant differences in pathogen detection between the pre-event and event periods across facilities. A sensitivity analysis that included the post-event period identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2 detection, but this increase mirrored broader regional and national trends, making it difficult to attribute to the event itself. The study demonstrates the feasibility of qualitative multiplexed PCR assays for population-level pathogen surveillance during mass gatherings, while acknowledging that the absence of quantitative data, wide confidence intervals, and limited post-event sampling constrain definitive conclusions.
items.citation: Raymo N, Kraft CS, Gulick D et al.. Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings
items.citation: Ahmed W, Medlicott K, Nolan M. A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings. ACS ES&T water. 2026

items.title: Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards
items.summary: This paper proposes a framework for an artificial intelligence-powered occupational health surveillance system intended to overcome the limitations of traditional monitoring approaches, such as delayed hazard detection and poor adaptability to changing workplace conditions. The system integrates wearable devices and Internet of Things sensors to continuously collect data on both environmental factors and individual employee health metrics, which are then processed through machine learning algorithms and predictive analytics to identify anomalies and forecast emerging risks. A user-facing dashboard provides visualized insights, automated reporting, and actionable recommendations, while also supporting regulatory compliance through documentation and audit trails. The authors argue that combining real-time data collection with AI-driven analysis enables proactive intervention before hazards escalate into serious incidents. The proposed framework is designed to be scalable across diverse industries, positioning it as a broadly applicable solution for improving workplace safety and employee well-being.
items.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.citation: Cynthia Obianuju Ozobu. Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards. WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of different SARS-CoV-2 variants as they co-circulated during the pandemic. The researchers developed a method that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts alongside genomic sequencing data, moving beyond approaches that rely solely on variant frequency proportions, which cannot capture full epidemiological dynamics. By applying this framework to data from US states over a period spanning early 2021 to early 2022, they were able to estimate variant-specific effective reproduction numbers alongside variant frequencies simultaneously. The model also incorporates structured relationships across time series to estimate fixed growth advantages attributable to specific variants across different geographic locations. Their approach yields estimates of transmission advantage for multiple variants of concern and interest that are consistent across locations, demonstrating the value of integrating case and sequencing data for epidemiological inference.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
items.summary: This paper investigates electron thermopower in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, focusing on how the structure of Fermi-surface deformations—rather than just their relaxation rates—influences transport. The authors introduce the concept of "thermal dressing," which describes local temperature changes associated with these deformations, and show that thermopower probes this structure directly. They find that thermopower overshoots its hydrodynamic value as a function of wave vector before settling at half that value in the ballistic limit, a phenomenon driven by collinear scattering that redistributes energy across the Fermi surface. Notably, the excess thermopower exhibits only a logarithmic dependence on temperature rather than the linear scaling expected for a Fermi liquid, defining a distinct thermographic transport regime that differs fundamentally from tomographic effects seen in charge conductivity. The authors argue that this overshoot is robust against realistic disorder and should be experimentally detectable in thermocouple measurements using high-mobility samples.
items.citation: Johannes Hofmann. Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
items.summary: This paper investigated the properties of an early galaxy to search for evidence of Population III stars — the first generation of stars formed from primordial light elements following Big Bang Nucleosynthesis. Using deep spectroscopy from the James Webb Space Telescope, the researchers observed a strongly gravitationally lensed galaxy at a redshift corresponding to roughly one billion years after the Big Bang. They detected helium and hydrogen emission lines at high significance, along with an exceptionally low oxygen abundance in the interstellar medium, estimated at a tiny fraction of the solar value, derived from weak oxygen emission lines. The observed ratios of helium-to-hydrogen emission are consistent with theoretical predictions for the extreme ionizing radiation fields and low metallicities expected from Population III stellar populations, though contributions from accreting black holes cannot be ruled out. These findings reveal that pockets of nearly pristine, chemically unenriched gas persisted well into the first billion years of cosmic history and that such environments are dominated by very massive stars, offering a potential observational window into the conditions where the universe's first stars are predicted to form.
items.citation: Takahiro Morishita, Massimo Stiavelli, Tommaso Treu et al.. Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of object penetration in interactive video world models, where simulated agents pass through physical obstacles rather than being blocked by them. The authors created a benchmark called NoPeBench to systematically evaluate how existing open-source world models handle physical obstacles, finding that none reliably prevent penetration failures. Interestingly, they discovered that despite these failures, the hidden states of diffusion transformers already encode sufficient information to predict whether a given action will cause a penetration violation. Building on this insight, they developed NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that trains a small prediction head on top of frozen diffusion transformer hidden states to classify candidate actions as safe or unsafe, then substitutes unsafe actions with safe alternatives that preserve the original intent. The resulting system dramatically reduces physical violation rates across multiple video world models and generalizes zero-shot to open-domain imagery, different viewpoints, and moving obstacles.
items.citation: Yuhang Dai, Yinwei Wu, Ziyue Lin et al.. Non-penetrating World Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: This paper investigated the integration of neuromorphic sensing and computing into a complete autonomous robotic system, addressing the gap between isolated benchmarks and real-world deployment. The researchers built a four-wheel rover platform combining three perception pipelines: a conventional audio tagging system running on a GPU, a spiking neural network deployed on dedicated neuromorphic audio hardware for on-chip sound classification, and an event-camera-based spiking detector for traffic cone recognition. All pipelines were containerized and coordinated through a robotics middleware framework, with a dispatcher translating detected classes into robot behaviors to close the perception-action loop. The platform was demonstrated in a proof-of-concept scenario requiring real-time multimodal perception, showing that the neuromorphic audio chip could handle the full processing chain from raw microphone input to classification entirely on-chip. The work establishes the feasibility of integrating neuromorphic hardware components into a functional, multimodal robotic platform operating under real-time constraints.
items.citation: Guillem Fustier-Castillo, Ruben Ribes-Serrano, Javier Naranjo-Alcazar et al.. Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
items.summary: This paper reframes Rydberg-atom receivers within the established framework of microwave-photonics, specifically treating them as intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical links in which the laser-driven atomic vapor acts as the modulator. The authors derive a closed-form expression for the transmission of a warm vapor by averaging the four-level atomic response over thermal velocity distributions, and from this single function extract standard receiver figures of merit including conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range. They find that the instantaneous bandwidth equals half the width of the electromagnetically induced transparency window, and that the local oscillator governs even-order linearity by setting the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field strength. Closed-form predictions agree well with a full velocity-resolved density-matrix model for gain slope and intercepts, though group delay is underestimated, and the sensing volume is shown to circumvent the Chu limit. Despite this advantage, the analysis concludes that the noise figure of a warm vapor is too poor to position Rydberg-atom receivers as general replacements for conventional antenna and low-noise amplifier systems.
items.citation: David Rosser. A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations in existing segmentation evaluation metrics when reference annotations contain systematic biases such as merged touching objects or fragmented instances. The authors identify that standard metrics like Panoptic Quality treat all instances equally and cannot distinguish between legitimate segmentation errors and artifacts introduced by heuristic or biased reference annotations. To address this, they developed Star Panoptic Quality, a novel evaluation framework that constructs a star forest from the bipartite matching graph between predicted and reference instances, isolating distinct failure modes into clean, merge, and split categories. The framework then computes a final metric by applying individually adjustable weights to each failure mode, allowing practitioners to penalize or tolerate specific types of errors depending on known biases in their reference data. Through multiple experiments, the authors demonstrate that their approach both enables targeted evaluation and serves as a diagnostic tool for characterizing the prevalence of different segmentation failure modes.
items.citation: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.. Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Why emerging infectious diseases are becoming more complex in the twenty-first century.
items.summary: This review examines why emerging infectious diseases have grown increasingly complex in the twenty-first century, arguing that pathogen-centered models alone are insufficient to understand modern infectious disease threats. The paper synthesizes how interactions among microbial adaptation, reservoir ecology, climate change, land-use change, globalization, urbanization, and unequal public health capacity collectively shape disease emergence and spread. Drawing on case examples spanning Ebola, SARS, avian influenza, MERS, COVID-19, Nipah virus, and mpox, the review demonstrates that containment outcomes depend on the interplay of transmission biology, exposure settings, timing of infectiousness, and health system readiness rather than on any single factor. Antimicrobial resistance is highlighted as a parallel, slower-moving crisis in which resistant organisms and genes circulate across hospitals, communities, food systems, and environmental reservoirs simultaneously. The authors conclude that future preparedness must move upstream of initial human cases, integrating ecological prevention, reservoir-host surveillance, molecular insight, health care resilience, equity, and sustained global cooperation into unified control strategies.
items.citation: Li YY, Tay FR. Why emerging infectious diseases are becoming more complex in the twenty-first century.. One health (Amsterdam, Netherlands). 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infection in its intermediate snail hosts, addressing the limited sensitivity of conventional parasitological diagnostic methods used in schistosomiasis surveillance. The researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of *S. mansoni*, optimized for a simple, single-temperature reaction, and evaluated its performance against microscopy, conventional PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two endemic countries. The assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory conditions, outperforming microscopy and performing comparably to real-time PCR, while in field surveys it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR and identified infections entirely missed by parasitological techniques. The authors conclude that this LAMP assay is a sensitive, specific, and field-deployable tool suitable for routine snail surveillance and early detection of changes in schistosomiasis transmission risk.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Towards point-of-care diagnostics of neglected tropical diseases using nucleic acid amplification tests.
items.summary: This paper reviewed the state of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification tests for neglected tropical diseases, a group of conditions that carry a substantial global burden but have historically received less diagnostic innovation than other infectious diseases. The authors conducted a systematic analysis of studies to evaluate current point-of-care nucleic acid amplification test developments, focusing on operational feasibility and implementation barriers across the full testing workflow rather than on analytical performance metrics alone. Recurring positive developments identified included simplified extraction methods, integrated device platforms, smartphone-based result interpretation, and workflows designed to be independent of cold chains and electricity. Despite these advances, significant technical, analytical, and implementation barriers were found to prevent most current prototypes from transitioning into field-deployable tools. The review concludes that the majority of nucleic acid amplification test developments for neglected tropical diseases do not yet meet World Health Organization criteria for point-of-care application in resource-limited settings, and that careful end-to-end evaluation from sample collection to field implementation is necessary to close this diagnostic gap.
items.citation: Priem N, Rodriguez-Mateos P, Waweru H et al.. Towards point-of-care diagnostics of neglected tropical diseases using nucleic acid amplification tests.. Analytical and bioanalytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk
items.summary: This study developed and validated a rapid molecular detection platform for *Streptococcus agalactiae*, a major cause of bovine mastitis, targeting the conserved *cfb* gene. The researchers combined recombinase polymerase amplification with a prokaryotic Argonaute protein system to create two readout formats: a real-time fluorescence assay and a lateral flow dipstick assay. Both formats demonstrated high analytical sensitivity and specificity, with no cross-reactivity against non-target bacteria, and the fluorescence format achieved a lower detection limit than the dipstick format. Field validation using bovine milk samples from multiple dairy-farming regions in China showed that both molecular formats performed in complete concordance with a standardized quantitative PCR assay, and all molecular methods detected substantially more positive samples than conventional bacteriological culture. The findings indicate that this dual-readout platform offers a rapid, reliable, and practical alternative for on-site or laboratory detection of *S. agalactiae* in dairy settings.
items.citation: Xujie Zhao, Yuying Du, Qianlei Zhu et al.. Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk. Veterinary Sciences. 2026

items.title: Smartphone-integrated RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection system with microneedle sampling for early point-of-care diagnosis of potato late blight
items.citation: Jinbiao Zhao, Hanbo Xu, Shifang Fei et al.. Smartphone-integrated RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection system with microneedle sampling for early point-of-care diagnosis of potato late blight. Biosensors and Bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review paper examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious clinical syndromes, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which carry significant risks of illness and death. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics, and clinical management, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir populations and increase spillover risk to humans. The review identifies critical gaps in surveillance and diagnostic capacity, especially in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-informed early warning systems are highlighted as promising tools for improving outbreak detection and response. The authors argue that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks linking human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and preparing for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Molecular engineering of CRISPR/Cas12a: from activity enhancement to exponential signal amplification
items.summary: This review examines strategies to overcome the fundamental limitations of CRISPR/Cas12a as a molecular diagnostic tool, specifically its linear signal output and constrained amplification efficiency that reduce detection sensitivity. Rather than coupling Cas12a with external pre-amplification steps, the authors focus on molecular engineering approaches that intrinsically enhance its performance, representing a shift away from the conventional one-target-one-enzyme paradigm. The review systematically covers engineering strategies including guide RNA reprogramming, activator strand design, reporter probe optimization, and reaction environment tuning, all aimed at improving the enzyme's catalytic kinetics, specificity, and signal generation. Collectively, these approaches enable ultrasensitive detection of both nucleic acid and non-nucleic acid targets without requiring pre-amplification, simplifying workflows and reducing operational uncertainty. The authors propose that these integrated engineering solutions lay the groundwork for next-generation point-of-care diagnostic platforms suitable for deployment in field and clinical settings.
items.citation: Qing-Nan Li, Qi-Fan Yang, Wei-Liang Jin et al.. Molecular engineering of CRISPR/Cas12a: from activity enhancement to exponential signal amplification. Chemical Science. 2026

items.title: Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques
items.summary: This review examines the full landscape of bacterial identification methods, motivated by the ongoing global burden of infectious diseases and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed techniques spanning classical approaches such as microscopy, culture, and biochemical testing through to immunological, proteomic, and spectroscopic methods, as well as molecular tools including various forms of PCR, sequencing, and metagenomics. Emerging technologies such as CRISPR-based diagnostics and phage- and nanomaterial-based detection systems are also discussed alongside the growing role of artificial intelligence in enhancing analytical performance. The review finds that while the integration of these diverse approaches promises improved accuracy and speed across clinical, veterinary, agricultural, and environmental contexts, conventional methods remain constrained by slow turnaround times, limited sensitivity, and difficulty with fastidious or uncultivable organisms. The authors conclude that realizing the full potential of modern methods, particularly whole-genome sequencing, requires prioritizing standardization of bioinformatics frameworks, as variability in algorithmic cut-off values currently hinders routine implementation.
items.citation: Ina Gajić, Milos Jovicevic, Dušan Kekić et al.. Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Latent generative search unlocks de novo design of untapped biomolecular interactions at scale
items.summary: This paper addresses a longstanding challenge in de novo protein design: creating binders for polar, solvent-exposed epitopes and small flexible ligands such as carbohydrates, which lack the hydrophobic contacts that existing methods exploit. The authors developed a framework called latent generative search, which uses reward-guided inference-time search to steer a generative model that co-designs protein sequence and structure simultaneously in a continuous latent space, eliminating the inverse-folding step required by conventional approaches. Testing more than one million designs through multiplexed phage display, their method outperformed all other approaches evaluated, producing more experimentally validated binders across therapeutic receptors, a viral attachment protein, and intracellular signalling targets. Notably, the co-designed sequences outperformed those produced by post-hoc sequence redesign of the same structures. The approach also achieved a first in the field by generating de novo proteins that bind free carbohydrates, including one capable of discriminating between blood-group antigens, demonstrating access to a target class previously considered beyond the reach of computational protein design.
items.citation: Kieran Didi, Danny Reidenbach, Matthew Penner et al.. Latent generative search unlocks de novo design of untapped biomolecular interactions at scale. bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory). 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of classifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using electroencephalography signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing recordings from multiple participants across five task conditions, linking continuous brain signals to precomputed measurements spanning seven feature families and over one hundred feature definitions, while documenting quality decisions throughout. The goal was to create a resource enabling consistent, fair comparisons of EEG-derived features across shared time intervals and participants. Technical validation confirmed strong signal retention after preprocessing, and an illustrative machine learning analysis using gradient-boosted trees demonstrated that classification performance varied across task conditions, with one task showing stronger group discrimination than others. The authors emphasize that these results are descriptive and do not establish diagnostic validity, but the publicly released dataset and software are intended to support reproducible research in this area.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations in evaluating instance segmentation when reference annotations contain systematic biases such as merged or split instances, which arise from heuristic approximation or expert disagreement. The authors identify that standard metrics like Panoptic Quality treat all instances equally and cannot distinguish valid segmentation errors from artifacts introduced by biased reference annotations. To address this, they propose Star Panoptic Quality, a novel evaluation framework that constructs a star forest from the bipartite matching graph between predicted and reference instances, decomposing matches into clean, merge, and split categories that isolate distinct failure modes. The framework then computes a final metric by allowing practitioners to apply individual weights to each failure mode, enabling flexible penalization or leniency depending on the known biases in the reference data. Through multiple experiments, the authors demonstrate that their approach both enables targeted evaluation of specific segmentation failure modes and serves as a diagnostic tool for revealing their prevalence in a dataset.
items.citation: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.. Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary: This paper introduces the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, an industrial architecture designed to automate and scale user experience evaluation in large-scale web search, addressing limitations of traditional survey-based methods and coarse automated metrics. The framework combines two complementary systems: a macro-level sentiment regression detector built on a fine-tuned encoder-decoder language model that processes telemetry features to identify UX regressions at scale, and a micro-level multimodal system that analyzes visual renderings and spatial layouts of web result pages to quantify user effort in reaching satisfactory results. The macro tier uses multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering to improve precision while matching recall on validated regressions, dramatically reducing measurement latency from weeks to hours and cutting survey overhead substantially. The micro tier employs a multimodal large language model enhanced by reinforcement learning-based prompt optimization and an AI judge to diagnose layout friction and content quality issues, achieving meaningful improvement in classification performance. Together, the two tiers enable accurate, granular, and scalable UX attribution capable of processing hundreds of thousands of live experiment queries daily.
items.citation: Yi Ding, Gaurav Kumar, Rui Min et al.. The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate how well vision-language models can interpret electronic navigational charts, which encode safety-critical maritime information through complex symbols, geometries, and standardized notation. The authors constructed a large question-answering dataset derived from thousands of official nautical charts, organizing questions around four capability areas: perceiving chart features, spatial reasoning, combined perception and spatial reasoning, and applying navigational knowledge to assess chart changes. A progressive subset of questions traces linked reasoning chains from detecting a chart change through to evaluating its navigational significance, enabling fine-grained analysis of model reasoning. Evaluation of multiple open-weight vision-language models revealed substantial weaknesses in fine-grained nautical feature recognition and spatially grounded reasoning, though providing relevant perceptual and spatial context as evidence improved accuracy on change-criticality judgments. The benchmark is presented as a diagnostic resource for understanding model limitations in safety-critical maritime chart interpretation tasks.
items.citation: Jiyoon Pyo, Jacob Arndt, Yao-Yi Chiang et al.. ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of representing complex financial documents—which combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, and time-dependent facts—in a structured form suitable for automated reasoning. The authors developed a schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal knowledge graphs from financial documents, using a pipeline that includes large language model extraction across overlapping document windows, multi-strategy entity resolution, and provenance tracking to maintain traceability to source evidence. The approach incorporates temporal merge constraints, deterministic edge deduplication, and conflict-aware property management to preserve reporting-period validity and issuer identity. To assess the resulting graphs independently of downstream applications, the authors also proposed an intrinsic evaluation framework spanning multiple weighted quality dimensions and hard validation gates alongside structural diagnostics. By decoupling graph quality assessment from retrieval and answer generation tasks, the framework enables systematic diagnosis and iterative refinement of financial knowledge graph construction.
items.citation: Samarth Sarin, Lovepreet Singh, Dhagash Mehta. Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
items.summary: This paper investigates the robustness of Vision-Language Models when applied to scientific tasks under realistic conditions where input information may be erroneous or incomplete. The authors introduce the concept of Scientific Model Robustness, encompassing a model's capacity to detect anomalies, evaluate whether a problem is solvable, and self-calibrate in the face of information inconsistencies or insufficiency. To operationalize this, they construct RoSci-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark built through a seed-variant strategy covering six types of input degradation, and use it to evaluate existing models. They also propose RoSci-Agent, a framework employing a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline that vets problem premises before reasoning begins. Their findings reveal that current VLMs often attempt to answer questions with invalid or incomplete premises, while RoSci-Agent demonstrates improved overall robustness compared to standalone models on the benchmark.
items.citation: Junying Wang, Yijin Guo, Yalun Wu et al.. RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers in the Blood for Sepsis Diagnosis.
items.summary: This study addressed the critical need for early and accurate sepsis diagnosis in critically ill patients by searching for novel blood-based protein biomarkers. Using a multiphase approach that combined data-independent acquisition proteomics, targeted mass spectrometry verification, ELISA-based clinical confirmation, and machine learning, the researchers systematically identified and validated candidate biomarkers across discovery, verification, and prospective clinical cohorts. Three consistently downregulated proteins—α-2-HS-glycoprotein, clusterin, and kallistatin—were identified as the most robust candidates and combined into a triple-biomarker panel using a random forest model. When tested prospectively in patients with suspected sepsis, the panel demonstrated strong discriminatory performance that significantly outperformed the conventional inflammatory markers procalcitonin and C-reactive protein. The authors conclude that this three-protein panel represents a clinically translatable diagnostic tool capable of rapidly and accurately identifying sepsis at an early stage.
items.citation: Fan Z, Chen M, Sun Y et al.. Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers in the Blood for Sepsis Diagnosis.. Journal of proteome research. 2026

items.title: Circulating calprotectin and S100A8/A9-related biomarkers for diagnosis and prognostic stratification in adult acute infection and sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether circulating calprotectin and related S100A8/A9 biomarkers can accurately diagnose acute infection and sepsis and stratify prognosis in adults. The researchers searched multiple biomedical databases and trial registries, pooling data from independent cohorts using random-effects models for diagnostic and prognostic areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve, alongside bivariate analyses of threshold-based sensitivity and specificity. Overall diagnostic performance was moderate across both sepsis and acute infection outcomes, with pooled discriminative ability falling well short of what would be needed for a stand-alone diagnostic test, and prognostic discrimination for mortality was similarly modest. Threshold-based analyses revealed an asymmetric trade-off between sensitivity and specificity that varied by clinical context, and paired comparisons with other biomarkers did not establish clear superiority for calprotectin. The authors concluded that these biomarkers may serve as adjunctive indicators of host immune response in selected clinical contrasts, but that the very low certainty of current evidence precludes their use as universal diagnostic thresholds or replacements for established biomarkers and clinical judgment.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Liao YS, Deng YP, Song JL et al.. Circulating calprotectin and S100A8/A9-related biomarkers for diagnosis and prognostic stratification in adult acute infection and sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Serum TLR2, TLR4, TLR2/TLR4 Ratio, and ESM1 in Sepsis: A Single-Center Prospective Observational Study of Diagnostic and Prognostic Associations.
items.summary: This study investigated whether serum levels of endothelial cell-specific molecule-1, toll-like receptor 2, toll-like receptor 4, and the ratio between the two receptors could serve as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers in sepsis. Researchers conducted a prospective observational study comparing biomarker levels between patients hospitalized with sepsis and ambulatory controls, while also examining associations between these markers and in-hospital mortality. Toll-like receptor 2 levels were numerically lower in sepsis patients than controls, but this difference did not reach statistical significance, and receiver operating characteristic analysis suggested only modest diagnostic performance. No significant differences were found for endothelial cell-specific molecule-1, toll-like receptor 4, or the receptor ratio between groups, and none of the biomarkers were significantly associated with mortality. The authors conclude that these markers lack clear diagnostic or prognostic utility in their cohort and that further validation in larger studies with clinically relevant comparison groups is needed.
items.citation: Usanmaz M, Görgün S, Ocak M et al.. Serum TLR2, TLR4, TLR2/TLR4 Ratio, and ESM1 in Sepsis: A Single-Center Prospective Observational Study of Diagnostic and Prognostic Associations.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated <i>in vitro</i> diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of sepsis biomarkers with a focus on those that have advanced from laboratory discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostic use. The authors surveyed a broad range of markers—from established soluble proteins such as procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, and lactate to emerging severity and host-response markers, as well as transcriptomic, cellular, and functional immune assays—evaluating them not solely on diagnostic performance but also on biological rationale, sample requirements, turnaround time, regulatory status, and clinical workflow compatibility. The review identifies a persistent and substantial gap between the large number of proposed sepsis biomarkers and the small subset that has successfully navigated regulatory pathways toward certified clinical deployment. The authors situate this gap within an evolving regulatory environment shaped by frameworks such as the EU In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation and its associated database rollout. They conclude that future sepsis diagnostics will likely shift away from isolated inflammatory analytes toward integrated host-response and functional immune platforms capable of supporting early triage, risk stratification, antimicrobial stewardship, and individualized immune monitoring.
items.citation: Plata-Menchaca EP, Hernández-Jiménez E. From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated <i>in vitro</i> diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps.. Frontiers in medical technology. 2026

items.title: Clinical Comparator Dependence of Inflammatory and Hematologic Biomarker Discrimination for Sepsis: A Matched Retrospective Study Using MIMIC-IV Emergency Department Data.
items.summary: This study examined how the diagnostic accuracy of inflammatory and hematologic biomarkers for sepsis changes depending on which comparison group is used to evaluate them. Using a large linked emergency department database, the researchers matched sepsis episodes against two distinct comparator groups: patients without suspected infection and patients with suspected infection who did not develop sepsis. They assessed the discriminatory performance of eleven routinely available biomarkers using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve across both diagnostic contrasts. C-reactive protein performed best when sepsis was compared against non-infected controls but showed a marked drop in discrimination when compared against infected non-sepsis patients, while absolute lymphocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio maintained more consistent, modest performance across both settings. The authors conclude that biomarker diagnostic performance is substantially shaped by the clinical comparator chosen, underscoring the need to evaluate and interpret sepsis biomarkers within the specific diagnostic context in which they will be applied.
items.citation: Sánchez-Vela S, Llaca-Díaz JM, Díaz-Chuc EA et al.. Clinical Comparator Dependence of Inflammatory and Hematologic Biomarker Discrimination for Sepsis: A Matched Retrospective Study Using MIMIC-IV Emergency Department Data.. Journal of clinical medicine. 2026

items.title: Early Identification of Sepsis-induced Acute Kidney Injury Utilizing NGAL, Cystatin C, Urine Output, and Serum Creatinine in a Porcine ( <i>Sus scrofa</i>) Model of Septic Shock: A comparative Study of Fluid and Vasopressor Strategies.
items.summary: This study investigated whether early renal biomarkers—specifically NGAL and cystatin C—could detect sepsis-associated acute kidney injury sooner than conventional markers like serum creatinine and urine output in a porcine model of septic shock. Using a randomized experimental design, pigs underwent standardized septic shock induction and were allocated to one of three resuscitation strategies involving Ringer's lactate, fluid combined with early norepinephrine, or early norepinephrine with maintenance fluids, with biomarkers measured repeatedly alongside hemodynamic monitoring. NGAL and cystatin C showed numerical fluctuations over time, with fluid-based resuscitation associated with post-intervention decreases in these markers while early norepinephrine administration was followed by numerical increases. However, none of the temporal or between-group changes for any biomarker reached statistical significance. The authors conclude that the findings are exploratory and insufficient to establish NGAL or cystatin C as early diagnostic indicators of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in this model.
items.citation: Primaputra Lubis A, Warli SM, Hamdi T et al.. Early Identification of Sepsis-induced Acute Kidney Injury Utilizing NGAL, Cystatin C, Urine Output, and Serum Creatinine in a Porcine ( <i>Sus scrofa</i>) Model of Septic Shock: A comparative Study of Fluid and Vasopressor Strategies.. F1000Research. 2026

items.title: Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026)
items.summary: The Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction is a consensus document that updates the clinical and pathophysiological framework for defining, classifying, and diagnosing myocardial infarction. The document introduces a new three-category clinical classification that distinguishes primary myocardial infarction arising from acute coronary pathology, secondary myocardial infarction resulting from myocardial supply-demand imbalance, and procedure-related myocardial infarction occurring as a complication of cardiac intervention or surgery. Updated diagnostic criteria incorporate cardiac troponin testing, electrocardiographic findings, and coronary and cardiac imaging, with refined thresholds for acute and chronic myocardial injury and accelerated diagnostic pathways. The classification system is aligned with International Classification of Diseases coding to improve consistency across clinical practice, public health reporting, and research. Guidance is also provided for special populations and low-resource settings where biomarker testing and advanced imaging may not be available.
authors: ESC/ACC/AHA/WHF Universal Definition Document Advisory Group
items.venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
items.citation: Nicholas L. Mills, Laura Kristin Newby, Sarah J. Zaman et al.. Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026). Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2026

items.title: Quantum–Photonic Topological Intelligence for Multiscale Biomedicine: Brain Networks, Biosignals, Spatial Multi-Omics and Autonomous Therapeutics
items.summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework called Quantum–Photonic Topological Intelligence for Multiscale Biomedicine, designed to integrate heterogeneous biomedical data spanning dynamic brain networks, physiological signals, spatially resolved molecular measurements, and treatment-response trajectories without collapsing their structure into a single undifferentiated feature space. The authors developed a unified mathematical and conceptual architecture combining graph and simplicial representations, persistent topological descriptors, multimodal learning, hybrid quantum–photonic feature maps, and constrained therapeutic optimization. The framework is organized into four coupled layers covering topology-preserving encoding, quantum–photonic representation, uncertainty-aware cross-modal fusion, and benefit–risk–cost constrained therapeutic decision support. Importantly, the study is entirely model-based and uses an illustrative numerical scoring scheme rather than real patient data, explicitly making no claim of empirical clinical superiority. The authors argue that the framework's value lies in disciplined multiscale coupling across its components and call for future empirical work benchmarking each element under matched datasets, prospective validation, and clinically meaningful endpoints before any deployment advantage is claimed.
items.venue: International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI)
items.citation: Murali Krishna Pasupuleti. Quantum–Photonic Topological Intelligence for Multiscale Biomedicine: Brain Networks, Biosignals, Spatial Multi-Omics and Autonomous Therapeutics. International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI). 2026

items.title: Detection of Chagas disease from the ECG: the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025
items.summary: This paper describes the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025, a competition focused on detecting Chagas disease — a parasitic infection causing cardiomyopathy — using electrocardiogram recordings as a screening tool. The challenge was motivated by the limited serological testing capacity in Latin America and the fact that Chagas cardiomyopathy produces recognizable ECG signatures, making algorithmic triage a clinically feasible approach. Participating teams developed machine learning algorithms trained on a large multi-database Brazilian ECG collection combining weakly labeled patient-report data and smaller strongly labeled serologically confirmed datasets, evaluated using a novel metric reflecting the proportion of patients who could realistically be tested given local capacity constraints. The organizers also developed an ensemble model combining top-performing submissions, which showed more consistent performance across held-out datasets than any single model alone, though absolute sensitivity values varied considerably depending on the dataset. The challenge attracted substantial global participation and demonstrated that ECG-based Chagas screening algorithms can achieve clinically meaningful sensitivity, supporting their potential role in prioritizing patients for confirmatory testing.
items.citation: Matthew A. Reyna, Soheil Saghafi, Zuzana Koscova et al.. Detection of Chagas disease from the ECG: the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025. Physiological Measurement. 2026

items.title: 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, in collaboration with the European Renal Association (ERA)
items.summary: These guidelines address the diagnosis, risk stratification, and management of cardiovascular disease in patients with chronic kidney disease, developed jointly by the European Society of Cardiology and the European Renal Association. The document comprehensively covers the full spectrum of cardiovascular manifestations in this population, including heart failure, coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, valvular disease, cerebrovascular disease, and venous thromboembolism, as well as special populations such as patients on dialysis and kidney transplant recipients. Pharmacological recommendations are structured around key drug classes including sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors, renin-angiotensin system blockers, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, reflecting their demonstrated benefits in reducing both cardiovascular and kidney failure risk. The guidelines also address lifestyle interventions, blood pressure and glycaemic targets, dyslipidaemia management, antithrombotic therapy, and person-centred care including multidisciplinary collaboration and palliative approaches. Evidence gaps are identified throughout, and practical guidance is provided to support clinical decision-making across the intersection of these two disease domains.
items.citation: Kevin Damman, Jozine M. ter Maaten, Kaitlin J. Mayne et al.. 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, in collaboration with the European Renal Association (ERA). European Heart Journal. 2026

items.title: Integration of Federated Learning and Blockchain in Health Care: Tutorial on Medical Data, Architectures, Privacy, Security, and Regulatory Compliance
items.summary: This tutorial paper examines the integration of federated learning and blockchain technology within healthcare settings, focusing on how their combination can enable secure, privacy-preserving, and collaborative medical AI. The authors developed a comprehensive framework called blockchain-based federated learning, which addresses key vulnerabilities of federated learning alone—such as model poisoning and gradient leakage—by leveraging blockchain's immutable ledger and decentralized consensus mechanisms to enhance trust and auditability. The tutorial contributes a taxonomy of medical data types and their federated learning requirements, three distinct integration architectures analyzed for security and scalability, and a security analysis pairing healthcare-specific threats with advanced cryptographic mitigations including zero-knowledge proofs, homomorphic encryption, and differential privacy. A regulatory compliance framework is also presented to align the system with major standards governing health data and AI-enabled medical devices. The authors argue that this framework is applicable across diverse healthcare domains—including disease prediction, medical imaging, and drug discovery—and identify emerging research priorities such as quantum-resilient cryptography and automated compliance.
items.citation: Yahya Shahsavari, Yaser Baseri, Abdelhakim Senhaji Hafid et al.. Integration of Federated Learning and Blockchain in Health Care: Tutorial on Medical Data, Architectures, Privacy, Security, and Regulatory Compliance. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2026

items.title: Objective Bayes Factor Based Model Selection for Zero-Inflated Microbiome Count Data Under Jeffreys Prior
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of selecting appropriate statistical models for microbiome count data, which is characterized by excess zeros and overdispersion arising from complex biological influences such as diet, disease, and environmental factors. The authors developed a Bayes factor approach for model selection among negative binomial, Poisson, zero-inflated negative binomial, and zero-inflated Poisson distributions, using non-informative Jeffreys priors to maintain objectivity. This framework was evaluated through simulation studies and real data analysis derived from microbiome sequencing experiments. The proposed Bayes factor method was found to outperform traditional model selection criteria, specifically the Akaike information criterion and Vuong's test, in both settings. To make the methodology accessible, the authors also introduced a dedicated R package for implementing the Bayesian model selection procedure.
items.citation: Paramahansa Pramanik, Arnab K. Maity. Objective Bayes Factor Based Model Selection for Zero-Inflated Microbiome Count Data Under Jeffreys Prior. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research. 2026

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether neutrino disappearance channels can exhibit sensitivity to T-violation, challenging the widely held assertion in the literature that T-violation is identically zero in such channels. The authors demonstrate that this conventional claim holds only under restricted conditions — specifically for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase causes the Jarlskog invariant to vanish — and that muon and tau neutrino survival probabilities can carry a genuine sine-of-delta-dependent T asymmetry in asymmetric matter. They identify that the common misconception arises from applying an improper T test that amounts to subtracting a probability from itself, and they carefully distinguish proper from improper T, CP, and CPT tests for arbitrary matter profiles. Using a two-layer constant-density toy model, they find that T-violation is maximized when one layer is near the solar resonance and the other near the atmospheric resonance. The paper further evaluates whether the matter asymmetry encountered by existing and planned long-baseline experiments is sufficient to make this sine-of-delta dependence observable in muon neutrino survival probability, and discusses future experimental scenarios that could probe T and CP violation through this channel.
items.citation: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas. Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of classifying Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in children and adolescents using EEG signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing EEG recordings from multiple participants across five task conditions, linking raw signals to precomputed features drawn from seven distinct feature families and documenting all quality control decisions to enable consistent cross-study comparisons. Technical validation confirmed high signal retention after preprocessing, and the dataset along with curation software were made publicly available. As an illustrative example of dataset reuse, the authors compared a gradient-boosted classifier using all feature families against a baseline prevalence predictor, finding that discrimination between recruitment groups varied across task conditions. The authors explicitly caution that these descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity for any of the features or methods examined.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
items.summary: This paper investigates a novel side-channel vulnerability in Android smartphones whereby camera subsystem metadata can be exploited for acoustic eavesdropping without requiring any audio permissions. The researchers discovered that Android's Camera2 API exposes high-rate gyroscope measurements through vendor CaptureResult metadata as part of optical image stabilization pipelines, bypassing the permission restrictions and privacy toggle protections introduced in Android 12 to prevent motion sensors from functioning as covert microphones. Testing across a large set of smartphones from multiple vendors, they found that a substantial portion expose gyroscope data via this pathway at rates exceeding standard SensorManager limits, with some flagship devices streaming data at rates high enough to capture speech-induced chassis vibrations even when both the microphone and camera toggles are disabled. To exploit this channel without requiring device-specific calibration data, the authors developed Source-to-Leakage Learning, a physics-constrained simulation framework that trains a universal speech recognizer on synthetic sensor traces rather than real recordings from target devices. The resulting system, CamEar, substantially outperforms prior approaches on unseen phones and achieves meaningful word and character recognition accuracy across tested high-rate devices, demonstrating that hardware-agnostic acoustic eavesdropping through camera metadata is a practical threat.
items.citation: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang. Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational burden of hyperparameter optimization on large datasets by proposing a ranking-preserving coreset selection framework. The approach constructs a compact data subset that maintains the relative ordering of hyperparameter configurations as observed on the full training data, formulating this as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based rankings while penalizing subset size. The resulting coreset is then used to accelerate three evolutionary hyperparameter optimization algorithms across a diverse collection of tabular, text, and image benchmark datasets. Experiments demonstrate substantial speedups in the hyperparameter optimization stage while preserving test accuracy comparable to full-dataset optimization, and the coreset's ranking fidelity generalizes to configurations not seen during its construction, outperforming random subsets of equivalent size on most datasets. The one-time cost of constructing the coreset can be amortized when it is reused across multiple hyperparameter optimization runs.
items.citation: Mamoona Tasadduq, Maryam Bashir. Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
items.summary: This paper investigated whether the properties of buoyancy glitches in low-luminosity red giants — specifically their amplitude, location, and width — can be recovered from global stellar properties rather than through computationally expensive dedicated seismic modelling. The authors trained gradient-boosted tree machine learning models on a large grid of synthetic stellar models, using global parameters such as the frequency of maximum oscillation power and effective temperature as inputs. They found that the glitch location and width are recoverable with very high accuracy, while the glitch amplitude shows only moderate recoverability, particularly in a specific range of large frequency separations where the glitch sits in a structurally complex transition zone between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity. Interpretability analysis revealed that the machine learning models rely primarily on evolutionary state indicators, suggesting that glitch location and width are tightly governed by global evolutionary trends, whereas glitch amplitude reflects more localized interior complexity. The authors conclude that global stellar properties can serve as direct estimates of buoyancy-glitch parameters, offering a practical way to prioritize stars for dedicated mixed-mode inversions in large asteroseismic surveys.
items.citation: Jiang Chen. Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
items.summary: This study investigated how the amplitude and phase of sinusoidal blade pitching affect both power extraction and the energy exchanged through the pitching motion itself in a vertical-axis turbine. Experiments were conducted using a single-blade model traversing a circular path in a water channel across a range of tip-speed ratios, testing hundreds of prescribed pitch conditions and combining force measurements with particle image velocimetry to understand the underlying flow physics. The optimal pitching amplitude decreased and the corresponding phase shifted as tip-speed ratio increased, with substantial improvements in cycle-averaged power coefficient observed across all operating conditions. At lower tip-speed ratios, performance gains were linked to delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and shedding along with prolonged favorable blade loading, while at higher tip-speed ratios the improvements were more localized with minimal change to the main power-producing event. By mapping both power output and net hydrodynamic pitching work together, the study identified pitch motions that enhance performance while maintaining an energetic surplus even under assumed dissipation, offering promising candidates for passive or assisted pitching implementations.
items.citation: Zihan Zhang, Anchi Li, Qimin Feng et al.. Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.
items.summary: This study compared metagenomic next-generation sequencing, a commercial syndromic multiplex PCR panel, and conventional phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing for diagnosing bloodstream infections in a setting with high antimicrobial resistance burden. Using a retrospective design, the researchers evaluated these methods across a large series of positive blood culture episodes from patients at a tertiary-care center. Metagenomic sequencing recovered the full set of routine-culture organisms more completely than the multiplex panel and identified off-panel carbapenem resistance genes, particularly an oxacillinase found in *Acinetobacter baumannii*, that accounted for false-susceptible results on the molecular panel. However, broader genomic coverage did not consistently translate into superior prediction of phenotypic resistance across antimicrobial classes, and conventional susceptibility testing remained necessary for definitive clinical guidance. The authors conclude that syndromic panel testing and metagenomic sequencing have complementary strengths, and that neither approach currently replaces phenotypic methods for guiding treatment decisions.
items.citation: Nitayanon P, Phoonthong S, Peizner MT et al.. Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: High prevalence of CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance and diagnostic accuracy of NG-Test CTX-M Multi among ESBL-producing <i>Escherichia coli</i> in Vietnam.
items.summary: This study investigated the prevalence of CTX-M extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing *Escherichia coli* among inpatients at a tertiary-care hospital in Vietnam and evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the NG-Test CTX-M Multi lateral flow immunoassay. A prospective cross-sectional design was used, with ESBL-producing isolates identified by an automated expert system and confirmed by multiplex real-time PCR as the reference standard. CTX-M enzymes were found in a large proportion of ESBL-producing isolates and were strongly associated with broader multidrug resistance, including significantly higher resistance rates to cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones, while carbapenems and amikacin retained activity in both CTX-M-positive and CTX-M-negative groups. The NG-Test CTX-M Multi assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity compared to PCR, supporting its potential utility as a rapid screening tool in clinical microbiology. The authors conclude that CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance represents a substantial burden in this setting and that point-of-care immunoassay testing could support timely antimicrobial stewardship decisions, though larger validation studies are recommended.
items.citation: Le TL, Nguyen S-T, Le VC et al.. High prevalence of CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance and diagnostic accuracy of NG-Test CTX-M Multi among ESBL-producing <i>Escherichia coli</i> in Vietnam.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Pathogen identification and resistance gene expression tests using ASTar remnant bacterial suspension in gram-negative contrived positive blood cultures.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether remnant bacterial suspensions generated during routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing on the ASTar System could be repurposed for simultaneous pathogen identification and resistance gene detection, thereby streamlining diagnostic workflows for bloodstream infections. Using gram-negative bacterial strains contrived into blood culture bottles, the researchers applied matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry for identification and lateral flow assays targeting clinically important resistance mechanisms, including extended-spectrum beta-lactamases and carbapenemases. All samples produced high-confidence identification scores, and lateral flow assay results showed complete or near-complete agreement with reference isolate characterization for the resistance targets examined. The integrated approach enabled pathogen identification and resistance detection within approximately one to two hours of instrument start, with phenotypic susceptibility results available within roughly six hours total, and was also compatible with reflex testing workflows triggered by phenotypic results. The authors conclude that this consolidated use of a single bacterial suspension for multiple diagnostic outputs could reduce redundant testing, lower costs compared to commercial multiplex polymerase chain reaction, and support earlier antimicrobial decision-making within stewardship frameworks.
