items.citation: Gupta V, Myers M, Niklasson I et al.. Pathogen identification and resistance gene expression tests using ASTar remnant bacterial suspension in gram-negative contrived positive blood cultures.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: From empirical to targeted therapy: A comprehensive review of clinical microbiological diagnostics for urinary tract infections.
items.summary: This review examined the clinical microbiological diagnostic landscape for urinary tract infections, a globally prevalent condition made more challenging by high recurrence rates and rising antimicrobial resistance. The authors systematically surveyed the full diagnostic workflow, from specimen collection and traditional culture-based methods through modern identification technologies such as mass spectrometry and multilocus sequence typing, as well as a range of antimicrobial susceptibility testing approaches from broth microdilution to automated systems. They also reviewed advances in genotypic resistance detection using multiplex polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing. The review concludes that combining conventional phenotypic testing with rapid molecular diagnostics creates a practical foundation for shifting clinical practice from empirical to targeted antimicrobial therapy. The authors argue that systematic implementation of these integrated diagnostic pipelines supports antimicrobial stewardship, reduces unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic use, and lays the groundwork for precision medicine approaches in managing urinary tract infections.
items.citation: Kim JA, Kim JH. From empirical to targeted therapy: A comprehensive review of clinical microbiological diagnostics for urinary tract infections.. Investigative and clinical urology. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside
items.citation: Mugisha N, Fawaz L, Noureddine R et al.. Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside. Health science reports. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study examined whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antibiotic prescribing and patient outcomes compared to conventional susceptibility testing alone. Conducted at a hospital in Pakistan, the study enrolled adult patients with suspected bacterial infections and measured outcomes including time to effective therapy, antibiotic appropriateness, length of hospital stay, and mortality. The integrated approach dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and to initiation of effective therapy compared to conventional testing, while substantially increasing appropriate antibiotic use and reducing broad-spectrum antibiotic prescribing. Patients managed under the integrated strategy also experienced shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, and the AI model showed strong discriminatory ability for predicting antimicrobial resistance. The authors conclude that this combined diagnostic and predictive framework represents a scalable, cost-effective strategy for combating antimicrobial resistance, particularly in resource-limited healthcare settings.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Distributional Policy Evaluation for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects, Social Equity and Climate-Transition Governance
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental limitation of standard policy evaluation methods when applied to climate-transition policies, namely that average treatment effects can obscure concentrated burdens falling on vulnerable populations such as low-income households, carbon-dependent workers, and exposed regions. The authors develop a comprehensive distributional evaluation architecture called the D-PECT Framework, which integrates heterogeneous and quantile treatment effects, counterfactual outcome distributions, doubly robust estimation, and equity-sensitive social welfare optimization alongside climate-effectiveness and governance criteria. The framework is formalized through potential-outcome equations, a multivariate matrix model, dynamic transition-state equations, and a risk-adjusted master objective that incorporates inequality penalties, tail-harm measures, fiscal constraints, and procedural-justice indicators. Using a pedagogical numerical demonstration, the authors show that an adaptive targeted policy package scores meaningfully higher on an integrated resilience metric than an untargeted benchmark, and that policy rankings can reverse when the objective shifts from average welfare maximization to lower-tail protection. The paper concludes that compensation mechanisms are more credible when tied to estimated exposure, treatment response, and procedural inclusion rather than income alone, offering an interdisciplinary framework for institutions seeking climate action that is causally rigorous, distributionally transparent, and governable.
items.venue: International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI)
items.citation: Murali Krishna Pasupuleti. Distributional Policy Evaluation for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects, Social Equity and Climate-Transition Governance. International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI). 2026

items.title: Leveraging machine learning models in evaluating ADMET properties for drug discovery and development
items.summary: This review examined how machine learning approaches are being applied to predict the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity properties of drug candidates, which represent a persistent bottleneck in pharmaceutical development. The authors systematically surveyed the landscape of machine learning applications in this domain, covering algorithm types, molecular descriptors, datasets, model validation strategies, and regulatory considerations, with particular focus on supervised and deep learning techniques. Machine learning models were found to outperform some traditional quantitative structure-activity relationship models across key endpoints including solubility, permeability, metabolism, and toxicity, while offering faster and more cost-effective predictions that integrate into existing drug discovery workflows. The review highlights that challenges remain around data quality, model interpretability, and regulatory acceptance of computationally derived predictions. The authors conclude that continued integration of machine learning with experimental pharmacology holds strong potential to improve early risk assessment, prioritize compounds more effectively, and reduce the high rate of late-stage drug candidate failures.
items.citation: Venkataraman Magesh, Gopi Chand Rao, M Jeevan Karthik et al.. Leveraging machine learning models in evaluating ADMET properties for drug discovery and development. ADMET & DMPK. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning in large language models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning. The researchers introduced a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from eight medical datasets, using difficulty-aware selection and contamination screening to ensure genuine complexity. They evaluated a range of internalized reasoning models, standard base models, and agent-based multi-model frameworks across this benchmark. The key finding is that both approaches independently improve performance and their benefits are additive, with the highest accuracy achieved by combining an internalized reasoning model with an agent workflow. Additionally, Pareto analysis revealed that this combined approach dominates the cost-performance frontier, while lightweight optimization of less expensive models provides a viable path for resource-constrained clinical settings.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches collectively illuminate disease mechanisms at a molecular level, while deep learning architectures extract meaningful patterns from these complex, high-dimensional datasets. The paper analyzes the combined application of these technologies across the drug development pipeline, encompassing target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas including oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate how this convergence accelerates therapeutic innovation. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic biases, while arguing that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence ultimately enables more precise therapeutic interventions and heralds a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
items.citation: Avina Vongpradith, Regina-Mae Villanueva Dominguez, Lorainne Tudor Car et al.. Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023. The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Generative AI-enabled clinical decision support system in primary care: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial
items.summary: This trial investigated whether large language model-based clinical decision support integrated into electronic medical records could improve patient outcomes in real-world primary care settings in Kenya. Using a pragmatic cluster-randomized design across sixteen facilities, clinical officers were randomly assigned to manage patients either with or without access to the artificial intelligence assistance tool. The primary outcome was a composite measure of treatment failure events occurring within two weeks of patient enrollment, adjudicated by independent experts. No statistically significant difference in treatment failure rates was found between patients managed with and without the artificial intelligence assistance, and the tool demonstrated an acceptable safety profile with no related serious adverse events identified. The investigators conclude that while the intervention appeared safe, it did not meaningfully reduce treatment failure, and any clinical benefit, if real, is likely to be modest.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Vaishnavi Menon et al.. Generative AI-enabled clinical decision support system in primary care: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of classifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using EEG signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing EEG recordings from participants across five task conditions, linking continuous signals to precomputed features spanning seven distinct feature families and documenting all quality control decisions to enable consistent cross-study comparisons. Technical validation confirmed high signal retention rates after preprocessing, and an illustrative machine learning analysis using gradient boosting across all feature families was compared against a baseline prevalence predictor. Results showed that the ability to discriminate between recruitment groups varied across task conditions, with one task yielding stronger separation than others, though the authors explicitly note these findings do not establish diagnostic validity. The curated dataset, curation software, and aggregate predictive results were made publicly available to support reproducible research on EEG-based ADHD classification.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: This paper investigated how propulsion load changes propagate through the interconnected nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical systems of a small modular reactor-powered all-electric ship. The researchers developed an integrated dynamic model coupling a pressurized water reactor, steam generator, turbine, synchronous generator, shipboard electrical network, propulsion motor, and battery energy storage system, then simulated a sudden reduction in propulsion load to compare system responses with and without battery support. Without the battery, the mismatch between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand produced a large frequency overshoot, while the battery configuration absorbed excess electrical power and dramatically reduced the frequency excursion. Beyond stabilizing grid frequency, the battery's intervention also smoothed upstream disturbances throughout the steam cycle and reactor, including steam flow, pressure, coolant temperature, reactivity, and thermal power. The study concludes that treating nuclear-powered electric ships as tightly coupled multi-domain systems is essential and that battery energy storage meaningfully improves short-term load-following performance.
items.citation: Ali Mahboub Rad, Jie Zhang. Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations in evaluating instance segmentation when reference annotations contain systematic biases such as merged touching objects or split fragmented ones, problems that arise both from heuristic approximations and from expert disagreement. The authors argue that existing metrics like Panoptic Quality treat all instances equally and cannot distinguish valid from invalid over- or under-segmentation when references themselves are biased. To address this, they introduce Star Panoptic Quality, a novel evaluation framework that constructs a star forest from the bipartite matching graph between predicted and reference instances, isolating distinct failure modes into clean, merge, and split categories. The framework then computes a final metric by allowing practitioners to apply individual weights to each failure mode, enabling targeted penalization or leniency depending on the known biases in the reference annotations. Through experiments, the authors demonstrate that their method both improves control over how segmentation errors are penalized and serves as a diagnostic tool for revealing the prevalence of different failure modes in a dataset.
items.citation: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.. Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Metadata-Private Voice Communication over Tor using Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation
items.summary: This paper investigated the dual challenge of metadata exposure and quantum computing threats in encrypted voice communication systems, noting that existing tools address only one concern at a time. The researchers developed SAPEC, a peer-to-peer voice communication system that routes all traffic through Tor hidden services to conceal both parties' network identities while incorporating post-quantum cryptographic primitives, specifically ML-KEM-1024 for key encapsulation and Dilithium for mutual identity verification, with audio encrypted under AES-256. The system also employs a removable physical key device to prevent identity key material from persisting on the host machine. Empirical testing demonstrated that interactive voice communication over onion routing is practically feasible, achieving median one-way audio delay and connection setup times that fall within acceptable ranges for real-time conversation.
items.citation: Noah Zeinali Yazdi, Samuel Zeinali Yazdi. Metadata-Private Voice Communication over Tor using Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary: This paper introduces the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, an industrial architecture designed to automate and scale user experience evaluation in large-scale web search systems. The framework addresses limitations of traditional survey-based methods and coarse automated metrics by combining two complementary components: a macro-level system that uses a fine-tuned encoder-decoder language model on telemetry features to detect user sentiment regressions across experiments, and a micro-level system that employs a multimodal large language model to assess visual renderings and spatial layouts of web result pages, quantifying the effort users must expend to find satisfactory results. The macro system incorporates multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering, while the micro system is enhanced through reinforcement learning-based prompt optimization and an AI judge for identifying win/loss patterns. Together, the two tiers achieve meaningful gains in precision-recall and F-score performance on held-out data and experiments. The deployed framework reduces measurement latency from weeks to hours, substantially cuts survey overhead, and enables diagnostic UX attribution at the scale of hundreds of thousands of live experiment queries processed daily.
items.citation: Yi Ding, Gaurav Kumar, Rui Min et al.. The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate how well vision-language models can interpret electronic navigational charts, which encode safety-critical maritime information through complex symbols, geometries, and standardized attributes. The researchers constructed a large question-answering dataset derived from thousands of official nautical charts, organizing questions around four capability areas: perceiving chart features, spatial reasoning, combined perception and spatial reasoning, and applying navigational knowledge to assess chart changes. A progressive subset of questions was designed to trace how models move from detecting changes in charts to judging their navigational significance, enabling fine-grained analysis of reasoning chains. Evaluation of ten open-weight vision-language models revealed significant weaknesses in fine-grained feature recognition and feature-grounded spatial reasoning, though providing explicit perceptual and spatial evidence was shown to improve models' ability to assess the criticality of chart changes. The benchmark is presented as a diagnostic resource for understanding model limitations in safety-critical nautical chart interpretation tasks.
items.citation: Jiyoon Pyo, Jacob Arndt, Yao-Yi Chiang et al.. ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Why Sensors Fail in Biological Samples: Fouling, Blocking, Matrix Effects and Prevention Solutions
items.summary: This review paper examines why sensors and biosensors fail when deployed in biological fluids such as blood, serum, plasma, and sweat, focusing on surface fouling, interface blocking, and matrix interference as interconnected phenomena rather than isolated problems. The authors provide a mechanistic account of how processes such as protein adsorption, nonspecific binding, ionic strength variations, pH fluctuations, viscosity changes, and electroactive interferents degrade sensor performance, leading to signal drift, reduced sensitivity, false-positive responses, and shortened operational lifetime. The review systematically compares how these failure modes manifest across diverse sensing platforms, including electrochemical, optical, capacitive, potentiometric, field-effect transistor, and wearable biosensor architectures. Prevention strategies already implemented in real biomarker sensing platforms are surveyed, encompassing antifouling coatings, zwitterionic and hydrogel interfaces, blocking agents, membrane engineering, microfluidic sample pre-treatment, and artificial intelligence-assisted drift correction. The paper concludes by synthesizing advances across materials engineering, surface chemistry, and algorithmic correction to offer a practical guide for designing stable, low-fouling, and self-correcting biosensors suitable for point-of-care biomarker analysis.
items.citation: Nikola Lenar, Beata Paczosa‐Bator. Why Sensors Fail in Biological Samples: Fouling, Blocking, Matrix Effects and Prevention Solutions. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Transforming Diagnostic Precision in Periodontology Through Lab-on-a-Chip Technology: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: This scoping review examined the state of evidence for lab-on-a-chip and microfluidic technologies as point-of-care diagnostic tools for periodontal and peri-implant disease, addressing the limitation that conventional periodontal diagnostics measures past damage rather than active disease. Following established scoping review methodology, the authors searched multiple electronic databases over a defined timeframe, screening studies for relevance to biosensor, microfluidic, or lab-on-a-chip platforms targeting periodontal tissues, and extracting data on technology type, biomarker targets, diagnostic performance, and developmental readiness. A small subset of identified records met inclusion criteria, revealing that saliva was the predominant sample matrix and that platforms spanning paper-based microfluidics, electrochemical and optical biosensors, and continuous-flow PCR chips most commonly targeted key periodontal pathogens and host inflammatory markers. Despite demonstrating analytical promise, the reviewed devices were predominantly at the prototype stage, with clinical diagnostic accuracy rarely reported and validation conducted largely under controlled laboratory rather than real-world clinical conditions. The authors conclude that advancing these technologies to routine clinical use will require multicentric clinical validation, standardized fabrication protocols, and clearer regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Manoj M, Jaison J, Varghese J. Transforming Diagnostic Precision in Periodontology Through Lab-on-a-Chip Technology: A Scoping Review.. International journal of dentistry. 2026

items.title: Microfluidic Biosensors for the Detection of Foodborne Pathogens: A Comprehensive Review.
items.summary: This review examines the current state of microfluidic biosensors designed to detect foodborne pathogens in complex food matrices, where interferents such as lipids, proteins, and background microorganisms complicate both sample preparation and signal readout. The authors systematically compared published devices across substrate types, fabrication approaches, sample handling strategies, and detection modalities including optical, electrochemical, and nucleic-acid-based readouts. While the reviewed literature demonstrates rapid pathogen detection in selected food samples, the authors highlight that reported performance metrics are rarely comparable across studies due to inconsistent reporting of matrices, units, enrichment steps, and assay times. Key translational barriers identified include reproducible manufacturing, reagent stability, integrated sample-to-answer workflows, and validation in authentic food samples rather than controlled laboratory conditions. Emerging approaches such as CRISPR-assisted assays, orthogonal readouts, and AI-supported interpretation are noted as promising but require direct head-to-head comparison and independent validation before claims of commercial readiness can be substantiated.
items.citation: Mao W, Zhang L. Microfluidic Biosensors for the Detection of Foodborne Pathogens: A Comprehensive Review.. Food science & nutrition. 2026

items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review paper examines the translational pathway of wearable and implantable microfluidic systems from laboratory prototypes toward clinical deployment in personalized medicine. The authors synthesize the field along a coherent trajectory spanning functional biomaterials, fabrication techniques, diagnostic performance benchmarking, and closed-loop theranostic platforms capable of both monitoring and therapeutic response. A particular focus is placed on how artificial intelligence is integrated across sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular signal decoding, and autonomous on-device decision-making. The review critically identifies socio-technical barriers to clinical translation, arguing that biofluid data heterogeneity and population-level baseline disparities introduce algorithmic bias that undermines equitable deployment. The authors conclude that standardized validation benchmarks, robust hardware interfaces, and alignment with regulatory frameworks are essential prerequisites for responsible and equitable digital health applications.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
items.summary: This study investigated how pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells obtain essential lipids within a dense fibroblastic stroma that lacks functional blood vessels. The researchers discovered that cancer-associated fibroblasts acquire lipids from blood-borne particles and transfer them to pancreatic cancer cells through trogocytosis, a process involving the partial transfer of plasma membrane between cells. This transfer depends on synapse-like contacts between cancer cells and fibroblasts that trigger calcium influx in fibroblasts via Orai channels, activating the phospholipid scramblase ANO6, which drives phosphatidylserine exposure on fibroblast membranes and initiates trogocytosis and lipid transfer, including cholesterol. Beyond fueling cancer cell survival, ANO6-dependent phosphatidylserine externalization also enables fibroblasts to suppress cytotoxic T cell activity through the same trogocytic mechanism. Blocking ANO6 impaired tumor growth by disrupting cholesterol delivery to cancer cells and reduced immune suppression, identifying ANO6 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
items.citation: Charline Ogier, Charles Solomon Akino Mercy, Elena Bondarenko et al.. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression. Nature Cancer. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: This review examines the development of ferrite-based nanomaterials as multifunctional platforms for biomedical applications, tracing their evolution from basic magnetic contrast agents to sophisticated systems capable of actively modulating biological microenvironments. The authors analyze how atomic-level engineering strategies, including cation distribution, defect modulation, and morphological anisotropy in spinel and hexagonal ferrites, can be used to tune magnetic, catalytic, and thermal properties relevant to applications such as magnetic resonance imaging, drug delivery, hyperthermia, and antimicrobial therapy. The review also highlights emerging areas including viscosity-independent magnetic hyperthermia, reactive oxygen species-mediated therapies, and magnetic tissue engineering. A central concern is the translational gap between laboratory performance and clinical application, with critical attention given to obstacles such as discrepancies between colloidal and intracellular heating efficiency, protein corona formation, and the challenges of scalable, regulatory-compliant synthesis. The authors conclude by proposing a roadmap that integrates artificial intelligence-driven material discovery and green chemistry approaches to advance next-generation magnetotheranostic systems for precision medicine.
items.citation: Pramod D. Mhase, Varsha C. Pujari, Akash V. Fulari et al.. Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, focusing on how existing pharmaceutical frameworks apply to these acellular biological entities. The authors analyzed divergent regulatory approaches across major jurisdictions, noting that the European Union has recently clarified that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside advanced therapy medicinal product definitions and require case-by-case classification, while the United States treats such products as drugs and biologics subject to premarket review, and other regions apply their own jurisdiction-specific criteria. This fragmentation creates significant challenges for product classification, quality assessment, comparability studies, and multinational clinical development. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle products can and should be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks, provided that regulatory tools are applied consistently and that unresolved grey zones—including classification criteria, critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability standards—are systematically addressed. The review is intended to support regulatory dialogue among international agencies and scientific societies rather than to prescribe new normative frameworks, with the ultimate goal of enabling safe and internationally credible clinical translation of extracellular vesicle-based therapies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)/polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): current and future trends
items.summary: This review examines polycystic ovary syndrome, the most common endocrinologic disorder in women, addressing gaps in understanding that have complicated both diagnosis and treatment. The authors discuss the proposed pathophysiology of the condition from a translational perspective, surveying existing diagnostic criteria and current management strategies. The review also considers the long-term health consequences associated with the disorder and identifies future research directions. The authors highlight that incomplete knowledge of disease mechanisms has hindered effective care for a large number of affected individuals, and they advocate for greater research attention toward this often-overlooked condition.
items.citation: Jessica L. Chan, Irene Masini, Margareta Danuta Pisarska. Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)/polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): current and future trends. Journal of Clinical Investigation. 2026

items.title: AI for science: Progress, challenges, and perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examines the progress, challenges, and future directions of artificial intelligence applied to scientific discovery, covering a broad sweep of disciplines from physics and chemistry to life sciences and social science. The authors propose a unified closed-loop research paradigm organizing AI-driven science into six core modules spanning literature research, data analysis, hypothesis formulation, experimental execution, report generation, and autonomous evolution. They survey breakthroughs enabled by foundation models and reasoning-oriented AI across numerous frontier fields, emphasizing capabilities such as overcoming dimensionality constraints and enabling complex inverse design problems. The review also identifies persistent obstacles including scarcity of standardized high-quality data, insufficient model interpretability, and physical inconsistencies in generative outputs. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for cross-disciplinary scientific foundation models and envision a future paradigm of human-AI collaborative autonomous research.
items.citation: Yongjun Xu, Zezhi Shao, Xin Liu et al.. AI for science: Progress, challenges, and perspectives. The Innovation. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of classifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using electroencephalography signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing recordings from participants across five task conditions, standardizing the signal preparation, analysis windows, and quality decisions to enable fair comparison of multiple EEG feature families on identical time intervals. The resulting dataset links continuous brain signals to precomputed measurements spanning over a hundred feature definitions, alongside documentation of preprocessing choices and quality outcomes. Technical validation confirmed strong signal retention after preprocessing, and an illustrative machine learning experiment using gradient boosting across all feature families demonstrated that discrimination between recruitment groups varied by task condition. The authors emphasize that these descriptive findings do not establish diagnostic validity, but the publicly released dataset and software are intended to support reproducible and comparable EEG research in this population.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
items.summary: This paper investigates a novel side-channel attack that exploits Android's Camera2 subsystem to perform acoustic eavesdropping without requiring microphone permissions. The researchers discovered that Camera2's hardware abstraction layer captures high-rate gyroscope measurements through image stabilization pipelines and exports them via vendor metadata, bypassing Android's privacy protections that normally cap motion sensor rates and throttle them when the microphone toggle is disabled. Testing across a large set of smartphones from multiple vendors, they found that a substantial portion expose gyroscope data through this channel at sampling rates exceeding the standard ceiling, with some flagship devices streaming data at rates high enough to capture speech-induced vibrations even when both microphone and camera privacy toggles are engaged. To exploit this channel without requiring any device-specific calibration data, they developed Source-to-Leakage Learning, a framework that uses a physics-constrained simulator to decouple speech content from device-specific mechanical resonances, enabling a universal speech recognizer trained entirely on simulated data. Their resulting system, CamEar, substantially outperforms prior approaches on unseen devices, demonstrating that Android's current privacy architecture has a meaningful unaddressed vulnerability in the Camera2 metadata pathway.
items.citation: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang. Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
items.summary: This paper challenges the conventional practice in machine learning of treating model architecture as fixed prior to training, arguing instead that topology should emerge from the training process itself. The authors introduce Model Carving, a method that jointly learns both the weights and architecture of a Transformer by applying learnable scalar gates to each sublayer, allowing the training loss to eliminate unnecessary components and produce a heterogeneous, smaller network. They evaluate this approach by pre-training standard and looped Transformers across a range of parameter scales, comparing carved models against dense baselines, pruned models, and distilled models at equivalent compute budgets. Carved models achieve lower validation loss than dense models trained with substantially more compute, and outperform size-matched models obtained through post-hoc compression, with this advantage growing with scale and extending to few-shot and generation tasks. The resulting models also require meaningfully fewer floating-point operations per token and decode faster, supporting the authors' central claim that architecture, like weights, should be learned rather than fixed in advance.
items.citation: Kaden Zheng, Pratyusha Sharma. Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: This paper investigated the integration of neuromorphic sensing and computing into a complete robotic system capable of real-time multimodal perception. The researchers built a four-wheeled rover platform combining three perception pipelines: a conventional deep learning audio classifier running on a GPU, a spiking neural network deployed on dedicated neuromorphic audio hardware, and an event-camera-based spiking object detector for traffic cone recognition. All components were containerized and coordinated through a robotics middleware framework, with a dispatcher module translating detected perceptual events into robot behaviors. The platform was demonstrated in a proof-of-concept scenario requiring the robot to respond to sound classes and detect visual targets, showing that neuromorphic hardware can be successfully integrated alongside conventional computing in a functioning multimodal robotic system. The work advances the field by moving neuromorphic evaluation beyond isolated benchmarks toward deployment in a complete, closed-loop robotic platform operating under real-time constraints.
items.citation: Guillem Fustier-Castillo, Ruben Ribes-Serrano, Javier Naranjo-Alcazar et al.. Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of automatically selecting the best quantum processing unit (QPU) for a given circuit workload in multi-vendor cluster environments, rather than relying on users to manually specify a device based on average fidelity. The core challenge is that transpiling a circuit to match each candidate device's qubit connectivity introduces additional gates, meaning a device with nominally good error rates may still fail to meet a circuit's required success probability after compilation. To solve this, the authors developed a two-stage scheduling approach in which a training-free estimator rapidly predicts post-transpilation success probability across all candidate devices in milliseconds without actually compiling the circuit, filtering out unsuitable options before only the selected device performs full transpilation. The estimator closely matched the latency and ranking accuracy of compiling for every candidate, substantially reduced requirement violations compared to naïve device selection, and distributed load effectively under contention. The approach generalizes across vendors when published error rates are accurate, but breaks down when vendor-reported figures do not faithfully reflect actual device performance.
items.citation: Ana Paula Appel. Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations in evaluating instance segmentation when reference annotations contain systematic biases, such as merged touching objects or split fragmented ones arising from heuristic approximations or expert disagreement. The authors identify that existing metrics like Panoptic Quality treat all instances equally and cannot distinguish valid from invalid over- or under-segmentation when the reference itself is flawed. They propose Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), a novel evaluation framework that constructs a star forest from the bipartite matching graph between predicted and reference instances, isolating distinct failure modes into clean, merge, and split categories. The framework then computes a final metric by allowing practitioners to weight each failure mode independently, enabling targeted penalization or leniency depending on known annotation biases. Through multiple experiments, the authors demonstrate that StarPQ both accommodates delineation biases in references and serves as a diagnostic tool to reveal the prevalence of specific segmentation failure modes.
items.citation: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.. Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk
items.summary: This study developed a rapid molecular detection platform for *Streptococcus agalactiae*, a primary causative agent of bovine mastitis, by combining recombinase polymerase amplification with a prokaryotic Argonaute protein system targeting the conserved *cfb* gene. The researchers designed and screened multiple primer pairs and guide DNAs to optimize two detection formats offering dual readout: a real-time fluorescence assay and a lateral flow dipstick assay. The optimized platform achieved sensitive and specific detection, with the fluorescence format reaching a lower detection limit than the lateral flow format, and neither showed cross-reactivity with non-target bacteria. Field validation using bovine milk samples from multiple dairy farming regions in China demonstrated complete concordance between both RPA-PfAgo formats and a standardized quantitative PCR assay, while all molecular methods outperformed conventional bacteriological culture in identifying positive samples. The authors conclude that this dual-readout platform provides a rapid, reliable, and field-deployable diagnostic tool for detecting *S. agalactiae* in dairy cattle milk.
items.citation: Xujie Zhao, Yuying Du, Qianlei Zhu et al.. Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk. Veterinary Sciences. 2026

items.title: Detection of Salmonella Typhimurium using a nanoflower-mediated horseradish peroxidase-linked antibody signal system combined with microfluidic sensors.
items.summary: This paper developed a colorimetric biosensor for detecting the foodborne pathogen Salmonella typhimurium by combining aptamer-based target recognition with enzyme-mediated signal amplification. The researchers synthesized three-dimensional nanoflower-shaped organic-inorganic nanocomposites using a one-step method, incorporating horseradish peroxidase-labeled antibodies and Salmonella-specific aptamers into a sandwich-type sensing architecture. In the presence of hydrogen peroxide, the enzyme converts a colorless substrate into a colored product, enabling visual signal readout, and the system was integrated with a microfluidic device to simplify operation. The biosensor achieved a broad linear detection range and an extremely low detection limit, while also demonstrating good selectivity, reproducibility, and stability. The authors conclude that this platform shows strong potential for rapid, on-site pathogen screening and broader applications in food safety and public health diagnostics.
items.citation: Yu Y, Zhou H, Bu S et al.. Detection of Salmonella Typhimurium using a nanoflower-mediated horseradish peroxidase-linked antibody signal system combined with microfluidic sensors.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Early on-site diagnosis of citrus Huanglongbing via a microfluidic electrochemical biosensor for dual-modal detection of bacterial OmpA and host-derived H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>.
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge of rapidly diagnosing citrus Huanglongbing in field settings, a devastating disease caused by an unculturable bacterium for which conventional laboratory-based methods are poorly suited. The researchers selected high-affinity aptamers targeting the bacterial outer membrane protein OmpA and integrated them into a dual-modal microfluidic electrochemical biosensor platform that simultaneously detects this pathogen biomarker alongside host-produced hydrogen peroxide as a marker of immune response. The platform combined an aptamer-functionalized MXene and silver nanoparticle biosensor with a Prussian blue-based electrochemical sensor, enabling complementary signal verification to improve diagnostic reliability. The biosensor achieved a very low detection limit for OmpA and demonstrated strong agreement with quantitative PCR results when validated against field samples, completing the full assay in a fraction of the time required by conventional methods. The authors conclude that this portable platform enables rapid preliminary on-site screening to guide timely intervention and support management of infected citrus orchards.
items.citation: Xie C, Wang J, Chen Q et al.. Early on-site diagnosis of citrus Huanglongbing via a microfluidic electrochemical biosensor for dual-modal detection of bacterial OmpA and host-derived H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>. . Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.
items.summary: This study addressed the urgent need for rapid, low-infrastructure detection of *Acinetobacter baumannii* and its carbapenem resistance genes in clinical settings, where conventional methods are slow and the pathogen is a critical priority due to extensive drug resistance. The researchers developed oligonucleotide-functionalized gold nanoparticle biosensors targeting three distinct genetic markers: the *nucAb* gene for specific *A. baumannii* identification, the *bla*OXA-23 gene for the most prevalent carbapenem resistance mechanism in this species, and a conserved region of *bla*NDM to detect New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase variants across multiple Gram-negative pathogens. The biosensors were designed to work directly on clinical respiratory samples without requiring DNA purification or amplification, simplifying the workflow considerably. All three biosensors produced visible colorimetric results within thirty minutes and demonstrated sensitivity down to low nanogram quantities of DNA or low bacterial cell counts per milliliter. The authors conclude that these biosensors offer a practical, rapid, and economical tool for early clinical decision-making and antimicrobial resistance surveillance, capable of detecting resistance determinants beyond *A. baumannii* alone.
items.citation: Chalana A, Gupta V, Sharma P et al.. Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.
items.summary: The paper developed an electrochemical biosensing platform called SHIELD designed to detect viable foodborne pathogens with high sensitivity and specificity. The system combines Propidium Monoazide pretreatment to block DNA from dead bacteria, isothermal LAMP amplification of target DNA, and Argonaute-guided cleavage of dual-labeled electrochemical probes, with unreacted probes removed via magnetic separation to generate a signal-on readout. By operating in a homogeneous, immobilization-free format, the approach circumvents reproducibility issues associated with surface-fixed sensors. The platform was demonstrated for the detection of viable Salmonella typhimurium, achieving a very low detection limit within a relatively short assay time. The authors conclude that SHIELD offers a reliable and innovative paradigm for rapid, sensitive screening of viable foodborne pathogens by synergizing viability discrimination, nucleic acid amplification, and programmable enzymatic cleavage.
items.citation: Qiao J, Bai B, Zhang Y et al.. SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.
items.summary: This paper developed a photoelectrochemical biosensor for detecting a gene fragment specific to Legionella pneumophila, the bacterium responsible for Legionnaires' disease. The biosensor was constructed using a perylene-based compound as a photoactive material to generate a strong initial photocurrent, with gold nanoparticles electrodeposited on the electrode surface to anchor a DNA capture probe. Upon hybridization with the target mip gene sequence, a cobalt porphyrin compound intercalated into the resulting DNA duplex and quenched the photocurrent signal, enabling quantitative detection. The sensor achieved a wide linear detection range and a very low detection limit in the femtomolar range, demonstrating high sensitivity. The authors propose this platform as a promising tool for practical screening of Legionella pneumophila in respiratory specimens with high bacterial loads.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Zhang F, Lu L, Li S et al.. Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.. Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape
items.summary: The paper investigated the evolutionary dynamics of affinity maturation in germinal centers, where B cells undergo Darwinian selection to produce increasingly potent antibodies. The researchers developed an experimental evolution model in which they replayed over one hundred monoclonal germinal center reactions and used deep mutational scanning to assign affinity values to individual cells, mapping the underlying affinity landscape. Their analysis revealed that germinal centers achieve predictable evolutionary outcomes despite noisy selection, with the trajectory of affinity maturation heavily shaped by biases in somatic hypermutation that constrain which regions of sequence space are explored. By inferring a quantitative fitness landscape, they found it could accurately recapitulate the observed affinity maturation trajectory. Importantly, the study argues that previously noted features of germinal center selection, such as apparent tolerance for low-affinity lineages and rapid plateauing of antibody affinity, are likely artifacts of survivorship bias rather than genuine properties of the selection process.
items.citation: William S. DeWitt, Ashni A. Vora, Tatsuya Araki et al.. Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape. Cell. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: This review examines the development of ferrite-based nanomaterials as multifunctional biomedical platforms, tracing their evolution from basic magnetic contrast agents to sophisticated systems capable of modulating biological microenvironments. The authors analyze how atomic-level engineering approaches—including cation distribution, defect modulation, and morphological anisotropy—can be used to tune magnetic, catalytic, and thermal properties in both spinel and hexagonal ferrite structures. The review surveys both established applications such as MRI contrast enhancement and drug delivery, as well as emerging uses including nanozyme-based catalytic therapy, reactive oxygen species-mediated antimicrobial treatment, and magnetic tissue engineering. A central focus is the translational gap between laboratory performance and clinical implementation, with the authors critically examining obstacles such as discrepancies between colloidal and intracellular heating efficiency, protein corona formation, and the difficulties of scaling synthesis to good manufacturing practice standards. The authors conclude by proposing a roadmap that integrates artificial intelligence-driven material discovery and green chemistry principles to advance the next generation of ferrite-based theranostic systems for precision medicine.
items.citation: Pramod D. Mhase, Varsha C. Pujari, Akash V. Fulari et al.. Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses
items.summary: This paper investigated how hedgehog merbecoviruses — relatives of the Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus that circulate in hedgehogs across Europe and Asia — enter host cells, a question relevant to assessing zoonotic spillover risk. Using cell-based assays, pseudotype experiments with a vesicular stomatitis virus reporter system, and protein binding assays, the researchers tested candidate coronavirus receptors from European hedgehogs and identified aminopeptidase N as the functional entry receptor for these viruses. They found that viral spike proteins displayed enhanced infectivity when produced at temperatures matching hedgehog physiology rather than typical mammalian body temperature, suggesting adaptation to their natural host. A broad screen of aminopeptidase N orthologues from many mammalian species revealed restricted cross-species receptor usage, notably including an inability to use the human version of the protein. Electron cryomicroscopy further showed that the spike-receptor interface is structurally distinct from other known coronavirus–aminopeptidase N interactions, helping to explain the species barriers and informing risk assessments for potential viral emergence.
items.citation: Min Jin, Victoria A. Jefferson, Zhe Zhao et al.. Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses. Nature Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning to multimodal healthcare diagnostics, motivated by the tension between the richness of modern biomedical data and the privacy constraints that prevent centralizing such data for traditional AI training. The authors conducted a literature review spanning federated learning applications across biomedical imaging modalities, electronic health records, wearable and physiological signals, chronic disease management, elder care, and clinical decision support. The core mechanism reviewed is federated learning's approach of training models locally at each institution and sharing only model updates rather than raw patient data, which improves regulatory alignment while still enabling multi-site collaboration. The review identifies persistent technical and ethical challenges, including gradient leakage, model inversion attacks, system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns, noting that privacy is not automatically guaranteed by federation alone. The authors synthesize findings across these domains to offer practical guidance for regulators, developers, and healthcare institutions aiming to deploy safe and equitable federated learning systems across diverse geographic and institutional settings.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
items.summary: This paper investigates electron thermopower in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, focusing on how the structure of Fermi-surface deformations influences thermal transport rather than just their relaxation rates. The authors introduce the concept of "thermal dressing," which describes the local temperature change associated with these deformations, and show that thermopower probes this structure directly. They find that thermopower overshoots its expected hydrodynamic value as a function of wave vector before falling to half that value in the ballistic limit, with the overshoot driven by collinear scattering that redistributes energy across the Fermi surface. Notably, at low temperatures the excess thermopower deviates from the linear-in-temperature scaling characteristic of Fermi liquids, instead decreasing only logarithmically, defining a distinct thermographic transport regime that differs from previously known tomographic effects in charge conductivity. The authors conclude that this overshoot is robust against realistic disorder and should be experimentally detectable using a thermocouple geometry with high-mobility samples.
items.citation: Johannes Hofmann. Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
items.summary: This paper investigated the properties of one of the earliest generations of stars in the universe by searching for chemical and spectroscopic signatures of Population III stars, the hypothesized first generation formed from primordial Big Bang elements. Using deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy of a strongly gravitationally lensed galaxy approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, the researchers detected helium and hydrogen emission lines alongside extremely weak oxygen emission lines. The measured helium-to-hydrogen line ratios are consistent with theoretical predictions for the intense ionizing radiation expected from Population III stellar populations, while the oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated at a tiny fraction of the solar value, indicating a nearly pristine chemical environment. These findings suggest that pockets of near-primordial gas still persisted in the universe a billion years after the Big Bang, potentially enriched only slightly by Population III stars themselves, though the authors acknowledge that accreting black holes cannot be fully ruled out as an alternative source of the hard ionizing radiation. The study offers some of the most direct observational evidence yet for the extremely low-metallicity environments in which the universe's first stars are predicted to have formed.
items.citation: Takahiro Morishita, Massimo Stiavelli, Tommaso Treu et al.. Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of object penetration in interactive video world models, where simulated agents pass through solid obstacles rather than being physically blocked by them. The authors first introduce a benchmark called NoPeBench to systematically evaluate how existing video world models handle physical obstacles, finding that none of the tested open-source models reliably prevent such penetration failures. Despite this, they discover that the hidden states of diffusion transformers already contain sufficient information to predict whether a given action will result in a penetration event. Building on this insight, they develop NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that trains a small prediction head on top of a frozen diffusion transformer's hidden states to classify candidate actions as safe or unsafe, then substitutes unsafe actions with safe alternatives that best preserve the original intent. The approach dramatically reduces physical violation rates across multiple video world models and demonstrates zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles.
items.citation: Yuhang Dai, Yinwei Wu, Ziyue Lin et al.. Non-penetrating World Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: This paper investigated the integration of neuromorphic sensing and computing into a complete autonomous robotic system, addressing the gap between isolated neuromorphic benchmarks and real-world deployment. The researchers built a four-wheel rover platform combining three real-time perception pipelines: a conventional audio tagging system running on a GPU, a spiking neural network deployed on dedicated neuromorphic audio hardware for on-chip sound classification, and an event-camera-based spiking detector for traffic cone identification. All components were containerized and coordinated through a robotics middleware framework, with a dispatcher translating detected perceptual classes into robot behaviors to close the loop between sensing and actuation. The platform was demonstrated in a proof-of-concept scenario showing the robot responding to audio events and detecting visual landmarks simultaneously in real time. The work establishes the feasibility of combining multiple neuromorphic hardware components into a functional, multimodal robotic system operating under realistic latency and energy constraints.
items.citation: Guillem Fustier-Castillo, Ruben Ribes-Serrano, Javier Naranjo-Alcazar et al.. Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
items.summary: This paper reframes the Rydberg-atom receiver using established microwave-photonics concepts, specifically treating it as an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link in which the laser-driven atomic vapor acts as the modulator. The authors derive a closed-form expression for the transmission of a warm vapor by averaging the four-level atomic response over thermal velocity distributions, then extract standard RF link budget quantities including conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, and dynamic range from this single function. Key findings include that instantaneous bandwidth is determined by half the electromagnetically induced transparency window width, and that the local oscillator governs even-order linearity by setting the second-order intercept near twice its own field amplitude. The closed-form results show excellent agreement with a full velocity-resolved density-matrix model for gain slope and intercept points, and reasonable agreement for bandwidth, though group delay is underestimated. While Rydberg receivers benefit from sensing volumes unconstrained by the Chu limit and responses tied to atomic constants, the analysis concludes that the noise figure of a warm vapor prevents it from serving as a general replacement for a conventional antenna and low-noise amplifier combination.
items.citation: David Rosser. A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations in evaluating instance segmentation when reference annotations contain systematic biases, such as merged touching objects or split fragmented ones arising from heuristic approximation or expert disagreement. The authors argue that existing metrics like Panoptic Quality treat all instances equally and cannot distinguish valid from invalid over- or under-segmentation when references themselves are biased. To address this, they introduce Star Panoptic Quality, a novel evaluation framework that constructs a star forest from the bipartite matching graph between predicted and reference instances, isolating clean matches, merges, and splits into distinct structural categories. Each failure mode is then weighted independently, allowing practitioners to apply leniency or penalties according to known annotation biases. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed metric both enables targeted penalization of specific failure modes and serves as a diagnostic tool for revealing their prevalence in a dataset.
items.citation: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.. Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development and clinical validation of a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing panel for simultaneous DNA/RNA pathogen detection in respiratory tract infections: a comprehensive performance evaluation.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing panel designed to simultaneously detect a broad range of bacterial, fungal, and viral pathogens from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples in patients with suspected lower respiratory tract infections. The panel incorporated simultaneous DNA and RNA co-detection along with a novel SNP-based bioinformatics pipeline using machine learning to distinguish true infections from laboratory contamination. Performance was evaluated against both conventional microbiological testing and metagenomic next-generation sequencing using a combined retrospective and prospective cohort of several hundred clinical samples. The panel demonstrated high sensitivity, particularly for viral pathogens, reliably detected fastidious organisms such as *Pneumocystis jirovecii* and *Legionella pneumophila*, and showed strong concordance with phenotypic antimicrobial resistance testing. The authors conclude that this targeted approach offers diagnostic performance comparable to metagenomic sequencing while providing advantages in turnaround time, contamination control, and resistance prediction, positioning it as a promising clinical tool for lower respiratory tract infection diagnostics.
items.citation: Long J, Tao X, Wang J et al.. Development and clinical validation of a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing panel for simultaneous DNA/RNA pathogen detection in respiratory tract infections: a comprehensive performance evaluation.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
