items.title: Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial and mycoplasmal respiratory pathogens in goats. Two triplex TaqMan panels were designed, one targeting three Mycoplasma species and another targeting three bacterial pathogens, and were evaluated for analytical specificity, sensitivity, and reproducibility using plasmid standards and nucleic acids from both target and non-target organisms. The assay demonstrated high specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target organisms, low detection limits across all six targets, and excellent reproducibility as indicated by low intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation. When applied to field-collected goat nasal swab samples, the assay detected at least one pathogen in the majority of samples and identified mixed infections in a substantial proportion of positive cases, highlighting the complexity of respiratory disease etiology in goats. The authors conclude that this tool offers a rapid and reliable approach for simultaneous pathogen detection with practical utility for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance in caprine populations.
items.citation: Fu M, Liu Y, Zhang Z et al.. Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.
items.summary: This review examines syndromic testing, a diagnostic approach that simultaneously detects multiple pathogens and antimicrobial resistance determinants from clinical specimens using nucleic acid amplification, and its impact on infectious disease management in the United States over the past two decades. The authors surveyed the landscape of FDA-cleared multiplex panels across seven major clinical syndromes, including respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, and central nervous system infections, among others, comparing their performance to traditional culture-based workflows that require substantially longer turnaround times. The review synthesizes evidence showing that syndromic panels deliver comprehensive pathogen identification within hours, enabling faster clinical decision-making and more targeted antimicrobial therapy. When integrated with antimicrobial stewardship programs, these panels can reduce unnecessary antimicrobial use and hospital length of stay, and a mortality benefit has been observed particularly in patients with bloodstream infections. However, the authors caution that rapid results do not automatically translate into improved patient outcomes, and challenges including evolving resistance patterns, geographic variation in pathogen distributions, and optimal panel utilization remain important barriers to realizing the full potential of syndromic testing.
items.citation: Wang G, Chen F. Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape
items.summary: This paper investigated the evolutionary dynamics of affinity maturation in germinal centers, where B cells undergo Darwinian selection to produce increasingly potent antibodies. The researchers developed an experimental evolution model by replaying over one hundred monoclonal germinal center reactions and used deep mutational scanning to assign affinity values to individual cells, thereby constructing a quantitative affinity landscape. Their analysis revealed that germinal centers achieve predictable evolutionary outcomes despite noisy selection, with the trajectory of affinity maturation heavily shaped by biases in somatic hypermutation that constrain which regions of sequence space are explored. They inferred a fitness landscape that quantitatively reproduces the observed affinity maturation trajectory and demonstrated that seemingly established features of germinal center biology—such as tolerance for low-affinity B cell lineages and rapid plateauing of antibody affinity—are likely artifacts of survivorship bias rather than true properties of the selection process.
items.citation: William S. DeWitt, Ashni A. Vora, Tatsuya Araki et al.. Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape. Cell. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: This review examines the development of ferrite-based nanomaterials as multifunctional biomedical platforms, covering both spinel and hexagonal ferrite structures. The authors analyze how atomic-level engineering strategies, including cation distribution, defect modulation, and morphological control, can be used to tune magnetic, catalytic, and thermal properties relevant to applications such as magnetic resonance imaging, drug delivery, hyperthermia, and antimicrobial therapy. Emerging applications highlighted include viscosity-independent magnetic hyperthermia, reactive oxygen species-mediated antimicrobial treatments, and magnetic tissue engineering. The review critically addresses the translational gap between laboratory performance and clinical use, identifying barriers such as discrepancies between colloidal and intracellular heating efficiency, protein corona complexity, and challenges in scalable, quality-compliant synthesis. The authors conclude by proposing a roadmap that integrates artificial intelligence-driven material discovery and green chemistry approaches to advance ferrite nanoplatforms toward precision medicine applications.
items.citation: Pramod D. Mhase, Varsha C. Pujari, Akash V. Fulari et al.. Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: These guidelines address the growing challenge of managing infection risk in patients with inflammatory bowel disease who are treated with immunosuppressive and biologic therapies. The authors, representing a major European gastroenterology organization, developed an updated evidence-based consensus covering the prevention, diagnosis, and management of opportunistic and other infections in this patient population. The update was motivated by the rapid expansion of available treatments, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, each carrying distinct infection risk profiles not fully addressed by prior guidance. The guidelines cover risk stratification alongside viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections, with particular emphasis on preventative strategies tailored to the contemporary therapeutic landscape. The document represents the most current synthesis of evidence on infection-related considerations for clinicians managing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans
items.summary: This study compared the B cell immune responses induced by conventional split-virion influenza vaccines versus investigational mRNA-based influenza vaccines in healthy young adults across two consecutive vaccination seasons. The researchers examined antibody titers, memory B cell frequencies, germinal center reactions in draining lymph nodes, and serum immunoglobulin repertoires using proteomic and B cell lineage analyses. They found that mRNA vaccines elicited stronger antibody responses and sustained germinal center reactions lasting at least six months in a subset of participants, effects not observed with conventional vaccines. The mRNA vaccines also increased the diversity of vaccine-induced serum antibody clonotypes and promoted expansion within pre-existing clonotypes, with lineage tracing linking this expansion to ongoing germinal center activity. This repertoire remodeling resulted in broader antibody binding against antigenically divergent influenza viruses, highlighting the importance of persistent germinal center responses in achieving wider antibody coverage.
items.citation: Hanover C. Matz, Tae-Geun Yu, Kritika Dixit et al.. mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans. Nature Immunology. 2026

items.title: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19
items.summary: This study investigated the reactivation of chronic viral infections in hospitalized patients with acute COVID-19 and examined whether such reactivations persist into long COVID. Using multi-omic longitudinal data — including immunological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic measurements — from a large cohort of hospitalized patients, the researchers tracked the reactivation of viruses from the Herpesviridae and Anelloviridae families over time. They found that reactivation of these chronic viruses occurred frequently during acute COVID-19, with each virus displaying distinct temporal dynamics, and that the degree of reactivation correlated with disease severity, immune dysregulation, and clinical outcomes. Importantly, the findings challenge the assumption that chronic viral reactivation requires immunosuppression, as reactivations were common even in immunocompetent individuals and were associated with heightened systemic inflammation rather than immune deficiency. The study also identified viral reactivation persisting into convalescence and found an association between Anelloviridae reactivation and long COVID, suggesting that immune and molecular signatures of reactivation could have prognostic and therapeutic relevance.
items.citation: Cole P. Maguire, Jing Chen, Nadine Rouphael et al.. Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19. Nature. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious clinical syndromes, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which carry significant morbidity and mortality burdens globally. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review identifies critical surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances discussed include molecular and genomic diagnostic tools, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-informed early warning systems. The authors argue that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks uniting human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global disease burden and improving preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: A Spatial Clustering and Resource Allocation Approach for Critical Services in Massive MIMO-Enabled Cellular Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of guaranteeing quality-of-service for critical real-time applications in cellular networks that must simultaneously support non-real-time traffic. The authors develop a joint clustering and resource allocation framework that exploits the spatial multiplexing capabilities of Massive MIMO technology, grouping users by the directional alignment of their channel vectors through a downlink probing strategy to manage interference. Channel estimation and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio derivation are performed within these clusters, after which a resource allocation optimization problem is formulated across user groups to prioritize real-time service requirements. The authors prove that the general form of this optimization problem is NP-hard, but identify a special case solvable in polynomial time via linear programming, and propose a linear relaxation-based suboptimal solution for the general case. Simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness of both the clustering strategy and the proposed resource allocation approaches.
items.citation: Eva Al Hajj Sleiman, Youssef Hussein, Vincent Angilella et al.. A Spatial Clustering and Resource Allocation Approach for Critical Services in Massive MIMO-Enabled Cellular Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Dual-Mode Protocol for Space-Time-Coding Metasurfaces in OFDM ISAC Systems
items.summary: The paper addresses limitations in existing integrated sensing and communication systems that use space-time-coding metasurfaces, which have typically relied on idealized narrowband models ignoring frequency-selective and angle-dependent physical effects. The authors developed a physics-based signal-processing framework for wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing waveforms that explicitly accounts for beam squint effects across the metasurface aperture. They proposed a dual-mode protocol in which the metasurface acts as a time-varying surface during a brief acquisition phase and then reconfigures as a conventional reconfigurable intelligent surface for data transmission. During acquisition, angle of arrival and composite channel parameters are jointly estimated via maximum likelihood from a single pilot symbol using active subcarriers and deliberately introduced virtual carriers, with the resulting estimates used to optimize the surface for subsequent transmission. Numerical results confirm the validity of the framework and demonstrate performance gains achieved by the proposed dual-mode approach.
items.citation: Donatella Darsena, Ivan Iudice, Giacinto Gelli et al.. A Dual-Mode Protocol for Space-Time-Coding Metasurfaces in OFDM ISAC Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: WINSO: A Large-Size Very-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Dataset for Wind Turbine Detection and Solar Panel Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces WINSO, a large-scale benchmark dataset designed to support automated detection of wind turbines and segmentation of solar panels from very-high-resolution satellite imagery. The dataset comprises thousands of large-size images drawn from diverse geographic locations across the Asia-Pacific region, covering an extensive land area and totaling hundreds of gigapixels, with instances annotated via horizontal bounding boxes for wind turbines and polygon masks for solar panels through manual annotation and expert verification. To establish performance baselines, the authors evaluated a range of state-of-the-art object detection and segmentation models, architectures specialized for ultra-high-resolution imagery, and vision-language models using different inference strategies. Cross-dataset evaluations on external public datasets demonstrated that models trained on WINSO generalize well beyond its geographic scope. The authors present WINSO as a standardized benchmark intended to advance wide-area, automated monitoring of clean-energy infrastructure in support of the global transition to net-zero emissions.
items.citation: Di Wang, Ke Li, Zhaokun Li et al.. WINSO: A Large-Size Very-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Dataset for Wind Turbine Detection and Solar Panel Segmentation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: GaLF-ST: Gaussian Latent Fields for Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing spatial gene expression patterns from sparse and limited observations in spatial transcriptomics. The authors propose GaLF-ST, a method that represents tissue space using learnable Gaussian functions with anisotropic covariances, where the weighted average of latent vectors at each location is decoded into multi-gene expression profiles through a shared nonlinear decoder. Unlike prior two-stage approaches that separately learn spatial embeddings and expression predictors, GaLF-ST jointly optimizes the Gaussian geometry, latent vectors, and decoder parameters using expression reconstruction error in a single training process. To evaluate the approach rigorously, the authors constructed a unified benchmark spanning multiple dataset groups and held-out fractions, comparing GaLF-ST against representative competing methods under consistent conditions. GaLF-ST demonstrated leading reconstruction performance across diverse tissues and observation densities while also substantially reducing computational resource requirements in terms of runtime and memory usage.
items.citation: Baichuan Yang, Yifan Luo, Yong Liu et al.. GaLF-ST: Gaussian Latent Fields for Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots, which represents a major obstacle to scaling semiconductor spin qubit systems. The authors developed an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that uses multiplexed gradient descent to perform autonomous tuning without relying on conventional machine learning algorithms that require global information or significant computational resources. The approach was implemented on an FPGA paired with an emulated quantum dot device, enabling the system to track environmental drift, recover from discrete charge jumps, and maintain stabilization under low signal-to-noise conditions without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system can navigate the charge-stability landscape to lock quantum dots to optimal operating points while remaining resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations. The authors argue that this "compute-in-place" architecture has a logic and power footprint compatible with future cryo-CMOS integration, making it a promising route toward scalable, autonomous spin qubit control.
items.citation: Leonardo Gaytan, Bradley Lloyd, Paul Kliewer et al.. Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Unified Proximity-Tactile Observation by a Capacitive Fingertip Array Constrained by a Metal Phalanx
items.summary: This paper presents a mechanistic analysis of a capacitive fingertip sensor array mounted on a robotic metal phalanx, designed to detect both the proximity of conductive objects and contact force through a thin silicone skin. The authors modeled the multi-conductor system using Maxwell capacitance matrices to rigorously relate the capacitance-to-digital converter readout to the actual electrode-target capacitance, accounting for driven-shield parasitics, crosstalk, and time-division-multiplexing settling effects. Three core mechanisms were examined: driven-shield current hiding and gain/phase-mismatch leakage, distinct near- and far-field sensing operators, and frame-rate limitations imposed by shield loading during multiplexed acquisition. A key finding is that a single electrode layer cannot produce a material-independent force map because proximity and force signals are inherently conflated, leading the authors to propose and analyze a dual-array stack where an outer array acts as a Faraday screen during contact while an inner array reads silicone compression. Finite element simulations provided a baseline characterization of contact response and crosstalk, though the authors explicitly note that force mapping, mechanical crosstalk, and bench measurements remain unvalidated, positioning the work as a theoretical and computational foundation for future prototype calibration.
items.citation: Shun Cheng. Mechanistic Analysis of Unified Proximity-Tactile Observation by a Capacitive Fingertip Array Constrained by a Metal Phalanx. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: Two pentaplex real-time fluorescent PCR panels were developed to enable simultaneous detection of ten pathogens responsible for respiratory and reproductive diseases in sheep and goats. The first panel targets five respiratory pathogens including Bluetongue virus, Foot-and-mouth disease virus, and Peste des petits ruminants virus, while the second panel targets five reproductive pathogens including *Brucella* spp., *Toxoplasma gondii*, and Border disease virus, with each panel utilizing six fluorescent channels. Analytical validation using reference materials demonstrated very low limits of detection, excellent linearity, and minimal variation both within and between assay runs, with no cross-reactivity observed among the ten target pathogens. Clinical validation using a large set of field samples collected across multiple provinces in China showed strong agreement with established reference detection methods. The resulting assay system offers a rapid, sensitive, and highly specific tool for differential diagnosis and surveillance of major ovine pathogens in a single workflow.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Mycoplasma pneumoniae Infection Associated With a Severe Asthma Exacerbation in a Five-Year-Old Child: A Case Report
items.citation: Yahia A, Alaoui-Inboui F, Ahmito O et al.. Mycoplasma pneumoniae Infection Associated With a Severe Asthma Exacerbation in a Five-Year-Old Child: A Case Report. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Integrated microfluidic biosensors: shaping the future of quantitative life sciences and on-chip molecular diagnostics
items.summary: This review paper examines the integration of microfluidic technologies with biosensing platforms and their applications across the life sciences and medical diagnostics. The authors survey a broad range of microfluidic approaches, including three-dimensional cell culture systems, inertial separation, acoustofluidics, dielectrophoresis, optofluidics, and immunoassays, alongside biosensor modalities such as electrochemical, electrophysiological, plasmonic, Raman, and quantum sensing. These combined systems are capable of detecting analytes spanning a wide size range, from nanometer-scale nucleic acids and proteins to millimeter-scale organisms, enabling rapid and sensitive analysis. The review argues that the synergy between microfluidics and biosensing confers advantages in sensitivity, speed, portability, and real-time monitoring, with transformative implications for human and animal health diagnostics, environmental sensing, and point-of-care testing. The authors also address existing technical challenges, future development opportunities, and highlight commercially successful products that have emerged from these integrated technologies.
items.citation: Ty Downing Naquin, Chloe M. Naquin, Qian WU et al.. Integrated microfluidic biosensors: shaping the future of quantitative life sciences and on-chip molecular diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
items.summary: This paper developed a point-of-care lateral-flow biosensor designed to simultaneously detect two biomarkers—NLRC3, an inflammatory risk indicator, and cardiac troponin T, a myocardial injury marker—to improve screening and diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes. The biosensor employs europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel format, completing quantitative measurement of both analytes from serum within twenty minutes. A Naïve Bayes machine-learning classifier was integrated to combine the two biomarker signals, enabling discrimination between acute myocardial infarction and unstable angina. Clinical evaluation showed that while NLRC3 alone achieved moderate accuracy for identifying acute coronary syndrome, the dual-analyte approach with machine learning substantially improved sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy for distinguishing between the two conditions. The authors conclude that merging inflammatory and myocardial-injury detection pathways in a single lateral-flow platform offers a practical decentralized triage tool for acute coronary syndrome management.
items.citation: Gu X, Teng P, Li X et al.. Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Lateral Flow Immunoassay Technology for Blood-Based Infection and Sepsis-Related Biomarker Detection: Trends, Analytical Performance, and Clinical Translation.
items.summary: This review examined the current state of lateral flow immunoassay technology for detecting infection and sepsis-related biomarkers in blood-based samples, addressing the limitations of conventional microbiological methods that are slow and of host-response biomarkers that lack specificity. The authors surveyed platforms targeting a range of biomarkers including procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, and pathogen antigens, covering multiple detection modalities from colorimetric and fluorescence-based readouts to electrochemical and smartphone-integrated approaches. Analytical performance characteristics such as detection limits, precision, and agreement with reference methods were critically evaluated alongside pre-analytical interferences including hematocrit variation, hemolysis, and incomplete plasma separation. While some platforms demonstrate promising sensitivity and concordance with established immunoassay methods, the review identifies persistent shortcomings in study design, including reliance on spiked samples, single-centre cohorts, and non-transferable clinical cutoffs. The authors conclude that broader clinical translation requires validation with native whole-blood specimens, robust lot-to-lot quality control, prospective multicentre trials, and demonstrated impact on antimicrobial stewardship and patient outcomes in intensive-care settings.
items.citation: Thapa R, Fuloria NK, Bhat AA et al.. Lateral Flow Immunoassay Technology for Blood-Based Infection and Sepsis-Related Biomarker Detection: Trends, Analytical Performance, and Clinical Translation.. Critical reviews in analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Rapid carbapenemase detection in enterobacterales using a lateral flow immunoassay: diagnostic performance and association with antimicrobial treatment decisions.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a lateral flow immunochromatographic assay (LFA) for detecting carbapenemases in Enterobacterales and examined whether same-day LFA results influenced clinical antimicrobial treatment decisions. Researchers compared the LFA against a commercial quantitative PCR method as the reference standard, as well as against two phenotypic tests, using both retrospective and prospective collections of isolates. The LFA achieved complete agreement with qPCR for carbapenemase detection in both cohorts, outperforming the phenotypic comparator methods, which showed notably lower sensitivity. The LFA also showed strong concordance with qPCR for identifying the specific carbapenemase type, with only a small number of discrepancies involving isolates carrying multiple carbapenemase genes. Clinically, LFA positivity was independently associated with same-day treatment escalation in the prospective cohort, supporting the utility of rapid carbapenemase identification in guiding timely antimicrobial management.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Genç L, Üs İZ, Tok ŞA et al.. Rapid carbapenemase detection in enterobacterales using a lateral flow immunoassay: diagnostic performance and association with antimicrobial treatment decisions.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Harnessing Plasmonic Cu2-xSe Transducers for Quantitative Near-Infrared II Photothermal Lateral Flow Exosome Detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a photothermal lateral flow assay biosensor operating in the near-infrared II window for the sensitive detection of glioblastoma-derived exosomes in serum samples. The researchers engineered silica-coated copper selenide core-shell nanoparticles conjugated with anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies as the photothermal transducer, combining numerical simulations with experimental characterization to establish the superior plasmonic and photothermal properties of the material in the near-infrared II range. The resulting biosensor achieved a broad dynamic detection range and a limit of detection that substantially outperformed conventional colorimetric lateral flow readouts. The platform also demonstrated reliable accuracy and robustness when applied to complex serum matrices, highlighting its suitability for point-of-care diagnostics. The study positions copper selenide nanoparticles as high-performance photothermal transducers with strong potential for advancing quantitative lateral flow assay-based clinical diagnostics.
items.citation: Liu B, Su X, Chen H et al.. Harnessing Plasmonic Cu2-xSe Transducers for Quantitative Near-Infrared II Photothermal Lateral Flow Exosome Detection.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines lateral flow immunoassay technology as a diagnostic platform for viral infectious diseases, with the aim of repositioning it beyond its conventional point-of-care role toward a broader point-of-need self-testing tool capable of large-scale epidemic screening. The authors systematically surveyed recent advances across three dimensions: signal generation and transduction strategies using diverse nanomaterials such as colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems; multimodal and multiplex detection approaches; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and system optimization. Applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids are comprehensively reviewed. The review also critically addresses current limitations including sensitivity constraints, target specificity, and practical challenges related to cost, usability, and stability. The authors conclude by proposing future directions centered on advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection, arguing that lateral flow immunoassay holds transformative potential for emergency pandemic screening and routine decentralized diagnostics.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
items.summary: This paper investigated methods for isolating brain cell type-specific extracellular vesicles from biofluids as a non-invasive approach to monitor neurological conditions. The researchers combined gene expression data with extracellular vesicle proteomic data to computationally identify transmembrane proteins that could serve as surface markers specific to neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and microglia, while also developing a high-purity isolation method and cataloguing extracellular vesicle proteins in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays to validate their predictions, they confirmed that the protein NRXN3 is present on extracellular vesicles in both cerebrospinal fluid and plasma and successfully used it to immuno-isolate a neuron-specific extracellular vesicle population. The study establishes a generalizable computational and experimental framework for enriching cell type-specific extracellular vesicles from accessible biofluids, with potential applications for studying brain diseases.
items.citation: Dmitry Ter‐Ovanesyan, Sara T. Whiteman, Tal Gilboa et al.. Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles. Nature Neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, encompassing both the molecular mechanisms driving the disease and the therapeutic strategies being developed to combat it. The authors synthesize recent advances across several domains, including the role of apolipoprotein E biology, neuroimmunological processes, and biomarker discovery, alongside the complex pathological landscape that extends beyond amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles to drive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. The review highlights that newly developed disease-modifying therapies can slow cognitive decline by clearing amyloid from the brain, though interventions capable of preventing or halting cognitive impairment altogether remain unavailable. The authors argue that these collective advances are transforming both the diagnosis and treatment of Alzheimer's disease, raising the prospect that the condition may one day be not only treatable but preventable.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: Advances and Challenges in Wearable Sensors for Health Monitoring
items.summary: This mega-review examines the current state of wearable sensor technologies for continuous and non-invasive health monitoring, bringing together leading researchers to synthesize advances across the field. The authors conducted a citation network analysis to map the landscape of the discipline and then systematically reviewed chemical and physical biosensors operating across a range of biofluids and device formats, including smart contact lenses, textiles, mouthguards, wristbands, and implantable systems. The review also covers the underlying enabling technologies, including soft electronics and advanced materials, signal acquisition and transmission strategies, on-body energy harvesting, and the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning for data management and analytical enhancement. The authors identify wearable biosensors as capable of generating unprecedented volumes of health-relevant data that could support more informed clinical decision-making and closer patient follow-up. Beyond the science, the review addresses business, regulatory, and ethical considerations, positioning the work as both a synthesis of current capabilities and a guide for promising future research directions.
items.citation: Laís Canniatti Brazaca, Alvaro Moreno Lozano, Beatriz Mayol et al.. Advances and Challenges in Wearable Sensors for Health Monitoring. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious clinical syndromes — hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome — both carrying significant morbidity and mortality. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics, and clinical management, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review highlights critical surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. It also discusses emerging tools including molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems. The authors argue that integrated One Health frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring — alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration — are essential for improving outbreak preparedness and reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques
items.summary: This review examines the full spectrum of bacterial identification methods, motivated by the growing global burden of infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed techniques ranging from classical approaches such as microscopy, culture, and biochemical testing through to immunological, proteomic, and spectroscopic methods, as well as advanced molecular tools including various forms of polymerase chain reaction, sequencing, and metagenomics. Emerging technologies such as CRISPR-based diagnostics and phage- and nanomaterial-based detection systems are also discussed, alongside the incorporation of artificial intelligence into analytical workflows. The review concludes that integrating these diverse approaches can improve the accuracy, speed, and breadth of bacterial identification across clinical, veterinary, agricultural, and environmental contexts. However, the authors caution that inconsistencies in bioinformatics frameworks and algorithm-defined thresholds currently hinder standardized implementation, making harmonization and careful validation a priority alongside technological advancement.
items.citation: Ina Gajić, Milos Jovicevic, Dušan Kekić et al.. Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
items.summary: This paper studies the uniqueness of solutions to the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations within the symmetric class of axially symmetric, swirl-free flows. The authors construct two distinct Leray solutions that share identical initial data, are smooth for all positive times, satisfy the energy identity, and belong to optimal Sobolev and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin function spaces — a setting where smooth solutions are known to be globally regular. The construction is achieved through a computer-assisted proof that identifies a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, combining explicit asymptotic expansions, global residual estimates, weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals, and contraction arguments to correct both a stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair. The result establishes that non-uniqueness can occur even within a symmetry class that rules out finite-time blowup, and that it persists in the sharpest known function space thresholds previously thought to guarantee uniqueness. This work resolves, in this symmetric setting, a fundamental question about whether energy-class solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations can fail to be unique.
items.citation: Matthieu Cadiot, Alexandru Ionescu, Hao Jia et al.. On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of classifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using EEG signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing recordings from multiple participants across five task conditions, linking continuous EEG signals to precomputed features spanning seven distinct feature families and documenting all quality control decisions to ensure comparability across analyses. The resulting dataset provides a standardized resource where researchers can evaluate different EEG-derived measurements on identical time intervals for each participant and task. As an illustrative application, the authors compared a machine learning classifier using all feature families against a baseline prevalence predictor, finding that discrimination between recruitment groups varied across task conditions, with one task showing stronger separation than others. The authors explicitly caution that these descriptive findings do not establish diagnostic validity, and the dataset, curation tools, and example results are made publicly available to support future research.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: This paper investigated the dynamic behavior of an all-electric ship powered by a small modular reactor when propulsion loads change suddenly, examining how the resulting transients propagate across coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical subsystems. The researchers developed an integrated simulation model linking a pressurized water reactor, a moving-boundary steam generator, a turbine-generator set, an AC shipboard electrical network, a propulsion motor, and a battery energy storage system. They applied a step reduction in propulsion motor torque and compared system responses with and without battery support. Without the battery, the mismatch between turbine mechanical output and electrical demand caused a large over-frequency excursion, while adding the battery dramatically suppressed the frequency peak and simultaneously smoothed upstream disturbances in steam flow, reactor coolant temperature, reactivity, and thermal power. The findings underscore that nuclear-powered electric ships must be analyzed as tightly coupled multi-domain systems and that battery energy storage meaningfully improves short-term load-following performance.
items.citation: Ali Mahboub Rad, Jie Zhang. Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
items.summary: This study experimentally investigated how the amplitude and phase of sinusoidal blade pitching affect both power extraction and the hydrodynamic energy exchanged through pitching in a vertical-axis turbine, examining whether favorable pitch motions could potentially be sustained passively. Using a single-blade model traversing a circular path in a water channel, the researchers tested hundreds of prescribed-pitch conditions across a range of tip-speed ratios, measuring forces, power coefficients, and flow fields via particle image velocimetry. They found that the optimal pitching amplitude decreases and the optimal phase shifts as tip-speed ratio increases, with sinusoidal pitching yielding substantial improvements in cycle-averaged power coefficient across all conditions tested. Analysis of pitching-energy exchange revealed that the best-performing motions at lower tip-speed ratios involve nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work, while at higher tip-speed ratios the flow actually transfers net energy into the pitching motion, suggesting passive operation may be energetically feasible even under assumed dissipation. Flow measurements indicated that performance gains at low tip-speed ratio arise from delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and prolonged favorable loading, whereas at high tip-speed ratio only localized flow changes occur, and the joint power-and-pitching-energy maps provide a framework for identifying candidate motions for passive or assisted pitching device development.
items.citation: Zihan Zhang, Anchi Li, Qimin Feng et al.. Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately modeling vehicle dynamics near the limits of handling for autonomous racing, where mismatches between nominal and actual dynamics degrade performance. Existing on-track learning approaches handle either physical parameter adaptation or residual learning separately, limiting their ability to fully resolve dynamic mismatches. The proposed interactive semi-parametric framework jointly learns both physical parameters and a residual term under a single shared prediction-error objective, with the two components recursively updating each other in turn while only accepting updates that do not increase the objective, guaranteeing non-increasing convergence. Through numerical simulations and hardware experiments, the framework outperforms baseline methods, substantially reducing one-step prediction errors in lateral velocity and yaw rate compared to a nominal model alone.
items.citation: Jungbin Kim, Youngim Nam, Cheolhyeon Kwon. Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance
items.summary: This paper addresses the numerical modeling challenges associated with underground hydrogen storage in porous media, where accurate simulation of geochemical processes is critical for assessing feasibility and safe operation. The authors adopt a Globally Implicit Approach to avoid the splitting errors introduced by sequential solution methods, which also tend to assume a persistent liquid phase — an assumption that breaks down near wells during gas injection or withdrawal due to aqueous phase vaporization and mineral precipitation. They extend Coats' formulation to multiphase reactive transport, introducing new molar concentration unknowns for basis species that handle the disappearance and reappearance of the aqueous phase while preserving the nonsingularity of the Jacobian matrix, with phase appearance managed through a multiphase flash calculation algorithm. The method is validated against established carbon dioxide storage benchmark problems and then applied to a cyclic hydrogen injection and withdrawal scenario in an aquifer. The work provides a robust, fully implicit framework for simulating the complex coupled flow and geochemical dynamics relevant to underground hydrogen storage systems.
items.citation: Thomas Jacumin, Roland Masson, Laurent Jeannin et al.. A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: The study evaluated the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay as a candidate for primary nucleic acid testing within HIV-1 diagnostic workflows, with the goal of enabling both diagnosis and viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter at the point of care. The assay was assessed for analytical range, precision, reproducibility, and agreement against standard-of-care methods including the Roche cobas HIV-1 quantitative assay and four other HIV assays. The Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC demonstrated a broad measurable analytical range with perfect detection across tested concentrations and full agreement with the comparator quantitative assay on a panel of positive and negative samples, while achieving turnaround times substantially faster than conventional batch testing. However, positive agreement with other assays was incomplete, with most discrepancies occurring in samples below the lower limit of quantification, and the assay produced a small proportion of invalid results. The findings indicate that while rapid quantitative molecular testing holds promise for streamlining HIV-1 diagnosis and care linkage, current limitations in sensitivity at low viral loads underscore the need for continued development of both sensitive and rapid diagnostic approaches.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper structured opposing arguments around four key issues: whether athletes experience greater infection rates than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, and anxiety, and whether available biomarkers and study designs are adequate to assess immune health in those performing arduous exercise. While moderate-intensity exercise of limited duration is broadly considered beneficial for immune defense, the prevailing view that high-intensity or prolonged exercise characteristic of elite athletes and military personnel suppresses immunity has been challenged, given the difficulty of isolating exercise as a causal variable from the many other stressors these populations face. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but whether exercise per se independently drives increased infection risk in athletes remains unresolved. The authors call for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle these complex relationships within the field of exercise immunology.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. Exercise immunology review. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning in large language models. The researchers developed MedicalAgentsBench, a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets using difficulty-aware selection and contamination screening, then systematically evaluated a range of internalized reasoning models, base models, and externalized multi-agent scaffolding methods. They found that both approaches independently improve performance on complex clinical questions, and critically, that combining them yields compounding benefits, with the highest accuracy achieved by applying agent workflows on top of an internalized reasoning model. A cost-performance analysis further demonstrated that this combined approach dominates the efficiency frontier, while lighter-weight optimizations on less expensive models provide viable alternatives for resource-constrained settings.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize current knowledge across genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches, considering how deep learning architectures can extract meaningful patterns from these complex, high-dimensional biological datasets. The paper analyzes applications spanning the full drug development pipeline, including target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment, with illustrative cases drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The authors argue that combining multiomics with artificial intelligence accelerates hypothesis generation and enables more precise therapeutic interventions, while also acknowledging persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic biases. Overall, the review presents a forward-looking perspective on how this technological convergence is ushering in a new era of bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant rates of acute-on-chronic liver failure, end-stage cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of scientific progress. A regional taskforce of key opinion leaders was convened to synthesize current evidence and account for shifts in hepatitis B epidemiology, socioeconomic factors, and technological advances. The resulting clinical practice guidelines provide updated recommendations spanning thirteen major areas, encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance. The guidelines are intended to support healthcare professionals, policymakers, and patients in making practical, cost-effective decisions for managing chronic hepatitis B, with the overarching goal of reducing disease burden across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Time to HIV rebound after infusion of long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies 3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS and analytical treatment interruption (the RIO trial): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
items.summary: The RIO trial investigated whether a combination of two Fc-engineered long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies, 3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS, could maintain HIV suppression in the absence of antiretroviral therapy. In this double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, virally suppressed adults who had initiated antiretroviral therapy during early-stage HIV infection received either the antibody combination or saline placebo intravenously, after which antiretroviral therapy was interrupted. By twenty weeks after treatment interruption, the vast majority of participants in the antibody arm remained free of viral rebound, compared with very few in the placebo arm, with antibody recipients being substantially less likely to experience rebound. The safety profile was broadly similar between arms, with no treatment-related serious adverse events identified. The findings suggest that long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies represent a promising strategy for achieving extended antiretroviral therapy-free HIV remission in people treated during early infection.
items.citation: Ming Jie Lee, Louise-Rae Cherrill, Panagiota Zacharopoulou et al.. Time to HIV rebound after infusion of long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies 3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS and analytical treatment interruption (the RIO trial): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial. The Lancet HIV. 2026

items.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper introduces MemOnce, a new memory architecture designed to address the scalability limitations of large language models in long-horizon and continual interaction settings. Standard Transformers suffer from linear memory growth and quadratic computational complexity due to token-level key-value caches, while existing linear-time alternatives fail to preserve fine-grained details; MemOnce aims to overcome both limitations. The architecture relies on two core innovations: a memory encoder-decoder that caches a compact subset of final-layer hidden states and dynamically reconstructs key-value caches for attention layers, and a memory sparse attention mechanism that adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations using sparse indices computed once across all layers. Together, these designs yield linear-time complexity and dramatically reduced memory footprints compared to standard approaches. Experiments demonstrate that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and competing architectures across a range of model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms, while also generalizing zero-shot to downstream representation tasks with competitive results against specialized models.
items.citation: Chang Nie, Chaoyou Fu, Songlin Liu et al.. MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: This paper investigated the dynamic behavior of a small modular reactor-powered all-electric ship during propulsion-load changes, focusing on how transients propagate across coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical subsystems. The researchers developed an integrated model linking a pressurized water reactor, a steam generator, a turbine, a synchronous generator, a shipboard alternating-current electrical network, a propulsion motor, and a battery energy storage system. A sudden reduction in propulsion motor load was applied as the test scenario, and the system responses with and without battery support were compared. Without the battery, the mismatch between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand caused a large frequency overshoot, while with battery support the excess electrical power was absorbed and the frequency excursion was dramatically reduced. The study concludes that battery energy storage also indirectly stabilizes upstream steam-cycle and reactor variables, and that treating nuclear-powered electric ships as fully coupled multi-domain systems is essential for accurately assessing their load-following performance.
items.citation: Ali Mahboub Rad, Jie Zhang. Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
items.summary: This study investigated how sinusoidal blade pitching amplitude and phase affect both power extraction and the energy exchanged through the pitching motion itself in vertical-axis turbines. Using a single-blade model following a circular trajectory in a water channel, researchers experimentally tested hundreds of prescribed-pitch conditions across a range of tip-speed ratios. They found that the optimal pitching amplitude decreases and the optimal phase shifts as tip-speed ratio increases, with sinusoidal pitching substantially improving power output across all tested conditions. At lower tip-speed ratios, the performance gains were linked to delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and more favorable blade loading, while at higher tip-speed ratios the improvements were more localized with less alteration of the primary power-producing event. Crucially, the pitching-energy maps revealed that the best-performing motions at higher tip-speed ratios receive net energy from the flow through pitching, suggesting these motions may be achievable passively, and the analysis identifies candidate pitching conditions with sufficient energetic margin to remain viable even in the presence of mechanical dissipation.
items.citation: Zihan Zhang, Anchi Li, Qimin Feng et al.. Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of automatically selecting the best quantum processing unit (QPU) for a given circuit workload in multi-vendor cluster environments, rather than relying on user-specified device choices based on average fidelity. The core challenge is that transpiling a circuit to match different devices' qubit connectivity adds gates and degrades fidelity in device-specific ways, meaning the best device on average may not be best for a particular circuit, yet compiling for every candidate device to check is too slow for real-time scheduling. The proposed approach uses a training-free, compilation-free estimator that predicts post-transpilation success probability for all candidate QPUs in milliseconds, filters out devices unlikely to meet the user's fidelity requirement, and only then compiles and runs on the selected device. Evaluated in simulation and on real IBM hardware, the estimator closely matches actual post-compilation fidelity rankings and substantially reduces requirement violations compared to naive device selection, while also distributing load across devices rather than concentrating jobs on one. The approach generalizes across vendors when published error rates accurately reflect true device performance, but breaks down when vendor-reported figures are misleading.
items.citation: Ana Paula Appel. Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Interaction and confinement effects for a ${}^6\mathrm{Li}_2$ condensate in a shaken lattice
items.summary: This paper investigates a molecular Bose-Einstein condensate of lithium-6 dimers loaded into a Floquet-engineered double-well dispersion created by a shaken one-dimensional optical lattice. The researchers improved upon earlier experiments by aligning the lattice axis with the trapping potential and implementing a multifrequency counterdiabatic shaking sequence to load the condensate more efficiently into the double-well quasimomentum minima, extending the accessible experimental timescale well beyond previous limits. At longer times, they observed that stronger axial confinement produces a population peak at the Brillouin zone edge, with shaking-frequency spectroscopy revealing roughly equal occupation of the ground and first excited bands at that edge. By ramping the magnetic field toward a Feshbach resonance to increase interparticle interactions, they found that the characteristic bifurcation of the condensate into two clusters at opposite quasimomenta weakens and eventually vanishes, an effect they attribute to the increasing physical size of the molecules near resonance.
items.citation: Yang-Hao Lee, Duc Trong Le, John Karnosh et al.. Interaction and confinement effects for a ${}^6\mathrm{Li}_2$ condensate in a shaken lattice. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback: A teachable perception-action framework for everyday self-regulation
items.summary: This paper addresses the gap between body-based self-regulation practices and a coherent explanatory framework for how they work, arguing that understanding mechanism can itself influence experience, as has been demonstrated in pain neuroscience education. The authors developed the Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback, a model describing any action as moving through sensing, processing, choosing, and executing, with feedback operating across all steps via synaptic plasticity, habit formation, and allostatic load. The model was developed iteratively across multiple cohorts of a workshop for non-clinical adults and integrates established concepts including the perception-action cycle, interoceptive inference, the autonomic space model, and the defence cascade. A range of body-based practices are mapped onto the loop with proposed mechanisms and evidence appraisals, and the framework is translated into practitioner skills. The paper presents the model as a teachable wellbeing framework rather than a clinical treatment, and derives several testable propositions to guide future empirical evaluation.
items.citation: Sundeep Kapila. The Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback: A teachable perception-action framework for everyday self-regulation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Association of antiretroviral regimen changes and tuberculosis preventive therapy with all-cause mortality among adults on ART in a high-mobility primary care setting in Northwest Ethiopia: a retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This retrospective cohort study examined factors associated with all-cause mortality among adults receiving antiretroviral therapy at a primary health center in a high-mobility setting in Northwest Ethiopia, a location serving seasonal and migrant workers. Using survival analysis and multivariable Cox regression on a decade of follow-up data, the researchers assessed whether antiretroviral regimen changes, tuberculosis preventive therapy receipt, viral load suppression, and CD4 count were linked to mortality risk. They found that mortality remained substantial, with the absence of documented antiretroviral regimen changes and non-receipt of tuberculosis preventive therapy being the strongest independent predictors of death. Unsuppressed viral load and lower CD4 count were also independently associated with increased mortality risk. The authors conclude that appropriate antiretroviral regimen management, tuberculosis preventive therapy provision, and close immunological and virological monitoring are critical for improving survival in this population.
items.citation: Yenew M, Melese W, Tsega TD et al.. Association of antiretroviral regimen changes and tuberculosis preventive therapy with all-cause mortality among adults on ART in a high-mobility primary care setting in Northwest Ethiopia: a retrospective cohort study.. Tropical medicine and health. 2026

items.title: Integrated community-based HIV+NCD care in microfinance groups in Kenya: results from the Harambee cluster randomised trial.
items.citation: Genberg BL, Steingrimsson JA, Kafu C et al.. Integrated community-based HIV+NCD care in microfinance groups in Kenya: results from the Harambee cluster randomised trial.. BMJ global health. 2026

items.title: Viral suppression among adolescents and adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era.
items.summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the rate of viral suppression and its predictors among adolescents and adults living with HIV in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era, covering the period from early 2018 through late 2022. Using proportional stratified random sampling, the researchers followed over four hundred patients who initiated antiretroviral therapy at public health facilities in Shashemene City, applying Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression to assess time to and predictors of suppression. Roughly seventy percent of patients achieved viral suppression over the follow-up period, with a median time to suppression of approximately nine months, falling short of the international target of ninety-five percent suppression. Rapid ART initiation was strongly associated with earlier viral suppression, while undernutrition, poor ambulatory status, and suboptimal adherence were each independently associated with lower likelihood of achieving suppression. The authors conclude that strengthening rapid treatment initiation, supporting medication adherence, and providing nutritional interventions are critical strategies to improve viral suppression outcomes in this population.
items.citation: Jarso H, Asu R, Negawo S et al.. Viral suppression among adolescents and adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.
items.summary: This study examined long-term treatment outcomes among patients with advanced HIV disease who initiated antiretroviral therapy in rural KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, over a twelve-year period spanning multiple policy eras. Using a retrospective cohort design drawing on routine data from public health facilities, the researchers assessed retention in care and virological suppression at multiple time points among adults with severely compromised immune function. Retention in care remained high across follow-up periods, and viral load suppression exceeded the majority threshold among those with available test results, with outcomes improving notably under the Universal Test and Treat era compared to earlier treatment periods. Men and individuals with the lowest CD4 counts faced greater risk of loss to follow-up, while women and those starting treatment within a week of diagnosis were more likely to achieve virological suppression. The authors conclude that while retention and suppression rates are encouraging, viral load testing uptake remains inadequate and gaps persist in achieving undetectable viral loads, underscoring the need for the WHO advanced HIV disease care package, earlier treatment initiation, and targeted interventions for men.
items.citation: Kitenge MK, Fatti G, Laxmeshwar C et al.. Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.
items.summary: This study investigated why healthcare workers in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire sometimes fail to accurately record malaria rapid diagnostic test results, a problem that undermines malaria surveillance. Using a qualitative approach embedded within a broader mixed-methods evaluation, researchers photographed RDTs performed by healthcare workers, had results independently verified by an external panel, and then conducted semi-structured interviews with workers selected based on whether their recorded interpretations agreed or disagreed with the independent readings. The primary factor distinguishing those who recorded results accurately from those who did not was not a lack of knowledge or resources, but rather differing levels of confidence in negative RDT results, particularly fear that a negative result might be a false negative in a symptomatic patient. Workers with low recording accuracy more often reported deliberately falsifying registers—changing negative results to positive or omitting antimalarial prescriptions—to align documentation with their clinical decisions to treat despite a negative result. The authors conclude that interventions should focus on building clinical decision-making confidence for RDT-negative fevers, expanding non-malarial diagnostic options, and redesigning documentation systems to allow transparent recording of guideline non-adherence without incentivizing misreporting.
items.citation: Kouakou OMA, Bédia-Tanoh VA, Arnzen A et al.. A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.. Malaria journal. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are limited by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and compared the new Bioline Malaria multi-Ag RDT, which detects HRP2 and dual pLDH markers, against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and near-perfect agreement with microscopy, performing well for clinical diagnosis in routine settings. However, when qPCR served as the reference standard, sensitivity for *P. falciparum* detection declined notably, revealing that submicroscopic and low-density infections were frequently missed. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is suitable for frontline clinical diagnosis, more sensitive molecular tools are necessary for effective malaria surveillance and control in co-endemic areas.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026
