The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases
items.summary: This paper examined how human-driven environmental and social changes shape the geographic patterns of infectious disease outbreaks across a broad range of diseases. The researchers compiled a large database of outbreak event records spanning dozens of diseases and systematically evaluated multiple hypothesized drivers—including land use change, climate variables, agricultural intensification, and healthcare access—while accounting for detection and reporting biases. They found that outbreak risk tends to be highest in mosaic landscapes where people and livestock coexist near forests and fragmented ecosystems, and that declining precipitation is a shared driver for several vector-borne diseases, while directly transmitted zoonoses share few common drivers across diseases. A particularly consistent finding was that healthcare access strongly shapes observed outbreak geography, with reporting declining substantially for each additional hour of travel time to a health facility. The authors conclude that infectious disease emergence is fundamentally multi-causal, that interventions must be tailored to specific disease systems rather than applying universal strategies, and that investments in health infrastructure and One Health surveillance are essential complements to ecosystem-based approaches.
items.citation: Rory Gibb, Sadie J. Ryan, David M. Pigott et al.. The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases. Nature. 2026

items.title: Global trends in the burden of malaria: mapping the prevalence, incidence and mortality of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax in the era of climate change and emerging drug resistance
items.summary: This paper examined the global burden of malaria caused by the two principal parasite species, focusing on how climate change, antimalarial drug resistance, insecticide resistance, and vector adaptation are reshaping transmission and control prospects. The authors conducted a systematic review of evidence on prevalence, incidence, mortality, and geographical distribution, drawing on major bibliographic databases alongside authoritative surveillance and modelling sources, with findings synthesised by species, region, epidemiological outcome, and resistance characteristics. The review found substantial geographical heterogeneity in malaria burden, with one species dominating in sub-Saharan Africa and the other contributing considerably elsewhere, while climate variables such as temperature, precipitation, and humidity influenced transmission suitability, though projections of future climate-related shifts carried considerable uncertainty. Resistance to artemisinin and partner drugs, challenges in achieving radical cure for one species, and both insecticide resistance and behavioural changes in mosquito vectors were identified as major emerging threats to control efforts. The authors conclude that eliminating malaria sustainably will require integrated, species-specific strategies that are simultaneously sensitive to resistance patterns and climate dynamics, underpinned by robust surveillance and resilient health systems.
items.citation: Ebrahim Abbasi. Global trends in the burden of malaria: mapping the prevalence, incidence and mortality of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax in the era of climate change and emerging drug resistance. BMJ Global Health. 2026

items.title: Journal of Infectious Diseases and Immunity
items.summary: This study investigated the prevalence of malaria, syphilis, and Hepatitis B virus among pregnant women attending a health center in Nigeria, given the serious risks these infections pose to maternal and fetal health. Using serological testing on a consented group of pregnant women, researchers screened participants and also assessed their knowledge and use of mosquito prevention measures. Malaria was the most common infection identified, followed by Hepatitis B, while syphilis was absent entirely, and co-infection with malaria and Hepatitis B occurred in only a small number of participants. Age was not found to be a significant factor in the prevalence of either malaria or Hepatitis B. Despite universal awareness that mosquitoes transmit malaria, the majority of participants relied on room insecticide spray rather than insecticide-treated bed nets, suggesting gaps in preventive practice that public health education and early surveillance could help address.
items.venue: Journal of Infectious Diseases and Immunity
items.citation: Journal of Infectious Diseases and Immunity. Journal of Infectious Diseases and Immunity. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This paper investigated the subcellular organization of proteins in the malaria parasite *Plasmodium falciparum* during its invasive erythrocytic stage, aiming to address the large proportion of parasite proteins with unknown cellular locations or functions. The researchers applied a spatial proteomics approach called hyperLOPIT, combined with supervised machine learning, to map the subcellular localization of thousands of proteins expressed in late schizont stages. The resulting high-resolution maps resolved a large number of distinct cellular compartments, including sites within the infected host erythrocyte, and assigned a substantial portion of the detected proteome to specific niches. By integrating these spatial data with comparative genomic analyses, the study illuminated the evolutionary trajectories of *Plasmodium* organelles and the adaptive pressures shaping parasite biology. The work provides a foundational resource for understanding how the parasite's distinctive intracellular compartments underpin its ability to invade and develop within red blood cells, with implications for efforts to combat malaria.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Martin Quintana Flores, Alison C. Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.summary: The paper challenges the widely accepted claim that T violation is absent in neutrino disappearance channels, demonstrating that this holds only under specific conditions: symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase takes values that render the Jarlskog invariant zero. The authors show that the muon neutrino and tau neutrino survival probabilities contain a term dependent on the sine of the CP-violating phase that is genuinely nonzero when matter profiles are asymmetric, constituting a real T asymmetry rather than a mathematical triviality. They clarify that the conventional null result arises from an improper T test that amounts to subtracting a probability from itself, and they carefully distinguish proper from improper T, CP, and CPT tests for general matter profiles. Using a two-layer constant-density toy model, they find that T violation is maximized when one layer is near the solar resonance and the other near the atmospheric resonance. The paper further evaluates whether the matter asymmetry encountered in existing and planned long-baseline experiments is sufficient to make this sine-of-delta dependence observable in muon neutrino survival, and discusses future experimental scenarios that could probe this effect.
items.citation: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas. Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of classifying Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using EEG signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing EEG recordings from participants across five task conditions, linking continuous signals to precomputed measurements spanning seven feature families and over one hundred feature definitions, while documenting quality decisions throughout. The goal was to enable fair comparison of EEG-derived features by ensuring consistent signal preparation and shared analysis windows across participants and tasks. Technical validation confirmed high data retention after preprocessing, and an illustrative machine learning experiment using XGBoost across all feature families demonstrated that the ability to discriminate recruitment groups varied across task conditions. The authors emphasize that these descriptive findings from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity, and the dataset, curation software, and example results are made publicly available to support future research.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
items.summary: This paper investigates a previously unrecognized side-channel vulnerability in Android smartphones, demonstrating that the Camera2 subsystem can be exploited to eavesdrop on speech without microphone access. The researchers found that camera hardware stabilization pipelines capture high-rate gyroscope measurements and expose them through vendor metadata, completely bypassing Android's motion-sensor privacy defenses, including microphone toggle restrictions and sampling-rate caps. Testing across a large set of smartphones from multiple vendors, they found that a substantial proportion expose gyroscope data at rates exceeding the platform's official ceiling, with some flagship devices streaming at nearly double the permitted rate even when privacy toggles are engaged. To exploit this channel without requiring any device-specific calibration data, the authors developed Source-to-Leakage Learning, a physics-constrained simulation framework that trains a universal speech recognizer called CamEar on synthetic sensor traces rather than real recordings from target devices. CamEar substantially outperforms prior approaches that rely on target-device training data, achieving robust word and character accuracy across multiple high-rate devices while generalizing far better to unseen hardware than fine-tuned baseline models.
items.citation: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang. Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational burden of hyperparameter optimization on large datasets by proposing a ranking-preserving coreset selection framework. The approach identifies a compact data subset that maintains the relative ordering of hyperparameter configurations as evaluated on the full training data, formulating coreset construction itself as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes rank correlation while minimizing subset size. The resulting coreset is then used to accelerate three evolutionary hyperparameter optimization algorithms across a diverse set of tabular, text, and image classification benchmarks. Experiments demonstrate substantial reductions in optimization time with test accuracy comparable to full-dataset tuning, and the coreset's ranking preservation generalizes to held-out configurations not seen during construction. The one-time cost of building the coreset can be offset when it is reused across multiple hyperparameter optimization runs.
items.citation: Mamoona Tasadduq, Maryam Bashir. Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: This paper investigated how an all-electric ship powered by a small modular reactor responds to sudden changes in propulsion load, and how battery energy storage can mitigate the resulting transients. The researchers developed an integrated multi-domain model coupling a pressurized water reactor, a once-through steam generator, a turbine-generator set, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, a propulsion motor, and a grid-connected battery storage system. When a sudden reduction in propulsion motor demand was applied, the system without battery support experienced a large over-frequency transient as turbine mechanical power temporarily exceeded electrical demand, with cascading effects propagating back through the steam cycle and into reactor parameters such as coolant temperature, reactivity, and thermal power. Adding battery energy storage substantially reduced the frequency excursion by absorbing the surplus electrical power during the transient, and this electrical buffering also smoothed the upstream disturbances in steam flow, steam generator pressure, and reactor behavior. The findings underscore the necessity of treating nuclear-powered electric ships as tightly coupled multi-domain systems and demonstrate that battery integration meaningfully improves short-term load-following performance.
items.citation: Ali Mahboub Rad, Jie Zhang. Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
items.summary: This paper investigated whether the parameters describing buoyancy glitches in low-luminosity red giants — specifically their amplitude, location, and width — can be recovered from global stellar properties alone, rather than requiring detailed seismic modelling. The researchers trained gradient-boosted tree machine learning models on a large grid of synthetic stellar models, using global properties such as the frequency of maximum oscillation power and effective temperature as inputs. They found that the glitch location and width are recoverable with very high accuracy, while the glitch amplitude proved more difficult to recover, particularly in a specific range of large frequency separations where the glitch sits in a structurally complex transition region between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity. Interpretability analysis revealed that the machine learning models rely primarily on parameters reflecting evolutionary state, suggesting that two of the three glitch parameters are tightly governed by global evolutionary trends, whereas the amplitude encodes more localized structural information. The authors conclude that this approach offers a practical way to estimate buoyancy-glitch parameters for large asteroseismic surveys and to prioritize which stars warrant the more computationally expensive mixed-mode inversion analysis.
items.citation: Jiang Chen. Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Elusive Diagnosis: Miliary Tuberculosis With Initially Negative Diagnostic Tests.
items.summary: This case report describes the diagnostic challenges encountered in a young woman presenting with miliary tuberculosis, a severe disseminated form of *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* infection. The patient had persistent fever and respiratory symptoms with a travel history to a tuberculosis-endemic region, yet all initial rapid diagnostic tests — including sputum smears, PCR, and interferon-gamma release assay — returned negative results. Despite empirical treatment for pyrexia of unknown origin, the patient deteriorated to respiratory failure requiring intensive care, prompting initiation of empirical anti-tubercular therapy based on CT chest findings of bilateral pulmonary nodules and hilar lymphadenopathy. Definitive confirmation was ultimately achieved through endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration and mediastinal lymph node culture, after which the patient showed rapid and remarkable improvement. The case underscores the diagnostic difficulty posed by miliary tuberculosis when initial tests are falsely negative and highlights the value of invasive diagnostic modalities such as endobronchial ultrasound in securing a timely diagnosis.
items.citation: Khan MZ, Anwar A. An Elusive Diagnosis: Miliary Tuberculosis With Initially Negative Diagnostic Tests.. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Development of a Rapid Automated Point-of-Care Test for <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> Detection From Tongue Swabs and Sputum Specimens on the DASH® Rapid PCR System.
items.summary: This paper describes the development and evaluation of a rapid point-of-care PCR test for detecting *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* on the DASH® Rapid PCR System, designed for deployment in low- and middle-income countries with limited healthcare infrastructure. The assay uses cartridge-based sample preparation and targets two multicopy insertion sequences via quantitative PCR, and was evaluated using both tongue swab and sputum specimens from symptomatic clinic attendees in South Africa. The assay achieved a very low limit of detection and showed no cross-reactivity with non-tuberculosis mycobacterial strains, demonstrating strong analytical specificity. Clinical evaluations revealed high sensitivity and specificity for both specimen types, with tongue swabs performing comparably to paired sputum results assessed by an established reference method, and sputum specimens performing particularly well for smear-positive cases. The system's compatibility with battery operation and cartridge stability at elevated temperatures without refrigeration make it well suited for peripheral clinical settings lacking reliable electricity and air conditioning.
items.citation: Butzler MA, Reed JL, Olson AM et al.. Development of a Rapid Automated Point-of-Care Test for <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> Detection From Tongue Swabs and Sputum Specimens on the DASH® Rapid PCR System.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.
items.summary: This review examines the persistent diagnostic challenges posed by extrapulmonary tuberculosis, which disproportionately affects children and immunocompromised individuals and is complicated by low pathogen burden, anatomically diverse affected sites, and nonspecific clinical presentations. The authors integrate microbiological, molecular, sequencing-based, and histopathological evidence across multiple disease sites, including osteoarticular, lymph node, pleural, central nervous system, and disseminated forms, situating diagnostic approaches within the context of granuloma biology and caseous necrosis immunopathology. Key technologies reviewed include established molecular assays such as Xpert MTB/RIF and Ultra, targeted and metagenomic next-generation sequencing, and emerging host-response biomarkers alongside artificial intelligence-assisted histopathology. The review synthesizes comparative evidence to propose tiered diagnostic algorithms suited to resource-limited settings where the burden of disease is greatest, while identifying unresolved gaps in current international guidance. The authors argue that aligning diagnostic modality selection with anatomical site, specimen quality, pathological subtype, and available laboratory capacity can reduce time to diagnosis and support host-directed diagnostic strategies.
items.citation: Liu Q, Jiang Y. Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Microfluidic Profiling of an Immune Cell-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Signature for Active Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring.
items.summary: This paper investigated plasma extracellular vesicles carrying innate immune cell-associated surface proteins as biomarkers for diagnosing active tuberculosis and monitoring treatment response, aiming to address the limitations of conventional pathogen-detection methods in paucibacillary cases. Using whole-blood transcriptome profiling, the researchers identified four innate immune cell-associated surface markers and validated them through bead-based immunoprecipitation, then implemented this signature on an eight-channel microfluidic chip capable of analyzing a small volume of plasma within thirty minutes. In clinical testing, the platform achieved excellent discrimination between active tuberculosis patients and healthy controls, as well as between active tuberculosis and other respiratory diseases, while also providing complementary diagnostic information when standard individual tests yielded negative results. Additionally, longitudinal monitoring revealed that the tuberculosis-associated immune cell extracellular vesicle levels declined markedly following anti-tuberculosis treatment, suggesting utility for tracking therapeutic response. The authors conclude that this minimally invasive, rapid microfluidic profiling approach holds strong potential for both diagnosing active tuberculosis and monitoring treatment outcomes.
items.citation: Lee EJ, Nie C, Park S et al.. Microfluidic Profiling of an Immune Cell-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Signature for Active Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring.. Journal of extracellular vesicles. 2026

items.title: Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities
items.summary: This paper investigates security vulnerabilities in large language model-based multi-agent systems, specifically focusing on how manipulated knowledge can spread through communities of communicating agents. The researchers designed a two-stage attack methodology combining Persuasiveness Injection and Manipulated Knowledge Injection to cause agents to propagate both counterfactual and toxic information through normal agent communication, without relying on explicit adversarial prompt attacks. Experiments demonstrated that the attack successfully induced agents to spread manipulated knowledge while preserving their general capabilities, and that these manipulations persisted even through retrieval-augmented generation frameworks where agents store and later retrieve compromised chat histories. To counter these threats, the authors proposed two defense strategies involving system prompts that encourage critical verification of shared knowledge and the incorporation of supervisory agents to oversee interactions, both of which meaningfully reduced the spread of manipulated content. The work concludes that LLM-based multi-agent communities face critical and underexplored vulnerabilities requiring urgent adoption of targeted defensive measures.
items.citation: Tianjie Ju, Yiting Wang, Yi Hua et al.. Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities. Science China Information Sciences. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet, which employs a pseudobulk approach combining precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify genes differentially expressed with traits of interest across cell clusters. The tool was designed to handle complex statistical models while scaling efficiently to large cohorts, achieving substantially faster processing with lower memory requirements compared to existing workflows, and maintaining appropriate control of false positive rates. Performance was validated on previously published datasets as well as a novel dataset comprising over a million single nuclei from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls. The authors conclude that dreamlet offers a computationally and statistically improved solution for differential expression analysis in large-scale single-cell studies of human disease.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning in large language models. The researchers introduced a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets, with filtering for difficulty and contamination, to systematically evaluate both approaches. They tested a range of internalized reasoning models, standard base models, and externalized multi-agent frameworks across this benchmark. Their findings demonstrate that the two approaches are complementary rather than mutually exclusive, as combining agent workflows with an internalized reasoning model yielded the highest accuracy. Additionally, Pareto analysis revealed that this hybrid combination dominates the cost-performance frontier, while lightweight optimization on less expensive models provides a viable path for resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Training AI Co-Scientists Using Rubric Rewards
items.summary: This paper investigates how to train language models to generate better research plans for use as AI co-scientists assisting human researchers. The authors developed a scalable, automated pipeline that extracts research goals and domain-specific grading rubrics from existing research papers across multiple fields, then fine-tuned models using reinforcement learning where a frozen copy of the initial policy serves as a self-grader. This generator-verifier gap allows the model to improve without requiring external human supervision or execution feedback. Human expert evaluations involving hundreds of hours of assessment showed that experts preferred plans from the fine-tuned model the majority of the time and found the automatically extracted rubrics to be largely accurate. The approach demonstrated substantial relative improvements and strong cross-domain generalization, including to medical research settings where real-world execution feedback is impractical.
items.citation: Shashwat Goel, Rishi Hazra, Dulhan Jayalath et al.. Training AI Co-Scientists Using Rubric Rewards. International Conference on Machine Learning. 2026

items.title: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and the epitranscriptome: Advances in mapping native RNA landscapes
items.summary: This review examines nanopore direct RNA sequencing as a transformative approach for studying the transcriptome and epitranscriptome at single-molecule resolution. Unlike short-read RNA sequencing or complementary DNA-based long-read methods, the technology sequences native RNA molecules directly, allowing simultaneous detection of RNA modifications, full-length transcript structures, alternative splicing, and poly-adenylation tail features within individual reads. The authors trace the biophysical foundations and technological development of the method, compare its capabilities and limitations against competing approaches, and survey optimized experimental workflows for a broad range of RNA biotypes. They also review computational advances in modification detection, transcript reconstruction, isoform quantification, and integrative multi-layer analysis, while emphasizing the importance of benchmarking and orthogonal validation to distinguish genuine signals from computational inferences. The review concludes by highlighting emerging applications in complex transcriptome resolution, coordinated epitranscriptomic regulation, disease-associated RNA signatures, and the technology's potential role in precision medicine and broader biological research.
items.citation: Tianyuan Zhang, Jia Li, Chao Tang et al.. Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and the epitranscriptome: Advances in mapping native RNA landscapes. iMeta. 2026

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether T violation can manifest in neutrino disappearance channels, challenging the widespread claim that it cannot. The authors demonstrate that this claim holds only under restricted conditions — symmetric matter profiles or when the CP-violating phase is zero or π — and that muon and tau neutrino survival probabilities can carry a genuine sine-of-delta-dependent T asymmetry in asymmetric matter. They identify that the confusion in the literature stems from an improper T test that amounts to subtracting a probability from itself, and they carefully distinguish proper from improper T, CP, and CPT tests for arbitrary matter profiles. Using a two-layer constant-density toy model, they find that T violation is maximized when the two layers are near the solar and atmospheric resonances respectively, and they assess whether the matter asymmetry encountered by experiments such as DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande is sufficient to probe this effect in muon neutrino survival. The paper also discusses future experimental scenarios that could allow T and CP violation to be detected through the disappearance channel.
items.citation: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas. Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of classifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using electroencephalography signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing recordings from participants across five task conditions, computing features from seven EEG feature families applied to consistent time intervals, and documenting quality decisions throughout. The resulting dataset links continuous brain signals to precomputed measurements spanning over a hundred feature definitions, enabling systematic comparison across feature types on common analysis windows. Technical validation confirmed high retention of recording time after preprocessing, and illustrative machine learning analyses using gradient boosting showed that the ability to discriminate recruitment groups varied across task conditions, being stronger in one task than in others. The authors emphasize that these descriptive results do not establish diagnostic validity, but the publicly released dataset and curation software are intended to support reproducible research on EEG-based approaches to neurodevelopmental assessment.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
items.summary: This paper investigates a novel side-channel attack that exploits Android's Camera2 subsystem to perform acoustic eavesdropping without requiring any microphone permissions. The researchers discovered that Camera2's hardware abstraction layer captures high-rate gyroscope measurements through image stabilization pipelines and exposes them via vendor metadata, entirely bypassing Android's privacy protections—including microphone and camera toggle switches—and circumventing the sampling rate caps imposed on the standard SensorManager API. Testing across a wide range of smartphones from multiple vendors, they found that a substantial proportion expose gyroscope data through this channel, with several flagship devices streaming at rates far exceeding the regulated ceiling, since loudspeaker speech couples into chassis vibrations that are captured by this path. To exploit this channel without needing device-specific training data, the authors developed Source-to-Leakage Learning, a framework that uses a physics-constrained forward simulator to decouple speech content from device-specific mechanical resonances, enabling a universal speech recognizer trained only on simulated data. Their resulting system, CamEar, achieves substantially higher cross-device word and character accuracy than prior approaches that relied on real target-phone traces, demonstrating a practical and generalizable eavesdropping attack that defeats existing Android privacy defenses.
items.citation: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang. Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational burden of hyperparameter optimization on large datasets by proposing a ranking-preserving coreset selection framework. The approach identifies a compact data subset that faithfully reproduces the relative performance ordering of hyperparameter configurations seen on the full training set, formulating coreset selection itself as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes rank correlation while minimizing subset size. The resulting coreset is then used as a cheap proxy during hyperparameter search with several evolutionary algorithms, including a genetic algorithm, a CHC variant, and particle swarm optimization. Experiments across tabular, text, and image classification benchmarks demonstrate that the method substantially reduces the time spent in the hyperparameter optimization stage while preserving test accuracy comparable to full-data optimization, with speedups spanning roughly an order of magnitude depending on dataset and optimizer. The coreset also generalizes its ranking fidelity to configurations not seen during its construction, and its one-time construction cost can be amortized when the same coreset is reused across multiple optimization runs.
items.citation: Mamoona Tasadduq, Maryam Bashir. Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: This paper investigated the dynamic behavior of a small modular reactor-powered all-electric ship when propulsion loads change rapidly, examining how transients propagate across nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical subsystems simultaneously. The researchers developed an integrated simulation model coupling a pressurized water reactor, a moving-boundary steam generator, a turbine-generator set, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, a propulsion motor, and a grid-connected battery energy storage system. A sudden reduction in propulsion motor load was applied as a test case, and the system responses with and without battery storage were compared. Without battery support, the mismatch between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand caused a large over-frequency excursion, while adding the battery storage substantially dampened the frequency deviation and also smoothed upstream disturbances propagating into the steam cycle and reactor core. The findings underscore the value of treating nuclear-powered electric ships as tightly coupled multi-domain systems and demonstrate that battery energy storage meaningfully improves short-term load-following performance.
items.citation: Ali Mahboub Rad, Jie Zhang. Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
items.summary: This paper investigated whether the properties of buoyancy glitches in low-luminosity red giants—specifically their amplitude, location, and width—can be recovered from global stellar properties rather than through computationally expensive dedicated seismic modelling. The authors trained gradient-boosted tree machine learning models on a large grid of synthetic stellar models, with buoyancy-glitch parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. They found that the glitch location and width are recoverable with very high accuracy, while the glitch amplitude shows only moderate recoverability, particularly in a specific range of large frequency separations where the glitch lies in a transitional evanescent zone. Interpretability analysis revealed that the models rely primarily on the frequency of maximum oscillation power and effective temperature, indicating that predictions are largely driven by evolutionary state. The authors conclude that global stellar properties can serve as direct proxies for buoyancy-glitch parameters, offering a practical way to prioritize targets for detailed mixed-mode inversions in large asteroseismic surveys.
items.citation: Jiang Chen. Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cost and operational impact of a molecular point-of-care test for sexually transmitted infections in the emergency department.
items.summary: This study compared centralized laboratory testing to molecular point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections among female emergency department patients with suspected chlamydia, gonorrhea, or trichomonas. Using decision analysis and cost tables derived from a pre-post implementation study, researchers evaluated direct testing costs, follow-up costs, treatment accuracy outcomes, and emergency department return visits over a twelve-month horizon from both hospital and societal perspectives. Point-of-care testing was found to be more expensive in direct costs than centralized laboratory testing, and this difference was not offset by savings from reduced undertreatment follow-up or avoided societal costs of inappropriate treatment. From a societal standpoint, point-of-care testing increases overall costs and reduces hospital revenue compared to centralized testing under current pricing and reimbursement structures. However, the analysis suggests that hospitals with long emergency department wait times may achieve net revenue gains if improved patient throughput generates sufficient additional capacity utilization, even without full room occupancy or maximum reimbursement rates.
items.venue: The American journal of emergency medicine

items.title: Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank
items.summary: This paper studies multi-agent interacting particle systems that extend classical binary interactions to higher-order group interactions modeled on hypergraphs, where the underlying hypergraph is dense but nonuniform and of unbounded rank. The authors develop a rigorous mathematical framework combining PDE analysis, stochastic analysis, kinetic theory, and graph theory to derive the large-population mean-field limit of such systems. For the first time in the literature, they prove that when interaction kernels are sufficiently regular, the mean-field limit is governed by a Vlasov-type equation in the product space of positions and labels. The limiting hypergraph structure is encoded by a novel object called an unbounded-rank hypergraphon, and the resulting mean-field force incorporates infinitely many orders of interaction simultaneously. This work provides a foundational mathematical treatment of mean-field limits for higher-order interacting systems, addressing a setting of growing interest in the applied community.
items.citation: Nathalie Ayi, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato. Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank. Journal of Nonlinear Science. 2026

items.title: INSPECT-SR tool for assessing trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials
items.summary: The paper addresses the threat that untrustworthy randomised controlled trials pose to evidence synthesis, noting that such trials may contain serious flaws arising from research misconduct, fraud, or honest critical errors. When these problematic trials are included in systematic reviews and clinical guidelines, they risk distorting conclusions that inform healthcare decisions. To address this problem, the authors developed a tool called INSPECT-SR, designed to help researchers assess the trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials and identify those that should be excluded from systematic reviews. The paper describes the development process for INSPECT-SR and presents both the tool itself and an accompanying guidance document intended to support its use.
items.citation: Jack Wilkinson, Calvin Heal, Ella Flemyng et al.. INSPECT-SR tool for assessing trustworthiness of randomised controlled trials. BMJ. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines cyberpunk fiction through the interlocking lenses of cybernetics, the Gothic, and fiction, challenging the common characterization of cyberpunk as the literary expression of postmodernism or late capitalism. The author argues that postmodernism has been preoccupied with cybernetic themes while cybernetics itself has been haunted by the Gothic, and that Baudrillard's theories of simulation suggest fiction assumes a new cultural role in an era dominated by cybernetic processes. Drawing on Deleuze and Guattari's materialist reworking of the Gothic — derived from Worringer's concept of nonorganic continuum rather than conventional supernatural literary traditions — the thesis analyzes key cyberpunk texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition as centrally concerned with the collapse of boundaries between the animate and inanimate. The concept of the "flatline," borrowed from Gibson, is proposed as the theoretical site where the Gothic and cybernetics converge, encompassing both a state of "unlife" or "undeath" and a condition of radical immanence. The thesis is structured around four aspects of this flatline: the flatlining of cybernetics and postmodernism, of the body, of reproduction, and of fiction itself within the context of hyperreality.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases
items.summary: This paper investigated the anthropogenic drivers shaping the geographic distribution of outbreak risk across a large and diverse set of emerging infectious diseases. The researchers compiled tens of thousands of outbreak event records spanning dozens of diseases and systematically evaluated how social and environmental factors — including land use change, deforestation, agricultural intensification, climate variables, and healthcare access — influence where outbreaks occur, while correcting for detection and reporting biases. They found that outbreak risk is generally highest in mosaic landscapes where human settlements and livestock coexist near forests and fragmented ecosystems, and that long-term precipitation decline is a shared driver across several vector-borne diseases, while directly transmitted zoonoses such as Ebola and mpox share few common drivers. Healthcare access emerged as the most consistent cross-disease factor, with outbreak reporting declining substantially for each additional hour of travel time from a health facility. The authors conclude that infectious disease emergence is fundamentally multi-causal, that no universal prevention strategy is adequate, and that ecosystem-based public health interventions must be disease-specific and paired with strengthened health systems and One Health surveillance.
items.citation: Rory Gibb, Sadie J. Ryan, David M. Pigott et al.. The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases. Nature. 2026

items.title: Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming
items.summary: This paper investigated whether current large language models used in health and medicine are as safe and reliable as their performance on standard benchmarks suggests. The authors developed a Dynamic, Automatic and Systematic red-teaming framework that continuously stress-tests models across four safety-critical dimensions: robustness, privacy, bias, and hallucination, using adversarial agents that autonomously mutate test cases to expose vulnerabilities. Applying this framework to a broad set of state-of-the-art models revealed a stark "benchmarking gap," whereby models achieving strong accuracy on a widely used medical question-answering benchmark overwhelmingly failed when subjected to dynamic adversarial testing, suggesting their apparent competence reflects superficial memorization rather than genuine understanding. Failure rates were alarmingly high across all evaluated domains, with dynamic robustness testing, privacy elicitation, cognitive bias induction, and hallucination each exposing substantial vulnerabilities in models that appeared capable under static conditions. The authors argue that converting health-focused safety evaluation from fixed checklists into living adversarial audits is essential for identifying latent risks before these systems are deployed in clinical or consumer-facing settings.
items.citation: Jiazhen Pan, Bailiang Jian, Paul Hager et al.. Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of advances in prevention and treatment. A regional taskforce of key opinion leaders was convened to synthesize current evidence and account for shifts in hepatitis B epidemiology, socioeconomic factors, and emerging technologies. The resulting clinical practice guidelines provide updated recommendations across thirteen major domains covering screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance. The guidelines are intended to support healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and patients in making practical and cost-effective management decisions, with the overarching goal of reducing the disease burden of chronic hepatitis B across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.summary: This paper investigates whether neutrino disappearance channels can exhibit sensitivity to T-violation, challenging the widely repeated assertion in the literature that T-violation is zero in such channels. The authors demonstrate that this claim holds only under restricted conditions — specifically for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase causes the Jarlskog invariant to vanish — and that muon and tau neutrino survival probabilities carry a genuine sine-of-delta-dependent T asymmetry in asymmetric matter. They identify that the conventional claim stems from an improper T test that amounts to subtracting a probability from itself, and they carefully distinguish proper from improper T, CP, and CPT tests for arbitrary matter profiles. Using a two-layer constant-density toy model, they find that maximum T-violation arises when one layer is near the solar resonance and the other near the atmospheric resonance. The authors assess whether the matter asymmetry encountered by current long-baseline experiments is large enough to probe this effect in muon neutrino survival probability, and they discuss future experimental scenarios that could do so.
items.citation: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas. Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
items.summary: This paper investigates a novel side-channel attack that exploits Android's Camera2 subsystem to perform acoustic eavesdropping without requiring microphone permissions. The researchers discovered that Camera2's hardware abstraction layer captures high-rate gyroscope measurements through image stabilization pipelines and exposes them via vendor metadata, entirely bypassing Android's privacy defenses designed to prevent motion sensors from acting as covert microphones. Testing across a large set of smartphones spanning multiple vendors and release years, they found that a substantial majority exposed gyroscope data through this channel, with several flagship devices streaming at rates far exceeding the caps imposed on standard sensor access, and critically, neither disabling the microphone toggle nor the camera toggle suppressed the metadata stream. To exploit this channel without requiring device-specific training data, the authors developed Source-to-Leakage Learning, a physics-constrained simulation framework that decouples speech content from a particular phone's mechanical resonances and sampling characteristics, enabling a universal recognizer trained only on simulated data. Their system achieved substantially higher word and character recognition accuracy on unseen devices compared to prior approaches trained on real sensor traces, demonstrating that the attack generalizes across hardware without any target-device profiling.
items.citation: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang. Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of hyperparameter optimization on large datasets by proposing a ranking-preserving coreset selection framework that constructs a compact data subset suitable for evaluating hyperparameter configurations. The core idea is to formulate coreset selection itself as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes the Spearman rank correlation between configuration rankings obtained on the full dataset versus the subset, while simultaneously penalizing subset size. The resulting coreset is then used to accelerate three evolutionary hyperparameter optimization algorithms across a range of tabular, text, and image classification benchmarks. The framework achieves substantial speedups in the hyperparameter optimization stage while maintaining test accuracy comparable to optimizing on the full data, and the coreset generalizes its ranking-preservation property to held-out configurations not seen during construction. The one-time cost of building the coreset can be amortized when it is reused across multiple optimization runs.
items.citation: Mamoona Tasadduq, Maryam Bashir. Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
items.summary: This paper investigated whether the properties of buoyancy glitches in low-luminosity red giants — which encode localized information about stellar interior structure near the base of the convective envelope — can be recovered from global stellar observables using machine learning, rather than requiring computationally expensive dedicated seismic modelling. The authors trained gradient-boosted tree regressors on a large grid of synthetic stellar models, using global properties to predict buoyancy-glitch amplitude, location, and width, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. The glitch location and width were recovered with excellent accuracy, while the glitch amplitude showed only moderate recoverability, particularly in a specific range of large frequency separations where the glitch sits in a structurally complex transition region between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity. Interpretability analysis revealed that the predictions are dominated by effective temperature and the frequency of maximum oscillation power, indicating the regressors primarily leverage evolutionary state information. The authors conclude that global stellar properties can serve as direct estimates of buoyancy-glitch parameters, offering a practical way to prioritize stars for detailed mixed-mode inversions in large asteroseismic surveys.
items.citation: Jiang Chen. Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
items.summary: This study experimentally investigated how sinusoidal blade pitching amplitude and phase affect both power extraction and the energy exchanged through pitching motion in a vertical-axis turbine, with the goal of understanding whether blades could sustain such motions passively. Using a single-blade model following a circular trajectory in a water channel, researchers tested hundreds of prescribed-pitch conditions across a range of tip-speed ratios. They found that the optimal pitching amplitude decreases and the optimal phase shifts as tip-speed ratio increases, with sinusoidal pitching substantially improving power coefficients across all tested conditions. Analysis of pitching-energy maps revealed that the best-performing motions at lower tip-speed ratios involve nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work, while at higher tip-speed ratios the flow transfers net energy into the pitching motion, suggesting passive operation may be energetically feasible in those regimes. Flow visualization and force measurements showed that performance gains at low tip-speed ratios arise from delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and prolonged favorable blade loading, while at high tip-speed ratios the improvements involve more localized flow changes.
items.citation: Zihan Zhang, Anchi Li, Qimin Feng et al.. Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mammalian gonadal development: origins, specification and differentiation of ovary and testis cell lineages
items.summary: This review examines how mammalian gonads develop from a shared bipotential precursor structure into either testes or ovaries, drawing on mouse and human research. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how the adrenogonadal primordium gives rise to the gonadal primordium, and how progenitor cells derived from the coelomic epithelium generate the major somatic cell lineages, including supporting, steroidogenic, stromal, and supporting-like cells. A particular focus is placed on how these multipotent progenitors become progressively fate-restricted, with recent evidence highlighted for early lineage priming occurring within spatially organized domains of the coelomic epithelium. The review also explores the molecular pathways and cellular mechanisms that drive sex-specific differentiation of these lineages into the distinct architectures of testis and ovary. The authors identify remaining gaps in understanding how the bipotential gonad commits to one sexual fate and discuss the implications of these developmental processes for human health.
items.citation: Serge Nef, Maeva Guy, Marie-Christine Chaboissier. Mammalian gonadal development: origins, specification and differentiation of ovary and testis cell lineages. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic technologies to the detection of veterinary parasites, motivated by the inadequacy of conventional methods such as microscopy, serology, and culture techniques, which are hampered by low sensitivity, poor specificity, and dependence on specialized facilities. The authors systematically assess the principles and recent uses of CRISPR systems employing Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14 effectors for identifying protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites in livestock, companion animals, and wildlife. The review also evaluates how these platforms can be integrated with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to enhance diagnostic performance in field settings. Key challenges including sample preparation, assay standardization, multiplex detection, and regulatory and commercialization hurdles are discussed alongside future directions such as amplification-free assays and artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation. The authors argue that CRISPR-based diagnostics hold strong potential to transform veterinary parasite surveillance and support a One Health approach to disease control.
items.citation: Basit A, Hanif M. Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.. Molecular and biochemical parasitology. 2026

items.title: Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of high background signal (leakage) that limits the sensitivity and precision of amplification-free CRISPR-based nucleic acid detection. The researchers engineered the CRISPR RNA component of the Cas12a system by adding a DNA extension to the scaffold RNA's 3'-end, reshaping it into a conformational switch that uses steric hindrance to keep the system in an inhibited state until a target nucleic acid triggers precise activation. This allosteric regulation mechanism drives a cascade amplification strategy, termed CALCas, that suppresses spurious self-activation while still enabling large signal gains upon target recognition. The system achieved femtomolar detection sensitivity and was demonstrated for rapid detection of HPV16/18 within under thirty minutes. The approach establishes a framework for reprogramming Cas12a enzymatic activity to balance high sensitivity with a stable, low background signal suitable for quantitative nucleic acid diagnostics.
items.citation: Li X, Hu H, Jiang X et al.. Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines point-of-care testing as a diagnostic approach for infectious diseases, motivated by the growing global burden of such diseases and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the core technical platforms underpinning current point-of-care technologies, including lateral flow assays, chemiluminescence immunoassays, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and microfluidic chip systems, as well as their application across respiratory, bloodstream, gastrointestinal, urinary tract, and sexually transmitted infections. They assessed both immunochromatographic and molecular diagnostic modalities, weighing their technical characteristics against clinical utility. While acknowledging persistent limitations in detection sensitivity, quality control, cost, and clinical integration, the review concludes that advances in nanomaterials, microfluidic engineering, artificial intelligence, and industry standardization are driving improvements that position point-of-care testing to become a central tool in precision clinical management and public health infectious disease control.
items.citation: Fang Q, Lin Y, Hu G et al.. Point-of-care testing in the diagnosis of infectious diseases.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize current applications of genome-wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics alongside deep learning frameworks to analyze complex biological datasets underlying disease pathogenesis. They assess how this combined approach advances key stages of the drug development pipeline, including target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The review highlights disease-specific applications in oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions, while also acknowledging persistent challenges such as harmonizing heterogeneous omics data, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias. The authors argue that the convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence enables more precise therapeutic interventions and opens new avenues for data-driven translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance
items.summary: This paper investigated the relationship between cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of cell death reliant on FDX1-mediated protein lipoylation, and antitumor immune responses. The researchers found that CD8+ T cell-mediated immunity increases tumor cell susceptibility to cuproptosis, with cuproptosis inducers proving more effective in immunocompetent compared to immunodeficient hosts. Mechanistically, the interaction operates bidirectionally: cuproptotic tumor cells trigger immunogenic cell death by releasing damage-associated molecular patterns that activate dendritic cells, while CD8+ T cell-derived interferon-γ upregulates FDX1 transcription in tumor cells through the STAT1-IRF1 signaling axis, further sensitizing them to cuproptosis. Building on this crosstalk, the study demonstrated that combining a cuproptosis inducer with anti-PD-L1 therapy amplified tumor cell death and overcame resistance to checkpoint immunotherapy across multiple preclinical models. These findings establish a previously unrecognized link between cuproptosis and antitumor immunity and propose targeting this cell death pathway as a strategy to counteract immunotherapy resistance.
items.citation: Guang Lei, Zhengze Lu, Zhihao Xu et al.. Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance. Cell. 2026

items.title: Migration, Displacement, and Health Inequities: A Comparative Study of Refugee Populations and Access to Healthcare Services
items.summary: This paper examined healthcare inequities among refugee populations across different levels of healthcare access, with the stated aim of informing global health policy and humanitarian response. Rather than collecting any empirical data, the study constructed an entirely simulated framework using hypothetical refugee households distributed across four theoretical healthcare accessibility scenarios, from minimal access to comprehensive universal coverage. The researchers applied machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, to this synthetic dataset to predict healthcare utilization and identify determinants of equitable access. The simulated results suggest that comprehensive healthcare integration improves a wide range of health outcomes, including maternal health, childhood immunization, mental health services, and chronic disease management, while reducing overall inequities, with XGBoost performing best in identifying populations at risk of exclusion. The authors present this work explicitly as a methodological blueprint for future empirical investigation rather than a source of findings derived from real refugee populations or health records.
items.citation: Muhammad Riaz, Neelam Tariq, Madiha Iqbal et al.. Migration, Displacement, and Health Inequities: A Comparative Study of Refugee Populations and Access to Healthcare Services. Social science review archives.. 2026

items.title: Modulation of Gut Microbiota Through Functional Foods to Reduce Low-Grade Chronic Inflammation
items.summary: This paper examines the relationship between gut microbiota dysbiosis and chronic low-grade inflammation, which underlies conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, and cancer. The authors review how the gut microbial community regulates immune responses, nutrient metabolism, pathogen resistance, and intestinal barrier integrity, and how disruptions to this community contribute to inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction. The paper focuses on dietary interventions — specifically functional foods including probiotics, prebiotics, and bioactive compounds — as a means of restoring microbial balance by promoting beneficial bacteria and suppressing harmful microbial activity. The authors also highlight how advances in microbiome sequencing technologies have deepened understanding of host–microbe interactions, enabling more targeted nutritional strategies. Overall, the paper argues that modulating gut microbiota through functional foods represents a promising non-invasive approach to mitigating chronic inflammation and improving metabolic and immune health.
authors: Pakistan Journal of Medical & Cardiological Review
items.venue: Pakistan Journal of Medical & Cardiological Review

items.title: Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses
items.summary: This paper investigated how hedgehog merbecoviruses — relatives of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus circulating in hedgehogs across Europe and Asia — enter host cells, a question relevant to assessing their zoonotic potential. Using cell-based assays, pseudotype experiments with a vesicular stomatitis virus reporter system, and protein binding assays, the researchers tested candidate receptors from the European hedgehog and identified aminopeptidase N as the functional entry receptor for these viruses. They found that viral spike protein infectivity was enhanced at temperatures matching hedgehog physiology rather than human body temperature, and a broad screen of mammalian aminopeptidase N orthologues revealed restricted cross-species receptor usage, with human aminopeptidase N unable to support infection. Electron cryomicroscopy further showed that the hedgehog coronavirus spike-receptor interface is structurally distinct from other known coronavirus spike–aminopeptidase N interactions, helping explain species barriers. These results expand understanding of receptor diversity across merbecoviruses and betacoronaviruses while providing a basis for evaluating the risk of these viruses spilling over into humans or domestic animals.
items.citation: Min Jin, Victoria A. Jefferson, Zhe Zhao et al.. Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses. Nature Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Ohmic warm inflation
items.summary: The paper examines Warm Little Inflation, a previously proposed warm inflation framework, and identifies fundamental problems with it: it is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and fails to sustain the required thermal bath because the quasi-static approximation overestimated the dissipated power. To resolve these issues, the authors construct new anomaly-free models based on a fermion charged under a gauge group in one extra dimension, with a four-dimensional lattice formulation consisting of a ring of gauge groups with fermions at each site. The inflaton is identified with a Wilson line, which is protected against corrections for sufficiently large numbers of sites, and a monodromy potential becomes viable in the large-site limit. In the continuum limit, the inflaton velocity maps onto a five-dimensional electric field and the resulting friction mechanism becomes Ohmic dissipation, which the authors argue can sustain warm inflation in a manner consistent with observations.
items.citation: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia. Ohmic warm inflation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
items.summary: This paper studies linear regression in the heavy-tailed noise regime where the regression errors possess only a finite conditional moment of order strictly between one and two, and where the covariates themselves may have only limited moment assumptions. The authors develop a black-box reduction called empirical residual pruning that transforms any finite-variance linear regression procedure into one capable of handling this infinite-variance setting, without requiring knowledge of the moment exponent, noise scale, or covariance structure. The resulting estimator achieves a high-probability error bound that degrades gracefully as the moment order approaches one, recovering near-standard rates when the moment order approaches two. The authors prove a matching minimax lower bound under the same conditions, establishing that the reduction is optimal, and they extend the approach to distribution-free prediction guarantees and to mean estimation in analogous heavy-tailed settings. The reduction preserves computational efficiency from the underlying finite-variance subroutine, making it practically applicable whenever a computationally efficient finite-variance method is available.
items.citation: Artin Tajdini, Jasper C. H. Lee, Jonathan Scarlett et al.. Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
items.summary: This paper investigates how thermopower behaves in two-dimensional Fermi liquids as a function of wave vector, focusing on a phenomenon the authors call the thermal dressing of Fermi-surface deformations. Rather than characterizing transport solely through conventional relaxation times, the authors introduce the concept of thermal dressing—the local temperature change associated with deformations of the Fermi surface—and show that this structure governs the thermoelectric response. They find that the thermopower overshoots its expected hydrodynamic value with increasing wave vector before falling to half that value in the ballistic limit, with the overshoot driven by collinear scattering that redistributes energy across the Fermi surface. Notably, the excess thermopower at low temperatures does not follow the linear-in-temperature scaling characteristic of Fermi liquids, instead decaying only logarithmically with temperature at optimal wave vector. This thermographic transport regime is distinct from analogous tomographic effects in charge conductivity and is predicted to survive realistic disorder, making it experimentally accessible in thermocouple setups using high-mobility samples.
items.citation: Johannes Hofmann. Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
items.summary: This paper investigates the properties of one of the earliest stellar populations in the Universe by searching for evidence of Population III stars, the hypothesized first generation of stars formed from nearly metal-free primordial gas. Using deep spectroscopy from the James Webb Space Telescope, the researchers studied a strongly gravitationally lensed galaxy observed approximately one billion years after the Big Bang. They detected helium and hydrogen emission lines at high significance, along with extremely low oxygen abundance measured at a tiny fraction of the solar value, indicating an almost chemically pristine interstellar medium. The ratios of helium to hydrogen emission are consistent with theoretical predictions for the hard ionizing radiation fields expected from very massive, metal-poor Population III stars, though the authors acknowledge that accreting black holes cannot be entirely ruled out as an alternative explanation. The findings demonstrate that pockets of near-pristine gas, the birthplaces predicted for the Universe's first stars, still existed a billion years after the Big Bang and were being dominated by very massive stars.
items.citation: Takahiro Morishita, Massimo Stiavelli, Tommaso Treu et al.. Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang. arXiv. 2026

items.title: No Polynomial-Time Algorithm For Tarski Fixed Points Unless Cryptographic Assumptions Fail
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational hardness of finding a Tarski fixed point, a fundamental problem in lattice theory with connections to equilibrium computation. The authors construct a subexponential-time reduction from the Unique End of Potential Line problem to the Tarski fixed point problem, linking the difficulty of the latter to established cryptographic assumptions. By applying known cryptographic lower bounds for the source problem, they derive conditional lower bounds — most notably quasi-polynomial-time lower bounds — on any algorithm that finds a Tarski fixed point. These lower bounds are shown to match recently established quasi-polynomial query complexity lower bounds for the problem, suggesting that existing algorithmic approaches are essentially optimal under standard cryptographic assumptions.
items.citation: Eleni Batziou, John Fearnley, Alexandros Hollender et al.. No Polynomial-Time Algorithm For Tarski Fixed Points Unless Cryptographic Assumptions Fail. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
items.summary: This paper investigates sheaves of meromorphic functions satisfying Hölder continuity conditions on complex analytic varieties, parametrized by an exponent between zero and one with respect to the outer metric. The authors prove these sheaves are coherent, that only finitely many distinct ones exist with rational transition exponents determined by Rees valuations, and that each exponent defines a corresponding Hölder saturation sitting between the seminormalization and the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. For reduced curve germs, the Hölder saturations are computed explicitly from characteristic exponents of branches and classical invariants, and it is shown that homeomorphic curves are bi-Hölder homeomorphic for some positive exponent while bi-Hölder maps with exponent sufficiently close to one preserve multiplicity. The paper further introduces a relative version of this construction for families of varieties and establishes two notions of equisingularity — Hölder equisingularity and the stronger Hölder equisaturation — proving for families of reduced curve germs that these interpolate between topological, Whitney, and Lipschitz equisingularity with explicit exponent thresholds depending only on invariants of the special fiber.
items.citation: François Bernard, Antoni Rangachev. Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
items.summary: This paper presents a nucleic acid detection platform called TIMBER (templated incision mediated by endonucleases of repair) designed to overcome limitations of existing CRISPR-based diagnostic systems, particularly for multiplexed detection. Rather than relying on collateral nuclease activity as CRISPR diagnostics do, TIMBER exploits repair endonucleases that cleave abasic-site-containing probes only when hybridized to a matched target sequence, conferring high specificity including single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination. The system achieves sensitive detection both with and without preamplification, and results can be read by visual fluorescence or lateral flow, making it compatible with point-of-care deployment. The platform was validated on clinical saliva samples for SARS-CoV-2 detection and demonstrated simultaneous detection of four distinct targets, including identification of cancer-relevant EGFR mutations in lung cancer samples. The authors argue that TIMBER offers a flexible, instrument-light alternative to CRISPR diagnostics suitable for infectious disease surveillance and precision oncology applications.
items.citation: Garden PM, Li Y, Murugan V et al.. Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.. ACS sensors. 2026
