items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examines a central question in exercise immunology: whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper contrasts evidence suggesting that moderate, short-duration exercise benefits immune defense—particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease—against observations that high-performance athletes experience elevated infection burdens during intense training periods. Opposing groups debated whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, travel, and psychological stress, and whether commonly used biomarkers and in vitro data reliably reflect immune health under arduous exercise conditions. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but could not resolve whether exercise itself is a direct cause of increased infection risk in athletes. The authors conclude that the question remains open and call for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific contribution of exercise from the many co-occurring stressors unique to high-performance athletic and military populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. Exercise immunology review. 2026

items.title: The Dual Role of Interleukin-6 in the Pathophysiology of Skeletal Muscle: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Therapeutic Prospects
items.summary: This review examines the dual and context-dependent roles of interleukin-6 in skeletal muscle physiology and pathology. Under healthy conditions, particularly during exercise, contracting muscle cells release this cytokine as a myokine that regulates energy metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and muscle regeneration through autocrine, paracrine, and endocrine mechanisms. In contrast, chronically elevated levels seen in conditions such as cancer cachexia, sepsis, muscular dystrophy, and disuse atrophy drive muscle wasting, metabolic dysfunction, and functional decline. The review systematically analyzes the downstream signaling cascades involved, distinguishes between classical and trans-signaling modes, and highlights regulatory upstream mechanisms including mechanosensitive channels and mitochondrial function. It further identifies key research challenges and evaluates therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway, including monoclonal antibodies, kinase inhibitors, and lifestyle-based interventions, to inform future translational and clinical applications.
items.citation: Yingyu Wang, J Zhang, Jie Wang et al.. The Dual Role of Interleukin-6 in the Pathophysiology of Skeletal Muscle: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Therapeutic Prospects. Pharmaceuticals. 2026

items.title: Neurokinin-1 receptor antagonism as a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment; enhancing anti-tumor efficacy while mitigating treatment-related toxicities
items.summary: The paper reviewed the role of the Substance P/neurokinin-1 receptor signaling pathway in cancer biology, examining its contributions to tumor progression across multiple cancer types including pancreatic, breast, glioblastoma, and lung malignancies. The authors analyzed how this pathway drives key oncogenic processes such as metastasis, angiogenesis, cellular proliferation, treatment resistance, and evasion of apoptosis. A central focus was placed on aprepitant, an already-approved antiemetic drug that acts as a neurokinin-1 receptor antagonist, which was found to demonstrate promising anticancer properties in addition to its established clinical use. The review concludes that targeting this receptor pathway could serve a dual therapeutic purpose: enhancing the efficacy of existing cancer treatments while simultaneously reducing the toxicities associated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy, making it a compelling candidate for incorporation into combination therapy regimens.
items.citation: Anirban Maitra, Miguel Muñoz, Rafael Coveñas et al.. Neurokinin-1 receptor antagonism as a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment; enhancing anti-tumor efficacy while mitigating treatment-related toxicities. npj Precision Oncology. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review paper examined how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with particular focus on the immune response to exercise. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search to gather all relevant existing research on exercise immunology in individuals with spinal cord injury across patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations, grounding the discussion in the anatomical and physiological foundations of neuroimmune regulation. Spinal cord injury was found to impair immunity through multiple pathways, including reductions in lymphocyte numbers, loss of autonomic function, and altered catecholamine concentrations, with individuals with tetraplegia being especially affected due to greater disruption of adrenergic signaling to lymphoid cells. However, some immune responses to exercise, such as increases in natural killer cell cytotoxicity and mucosal immune responses, appeared to occur independently of catecholamine changes or were comparable to those seen in able-bodied individuals, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms such as sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, or neuroendocrine adjustments may partially offset injury-related immune deficits. The authors concluded that exercise and rehabilitation hold promise as tools to maintain or improve immune and autonomic function in this population, while calling for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria Louise Goosey-Tolfrey, NICOLETTE CLAIRE BISHOP. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. Exercise immunology review. 2026

items.title: Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape
items.summary: The paper investigated the evolutionary dynamics of affinity maturation in germinal centers, where B cells undergo iterative mutation and selection to produce increasingly effective antibodies. To study this, the researchers developed an experimental evolution model in which over one hundred monoclonal germinal center reactions were replayed, using deep mutational scanning to assign affinities to individual cells and map the underlying affinity landscape. Their findings show that germinal centers achieve predictable evolutionary outcomes despite noisy selection, with the exploration of the affinity landscape being heavily shaped by biases in somatic hypermutation. By inferring a quantitative fitness landscape, the authors were able to recapitulate the affinity maturation trajectory of their clone. Notably, they argue that commonly observed features of germinal center selection—such as apparent tolerance for low-affinity B cell lineages and rapid plateauing of antibody affinity—are artifacts of survivorship bias rather than true properties of the selection process.
items.citation: William S. DeWitt, Ashni A. Vora, Tatsuya Araki et al.. Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape. Cell. 2026

items.title: EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation
items.summary: These guidelines address the clinical management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and, for the first time explicitly, Richter transformation, representing an updated framework developed under the European Hematology Association rather than its previous sponsor. The guidelines adopt a holistic approach spanning initial diagnosis and active surveillance through treatment decisions, emphasizing the interplay between disease-specific and patient-specific factors in clinical decision-making. A notable procedural innovation is the inclusion of patient advocacy representatives alongside medical experts from multiple European countries in the consensus process. Updated treatment recommendations incorporate a recently approved time-limited combination regimen for first-line therapy as well as a continuous therapy option for patients with relapsed or refractory disease who have been previously exposed to covalent Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The guidelines are intended to be published annually to remain current with the rapidly evolving landscape of research and clinical applications in this field.
items.citation: Barbara F. Eichhorst, Paolo Ghia, Francesc Bosch et al.. EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation. HemaSphere. 2026

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.summary: This paper investigates whether neutrino disappearance channels can exhibit sensitivity to T-violation, challenging the widely held claim in the literature that T-violation vanishes in such channels. The authors demonstrate that this claim holds only under restricted conditions — specifically, symmetric matter profiles or when the CP-violating phase is zero or π — and that the muon and tau neutrino survival probabilities carry a genuine sine-of-delta-dependent T-asymmetry in asymmetric matter. They identify that the conventional null result arises from an improperly constructed T test that amounts to a mathematical identity rather than a physical measurement, and they carefully distinguish proper from improper T, CP, and CPT tests for general matter profiles. Using a two-layer constant-density toy model, they find that T-violation is maximized when one layer is near the solar resonance and the other near the atmospheric resonance. The paper further evaluates whether the matter asymmetry encountered by existing and planned long-baseline experiments is large enough to make this effect experimentally accessible in muon neutrino survival probability, and discusses future scenarios that could probe such T and CP violation in disappearance channels.
items.citation: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas. Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
items.summary: This paper investigates a previously unknown side-channel attack that exploits Android's Camera2 subsystem to perform acoustic eavesdropping without requiring microphone permissions. The researchers discovered that Camera2's hardware abstraction layer captures high-rate gyroscope measurements through image stabilization pipelines and exports them as vendor metadata, entirely bypassing Android's privacy protections—including microphone and camera toggles—and circumventing the sampling-rate caps imposed on direct sensor access. Testing across a large set of smartphones from multiple vendors, they found that a substantial proportion expose this gyroscope metadata channel at rates exceeding normal limits, with several flagship devices streaming data at nearly double the permitted ceiling even when privacy switches are engaged. To exploit this channel without requiring device-specific calibration data, the authors developed Source-to-Leakage Learning, a physics-constrained simulation framework that trains a universal speech recognizer on synthetic sensor traces rather than real recordings from target devices, thereby decoupling speech content from device-specific mechanical resonances. Their resulting system, CamEar, substantially outperforms prior approaches on unseen devices and achieves meaningful word and character recognition accuracy across the highest-rate phones, demonstrating that the attack generalizes effectively without any target-device profiling.
items.citation: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang. Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of hyperparameter optimization on large datasets by proposing a ranking-preserving coreset selection framework. The approach constructs a compact data subset that faithfully reproduces the relative performance ranking of hyperparameter configurations seen on the full training data, formulating coreset selection itself as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes rank correlation while minimizing subset size. The resulting coreset is then used to accelerate three evolutionary hyperparameter optimization algorithms across a range of tabular, text, and image classification benchmarks. Experiments demonstrate substantial reductions in optimization time with test accuracy comparable to full-dataset tuning, and the coreset's ranking fidelity generalizes to held-out configurations not used during its construction. The one-time cost of building the coreset can be recovered through amortization when it is reused across multiple optimization runs.
items.citation: Mamoona Tasadduq, Maryam Bashir. Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: This paper investigates how propulsion-load changes propagate through the interconnected nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical systems of a small modular reactor-powered all-electric ship, and how battery energy storage can mitigate the resulting transients. The researchers developed an integrated dynamic model coupling a pressurized water reactor, a moving-boundary steam generator, a turbine, a synchronous generator, a shipboard alternating-current electrical network, an asynchronous propulsion motor, and a grid-connected battery storage system. A sudden reduction in propulsion motor load was applied, and the transient responses of the reactor-alone and reactor-plus-battery configurations were compared. Without battery support, the mismatch between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand produced a large over-frequency excursion, while adding the battery substantially suppressed this frequency spike and also smoothed upstream responses including steam flow, reactor coolant temperature, reactivity, and thermal power. The findings underscore the necessity of treating nuclear-powered electric ships as tightly coupled multi-domain systems and demonstrate that battery energy storage meaningfully improves short-term load-following behavior.
items.citation: Ali Mahboub Rad, Jie Zhang. Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
items.summary: The paper investigated whether the properties of buoyancy glitches in low-luminosity red giants — specifically their amplitude, location, and width — can be recovered from global stellar properties without requiring dedicated seismic modelling. The authors trained gradient-boosted tree regressors on a large grid of synthetic stellar models, using global parameters such as the frequency of maximum oscillation power and effective temperature as inputs. They found that the glitch location and width are recovered with very high accuracy, while the glitch amplitude proves more difficult to recover, particularly in a specific range of large frequency separations where the glitch sits near a structurally complex transition zone. SHAP analysis revealed that the machine learning models rely primarily on evolutionary state indicators, suggesting that the glitch location and width are tightly governed by global evolutionary trends, whereas the amplitude reflects more localized structural complexity. The authors conclude that global stellar properties can provide direct estimates of buoyancy-glitch parameters, offering a practical way to prioritize targets for more intensive mixed-mode inversions in large asteroseismic surveys.
items.citation: Jiang Chen. Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
items.summary: This study investigated how sinusoidal blade pitching amplitude and phase affect both power extraction and the energy exchanged through the pitching motion in vertical-axis turbines, with the goal of understanding whether blades could sustain such motions passively. Experiments were conducted using a single-blade model traversing a circular path in a water channel across a range of tip-speed ratios, systematically testing a large number of prescribed pitch conditions. The researchers found that the optimal pitching amplitude decreases and the optimal phase shifts as tip-speed ratio increases, and that sinusoidal pitching can substantially improve power output compared to fixed-pitch operation across all tested conditions. Analysis of pitching-energy exchange revealed that the best-performing motions at lower tip-speed ratios involve nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work, while at higher tip-speed ratios the flow actually transfers net energy into the pitching motion, suggesting passive pitching may be energetically feasible in those regimes. Flow visualization and force measurements revealed that performance gains at low tip-speed ratio stem from delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and prolonged favorable loading, while at high tip-speed ratio the improvements are more localized, and the combined performance and energy maps provide candidate motions for future passive or assisted pitching device development.
items.citation: Zihan Zhang, Anchi Li, Qimin Feng et al.. Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation.
items.summary: This review examined the potential of microRNAs as host-response biomarkers for diagnosing emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases, focusing on the gap between biomarker discovery and clinical deployment. The authors evaluated miRNA diagnostic and translational potential across a range of viral and parasitic diseases including malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Japanese encephalitis, and Nipah virus disease. Rather than focusing solely on biomarker discovery or detection technology, the review took a cross-disease perspective that connected miRNA signatures to analytical and clinical validation, point-of-care platform development, economic considerations, and deployment in resource-limited settings. The authors conclude that the field has been hampered by a lack of reproducible multi-miRNA signatures, unstandardized pre-analytical workflows, and insufficient prospective multicentre validation. They argue that future progress requires integrating validated signatures into affordable, sample-to-answer diagnostic platforms and demonstrating measurable improvements in clinical decision-making under real-world conditions.
items.citation: Cappleman V, Gupta H. MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation.. Expert review of molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Sample-to-answer automated centrifugal microfluidics with computer-vision readout for point-of-care molecular diagnostics
items.summary: The paper addressed the need for decentralized, automated molecular diagnostic tools capable of operating at the point of care, particularly in resource-limited settings exposed as vulnerable during the COVID-19 pandemic. The researchers developed a fully automated centrifugal microfluidic platform that integrates loop-mediated isothermal amplification with computer-vision-based optical readout, performing the entire assay from sample to answer with a single button press and no user intervention. The system was demonstrated using SARS-CoV-2 detection, processing multiple samples simultaneously in under an hour. Testing with RNA fragments spiked into water and artificial saliva showed reliable detection down to a low copy number per reaction. The authors propose that this platform architecture is broadly applicable to other infectious diseases and could serve as a template for rapid, decentralized diagnostics in future outbreaks.
items.citation: Akhtar AS, Lapins N, Moura JM et al.. Sample-to-answer automated centrifugal microfluidics with computer-vision readout for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Enabling Ciprofloxacin Resistance-Guided Therapy for Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Aligning Diagnostics, Regulation, Guidelines, and Reimbursement.
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of moving away from empirical ceftriaxone treatment for gonorrhea toward individualized, resistance-guided therapy using ciprofloxacin, an oral antibiotic that is effective against susceptible strains. Because ciprofloxacin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae is predominantly caused by a single mutation in the gyrA gene, molecular diagnostics targeting this site can reliably predict whether ciprofloxacin will be effective for a given infection. A multicenter study is underway to generate regulatory-grade clinical performance data supporting submissions of multiple nucleic acid amplification tests to the Food and Drug Administration for this purpose. A multidisciplinary meeting was convened to map out a coordinated pathway that integrates diagnostic development, regulatory approval, clinical guideline updates, reimbursement policy, and implementation strategy. The paper presents highlights from that meeting, underscoring that enabling resistance-guided gonorrhea therapy in the United States will require simultaneous progress across all of these interconnected domains.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Trainor BW, Osborn JL, Klausner JD et al.. Enabling Ciprofloxacin Resistance-Guided Therapy for Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Aligning Diagnostics, Regulation, Guidelines, and Reimbursement.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the current state and future potential of saliva as a diagnostic biofluid across a broad range of clinical applications. The authors synthesized evidence on salivary biomarkers spanning glycemic control, cardiovascular risk, sepsis surveillance, endocrinology, infectious diseases, cancer liquid biopsy, and neurodegenerative disorders, while also evaluating the analytical technologies used to detect them, from immunoassays and mass spectrometry to wearable electrochemical biosensors. The review distinguished between diagnostics that have already received regulatory clearance and those still in discovery phases. Despite the clear advantages of saliva as a noninvasive alternative to blood collection, the authors found that widespread clinical adoption is impeded by unstandardized collection protocols, oral matrix interference, and absent normative reference intervals. They conclude that translation into mainstream diagnostics will require universal sampling standardization, matrix-matched biosensor engineering capable of sub-picomolar detection, and large multicenter prospective trials to establish clinical cutoffs and validate blood-saliva correlation kinetics.
items.citation: Mondal S, Das Sharma A, Mandal SK et al.. Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.. Expert review of molecular diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
items.summary: This paper investigated how well frontier language models can perform sequential diagnosis, a process that mirrors the iterative, stepwise reasoning clinicians use in real-world practice. The researchers built an interactive benchmark and an AI system designed to simulate a panel of physicians, which progressively refines a differential diagnosis while selecting cost-effective diagnostic tests based on an initial brief clinical presentation. The system was evaluated on two datasets drawn from published clinical case conferences and real emergency department admissions. The AI system substantially outperformed generalist physicians on diagnostic accuracy across both datasets, while the study also assessed the cost of the diagnostic workup. The authors conclude that, despite being tested in a controlled benchmark environment, these results suggest language models hold considerable promise for improving diagnostic accuracy and reducing costs in clinical settings.
items.citation: Harsha Nori, Mayank Daswani, Christopher J. Kelly et al.. Sequential diagnosis with language models. Science. 2026

items.title: Altered immune response to exercise in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis: A systematic literature review
items.summary: This paper systematically reviewed the scientific literature on how the immune system of patients with Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis responds to physical exercise compared to healthy sedentary controls. The researchers searched major databases and identified case-control studies meeting their criteria, then evaluated them for methodological quality. They found that CFS patients exhibit a more pronounced activation of the complement system, heightened oxidative stress with a delayed and reduced antioxidant response, and altered immune cell gene expression patterns following exercise, though no differences were observed in circulating pro- or anti-inflammatory cytokines. Many of these immune abnormalities were associated with post-exertional malaise, a hallmark symptom of the condition. Overall, the review concluded that there is moderate-level evidence supporting an altered immune response to exercise in CFS patients.
items.citation: Jo Nijs, Aandrea Nees, Lorna Paul et al.. Altered immune response to exercise in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis: A systematic literature review. Exercise immunology review. 2026

items.title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents
items.summary: The paper studied whether an autonomous artificial intelligence agent could manage patient cases within an electronic health record environment at a level comparable to physicians. The researchers developed MIRA, an agent operating in a sandboxed electronic health record that can gather patient histories, order and interpret diagnostic tests, generate differential diagnoses, and formulate treatment plans including prescriptions and surgical scheduling. When tested on simulations based on real patient cases covering multiple diagnoses, MIRA outperformed physicians in diagnostic accuracy and made decisions that were guideline-concordant, medication-safe, and appropriate regarding hospital admissions. Unlike prior large language model applications that addressed isolated clinical subtasks or provided unstructured advice, MIRA translates clinical intent into structured, actionable electronic health record operations, suggesting it could serve as a more effective decision-support tool. The authors note that prospective real-world studies are still needed to establish the system's generalizability, safety, and governance.
items.citation: Dyke Ferber, Lars Hilgers, Christiane Höper et al.. Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents. Nature. 2026

items.title: Inherent Bias in Electronic Health Records: A Scoping Review of Sources of Bias
items.summary: This scoping review examined the sources of bias inherent in Electronic Health Records, which are increasingly used to train medical artificial intelligence models, with the goal of understanding how such biases may exacerbate health inequities. The authors conducted a systematic literature search following the PRISMA approach, ultimately analyzing over one hundred peer-reviewed studies published across a seven-year period. From this synthesis, they proposed a taxonomy identifying six primary categories of bias in EHR data, encompassing bias from past clinical trials, data-related issues such as missing information, implicit clinician bias, referral and admission bias, diagnosis or risk disparity bias, and biases embedded in devices and algorithms. The review found that existing research disproportionately focuses on data-related and racial biases while other dimensions—such as gender bias, sexual orientation discrimination, and unconscious cognitive biases among clinicians—remain underexplored and poorly documented. The authors conclude that these diverse bias sources can compound one another to amplify healthcare disparities, and they call for a "bias-in-mind" approach in developing and deploying data-driven healthcare solutions, alongside greater empirical investigation into how specific biases affect clinical outcomes.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology
items.citation: Oriel Perets, Emanuela Stagno, Eyal Ben Yehuda et al.. Inherent Bias in Electronic Health Records: A Scoping Review of Sources of Bias. ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology. 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper examined whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning in large language models. The authors developed MedicalAgentsBench, a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from eight medical datasets using difficulty-aware filtering and contamination screening. They evaluated a broad range of models including internalized reasoning models, base language models, and agent-based frameworks that decompose problems across multiple collaborating models. Their findings show that internalized and externalized approaches independently improve performance and that their benefits are additive, with the highest accuracy achieved by combining an internalized reasoning model with an agent workflow. A cost-performance analysis further demonstrated that this hybrid combination dominates the efficiency frontier, while lightweight optimization on less expensive models provides a viable option for resource-limited deployment.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of classifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents using electroencephalography signals recorded during cognitive tasks. The researchers curated a large collection of existing recordings from over a hundred participants across multiple task conditions, linking continuous brain signals to precomputed measurements spanning seven distinct feature families derived from more than a hundred feature definitions. A key contribution was ensuring consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows, and documented quality decisions so that different EEG features could be compared on equal footing within the same dataset. Technical validation confirmed high data retention after preprocessing, and illustrative machine learning evaluations using gradient boosting demonstrated that classification performance varied across task conditions, with one task showing stronger group discrimination than others. The authors emphasize that these descriptive findings do not establish diagnostic validity, but the publicly released dataset and curation software are intended to support reproducible and comparable future research in this area.
items.citation: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.. On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease
items.summary: This paper investigated why red blood cells in Gaucher disease adhere abnormally to vessel walls, asking whether the known elevation in Lutheran/basal cell adhesion molecule receptor abundance alone can explain the increased adhesion. The researchers built a computational model simulating stochastic receptor-ligand bond formation, calibrated it using control donor data, and then tested whether the modest increase in total receptor count predicted by experiments could account for observed adhesion on laminin and endothelium. The model substantially underpredicted actual adhesion, and closing the gap required assuming a much larger increase in binding-competent receptors, consistent with estimated rises in phosphorylated, functionally active receptor fractions. The study further demonstrated that membrane stiffening or increased bond affinity could not resolve the discrepancy at high shear stress, and that in sickle cell disease the model accurately tracked adhesion changes under hydroxyurea when active rather than total receptor counts were used. The authors conclude that receptor activation state, rather than overall receptor abundance, is the principal determinant of red blood cell adhesion in these diseases, while membrane stiffening appears more relevant to splenic retention.
items.citation: Zhaojie Chai, Pierre A. Buffet, Melanie Franco et al.. Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: This paper addresses a limitation in standard segmentation evaluation metrics when reference annotations contain biased or heuristically-derived instances that may incorrectly split or merge objects. The authors identify that existing metrics like Panoptic Quality treat all instances equally and cannot distinguish between valid segmentation errors and artifacts introduced by biased reference annotations, such as merged touching objects or fragmented instances. To address this, they developed Star Panoptic Quality, a novel evaluation framework that constructs a star forest from the bipartite matching graph between predicted and reference instances, isolating distinct failure modes into clean, merge, and split categories. The framework then computes a final metric by allowing practitioners to independently weight each failure mode, enabling selective penalization or leniency depending on the known biases in the reference annotations. Through multiple experiments, the authors demonstrate that their approach both enables nuanced control over how different segmentation errors are penalized and serves as a diagnostic tool for revealing the prevalence of specific failure modes in a dataset.
items.citation: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.. Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary: This paper presents the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, an industrial architecture designed to automate and scale user experience evaluation in large-scale web search, addressing limitations of traditional surveys and coarse automated metrics. The framework consists of two tiers: a macro-level system using a fine-tuned encoder-decoder language model on telemetry features to detect user sentiment regressions across experiments, and a micro-level system employing a multimodal large language model to visually assess web result page layouts and quantify the effort users must expend to find satisfactory results. The macro tier uses multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering to improve precision and dramatically reduce measurement latency from weeks to hours while cutting survey overhead, whereas the micro tier leverages reinforcement learning-based prompt optimization and an AI judge to improve diagnostic accuracy of visual and spatial layout friction. Together, the two tiers achieve meaningful gains in precision-adjusted detection performance and F1 score respectively, while enabling daily processing of live experiment queries at scale. The framework ultimately provides both scalable regression detection and granular, visually-grounded diagnostics for UX attribution in production search systems.
items.citation: Yi Ding, Gaurav Kumar, Rui Min et al.. The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability
items.summary: This paper investigated how arachidonic acid metabolites influence the dynamics of nervous tissue activity, particularly in the context of cortical spreading depression. The researchers developed a mathematical model of a spatially distributed system of interconnected neurogliovascular units to examine how vasoconstrictor and vasodilator effects of arachidonic acid metabolites shape neural activity patterns. By simulating the influence of these metabolites on the neurogliovascular unit, the study analyzed how astrocytic activity affects the spatiotemporal characteristics of propagating cortical depression waves. The findings suggest that arachidonic acid can control the stability of this system, with implications for understanding pathological conditions such as epilepsy, migraines, and neurodegenerative diseases associated with cortical spreading depression.

items.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate how well vision-language models can interpret electronic navigational charts, which encode safety-critical maritime information through complex symbols, geometries, and standardized notation. The authors constructed a large question-answering dataset derived from thousands of official nautical charts, organizing questions around four capability dimensions: perception of nautical features, spatial reasoning, combined perception and spatial reasoning, and practical application to assessing chart changes. A progressive subset of questions traces a chain from detecting changes between chart versions through to evaluating the navigational significance of those changes, enabling fine-grained diagnosis of model reasoning. Evaluation of multiple open-weight vision-language models revealed substantial weaknesses in recognizing fine-grained nautical features and in performing spatially grounded reasoning, though providing relevant perceptual and spatial context as evidence did improve performance on change-criticality judgments. The benchmark is presented as a diagnostic resource for understanding model limitations in safety-critical nautical chart interpretation tasks.
items.citation: Jiyoon Pyo, Jacob Arndt, Yao-Yi Chiang et al.. ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts. arXiv. 2026

items.title: WHO target product profiles for dengue therapeutics: an interdisciplinary analysis of ethical, regulatory, and implementation considerations.
items.summary: This paper examined the ethical, regulatory, and implementation challenges surrounding the development of therapeutic treatments for dengue, a mosquito-borne viral disease currently experiencing its largest recorded surge. The authors focused particularly on populations at heightened risk of severe disease, including those with multimorbidity and immunosuppression, who cannot benefit from existing live-attenuated vaccines. Through an interdisciplinary analysis, the researchers identified gaps in how at-risk groups are characterised and included in research, and evaluated barriers that impede equitable access to treatments, such as the absence of rapid diagnostics. Their findings call for enhanced surveillance, co-produced research approaches that meaningfully involve vulnerable populations, and targeted strategies to overcome socioeconomic barriers to access. The authors propose that this framework for equitable development and delivery of dengue countermeasures could serve as a model for responding to other infectious disease threats to global health.
items.citation: Johnson T, Loganathan S, Jamrozik E et al.. WHO target product profiles for dengue therapeutics: an interdisciplinary analysis of ethical, regulatory, and implementation considerations.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

These findings push back the timeline for crustal recycling and deep burial processes on Earth significantly.

items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals a systematic disparity in how credit is formally assigned in research, with a researcher's gender playing a role in determining whether their contributions earn full authorship or are relegated to mere acknowledgement.
items.citation: Anna Napolitano. Author or just ‘acknowledged’? How women are not gaining full credit for research. Nature. 2026

items.title: Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because engineered microbes could reduce agriculture's dependence on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers by supplying crops with nitrogen directly. The approach offers a potentially more sustainable path to feeding staple crops without the environmental costs associated with conventional fertilizers.
items.citation: James Dinneen, Mariana Lenharo. Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers. Nature. 2026

items.title: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method
items.summary: The paper studied whether a recently proposed diagnostic framework for obesity performs better than conventional body-mass-index-based criteria. The new framework incorporates waist circumference and related measures, and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity based on evidence of obesity-induced organ dysfunction. Using a large international multi-cohort study of adults, the researchers compared the two approaches for diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk. They found that combining body measurements with organ-function metrics outperformed body mass index alone in both classifying obesity and predicting mortality.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because a newer obesity diagnostic framework—which incorporates waist circumference and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity based on organ dysfunction—was shown in a large international multi-cohort study to outperform the long-standing body-mass-index-based approach in both diagnosing obesity and predicting mortality risk.
items.citation: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method. Nature. 2026

items.title: Personal incentives for public officials drove a drop in China’s fertility
items.why_notable: The work draws attention by revealing that China's fertility decline under the one-child policy was driven not simply by the policy itself, but by bureaucrats' personal career incentives tied to meeting birth targets. This raises the provocative question of whether a state that harnessed self-interest to suppress fertility can now reverse that entrenched dynamic to boost it.
items.citation: Jia Joya Yu. Personal incentives for public officials drove a drop in China’s fertility. Nature. 2026

items.title: Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize meaningfully, as it provides no specific research methods, findings, or claims beyond a general framing of the topic.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it addresses whether green technologies can offer a viable path to energy security at a time when political instability is placing exceptional stress on global energy markets. Researchers are actively seeking solutions to this urgent intersection of clean energy transition and geopolitical vulnerability.
items.citation: Nic Fleming. Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?. Nature. 2026

items.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
items.summary: This paper investigated how stalled DNA replication forks are restarted in human cells, focusing on the role of the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL during replication stress. Using purified human proteins to biochemically reconstitute fork stalling and restart, the researchers examined how PRIMPOL activity is coordinated by the replisome machinery. They discovered that the CMG helicase directly binds PRIMPOL and directs its activity specifically toward the leading strand, a finding supported by a cryo-electron microscopy structure showing the molecular basis of this interaction. Contrary to prior assumptions, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A was not required for fork restart in this reconstituted system. Disrupting the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction eliminated fork restart in vitro and impaired DNA damage tolerance in human cells, establishing PRIMPOL as a dedicated, integral component of the human replisome rather than an accessory factor recruited independently.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals a previously uncharacterized direct interaction between the core replication machinery and a specialized primase, explaining at a structural and biochemical level how cells restart stalled replication forks and prevent potentially dangerous gaps in newly synthesized DNA.
items.citation: Cristian Polo Rivera, Johann J. Roske, Emma Langdale Hands et al.. Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart. Nature. 2026

items.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
items.summary: The paper examined why China's fertility decline was delayed after the one-child policy was introduced, focusing on how bureaucratic enforcement mechanisms shaped policy effectiveness. The researchers investigated the role of the "one vote veto" policy, which barred local officials from career advancement if they failed to meet birth control targets, using provincial variation in when this stricter enforcement was implemented. They found that this strengthening of bureaucratic incentives was instrumental in driving the sharp fertility decline observed in the early 1990s, accounting for nearly half of the total fertility rate decline during that decade and pushing fertility below replacement level. Increased official promotion of intrauterine devices as a contraceptive method was identified as a particularly important pathway through which the policy operated. The findings challenge earlier research suggesting population policies have limited demographic impact, arguing instead that stringent enforcement mechanisms can make such policies substantially more effective.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention by revealing that bureaucratic incentive structures — rather than the one-child policy itself in isolation — were a major driver of China's fertility decline, with stronger enforcement mechanisms accounting for nearly half of that decline during a key decade.
items.citation: Lingsheng Meng, Han‐Mo Yang, Grant Miller et al.. Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China. Nature. 2026

items.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
items.summary: The paper evaluated a new diagnostic framework proposed by a major medical commission that distinguishes clinical obesity, characterized by organ dysfunction due to excess adiposity, from preclinical obesity, where excess adiposity exists but organ function is preserved, while also recommending anthropometric measures beyond body mass index alone. Using prevalence, incidence, and mortality data from hundreds of thousands of adults across cohorts in China, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Spain, the researchers compared this framework against conventional body mass index-based classification. They found that body mass index alone both overestimated and underestimated obesity in meaningful proportions of participants, and that incorporating waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio increased overall obesity prevalence estimates compared to body mass index alone. Clinical obesity represented roughly a quarter to a third of all obesity cases, and the large majority of individuals with preclinical obesity did not progress to clinical obesity over a decade of follow-up. Critically, clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality risk than preclinical obesity, and the combined anthropometric definition predicted mortality better than body mass index alone, supporting broader adoption of the new diagnostic framework in clinical practice and health policy.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it validates a proposed diagnostic framework that moves beyond BMI alone by incorporating additional measures like waist circumference and organ function to better classify obesity. The findings suggest this more nuanced approach offers greater clinical utility than traditional BMI-only classifications across diverse global populations.
items.citation: An Pan, Shengping Yang, Rafael Ramos et al.. Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts. Nature. 2026

items.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
items.summary: This paper investigated whether loss of TDP-43 nuclear function, a hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia, impairs synaptic activity in neurons. The researchers found that TDP-43 depletion induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact yet exhibit profound breakdown in synaptic communication, and they identified aberrant cryptic splicing of the UNC13A gene as a key driver of this dysfunction. To address this, they developed splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides capable of correcting UNC13A cryptic splicing in human cortical and spinal motor neurons as well as in a humanized mouse model. Correcting this single splicing defect was sufficient to restore spontaneous and evoked synaptic vesicle release, release probability at individual synapses, and broader network synchrony in human neurons. The findings establish UNC13A splice correction as a mechanistically grounded and genetically validated therapeutic strategy potentially applicable to the vast majority of patients with TDP-43 pathology across both diseases.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a pre-degenerative state in which neurons lose synaptic function before structural breakdown occurs, linking this directly to TDP-43 loss and aberrant *UNC13A* splicing. Crucially, it demonstrates that splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides can correct this cryptic splicing event and rescue synaptic dysfunction, pointing toward a potential therapeutic strategy for related diseases.
items.citation: Matthew J. Keuss, Peter Harley, Eugeni Ryadnov et al.. UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss. Nature. 2026

items.title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation
items.summary: The paper investigated why NLRP3 inflammasome activation behaves differently in laboratory cell culture compared to living organisms, a longstanding disconnect in the field. The researchers discovered that extracellular matrix stiffness is a key environmental variable governing this difference, finding that culturing human and mouse phagocytes on substrates with physiologically relevant stiffness recapitulates the in vivo condition where a single inflammatory signal (such as lipopolysaccharide alone) is sufficient to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome. They identified the transcription factor NRF2 as a mechanosensitive checkpoint induced by physiological matrix stiffness, which in turn promotes NLRP3 activity through transcriptional regulation of the gene Panx1. Consistent with this mechanism, macrophages residing in naturally stiff tissues showed altered NRF2 levels and corresponding changes in inflammasome activity, and patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity in alveolar macrophages. The study further demonstrated that NRF2 is required for effective antitumour immunity when NLRP3-activating adjuvants are used in cancer vaccines, positioning NRF2 as a central transcriptional regulator linking mechanical tissue cues to innate immune responses.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention by revealing that physical properties of the cellular environment—specifically extracellular matrix stiffness—can regulate a key inflammatory signaling complex, with NRF2 serving as the mechanosensitive link between mechanical cues and NLRP3 inflammasome activation both in vitro and in vivo.
items.citation: Daniel A. Okin, Joon H. Choi, Chun Wang et al.. NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Nature. 2026

items.title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
items.summary: This paper investigated how to achieve reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal-iodine batteries without relying on the halogen-containing electrolytes that have traditionally been required. The researchers developed a electrolyte design framework combining kosmotropic anions, polar anions, and nucleophilic species, where polar anions create a water-deficient, anion-enriched environment at the electrode interface and kosmotropic anions regulate interactions to increase the availability of nucleophilic species for stabilizing reactive hypervalent iodine cations through halogen bonding. This approach stabilizes the hypervalent iodine intermediates through nucleophile–iodine cation–nucleophile halogen bonds rather than the conventional interhalogen complexation mechanism. The framework was validated using diverse nucleophilic species and demonstrated to work in both aqueous zinc-iodine and aluminum-iodine battery systems. The findings establish a mechanistically distinct electrolyte chemistry that enables high-energy aqueous energy storage while eliminating the need for corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it achieves reversible four-electron iodine conversion—a high-capacity electrochemical process—using halogen-free aqueous electrolytes, overcoming a longstanding chemical compatibility challenge. The approach is validated in functional metal–iodine batteries, suggesting broad practical relevance for energy storage.
items.citation: Guanjie He, Haobo Dong, Yuhang Dai et al.. Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion. Nature. 2026

items.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
items.summary: This paper investigated how brown adipose tissue maintains two distinct subpopulations of brown adipocytes—those with high and low expression of the thermogenic protein UCP1—and how the balance between these states governs heat production. The researchers found that inflammatory cytokine IL-1β, secreted by neutrophils and macrophages, stabilizes a signaling enzyme that generates active glucocorticoids, which in turn activate the glucocorticoid receptor and suppress UCP1 expression, locking adipocytes in a low-thermogenic state. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels through sympathetic nervous system signaling, allowing the stabilizing enzyme to degrade and enabling low-UCP1 cells to convert into high-UCP1 thermogenic cells, while warming reverses this process. Genetically deleting the glucocorticoid receptor specifically in brown adipocytes during cold exposure locked cells in the high-thermogenic state and sustained elevated energy expenditure even after returning to normal temperatures. Crucially, aged animals showed chronically elevated IL-1β in brown adipose tissue that skewed the balance toward the low-thermogenic state, causing cold intolerance, and suppressing glucocorticoid receptor signaling in aged mice restored thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals a bistable regulatory mechanism by which immune signals from neutrophils and macrophages control brown adipocyte identity and thermogenic capacity. It shows that cold exposure drives a switch to high heat-producing states by suppressing this immune signaling through the nervous system, fundamentally linking inflammation, neural activity, and fat cell heterogeneity in temperature regulation.
items.citation: Anying Song, Yifan Wang, Guan Wang et al.. Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis. Nature. 2026

items.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
items.summary: This study investigated epigenetic heterogeneity within breast tumours, focusing on how distinct epigenetic cell populations within luminal-subtype tumours relate to cancer biology, diagnosis, and prognosis. Using a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, along with whole-genome DNA methylation deconvolution and single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of histone modifications, the researchers profiled treatment-naive human luminal tumours obtained after surgical resection. They discovered a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells within luminal tumours that carries a conserved epigenetic signature across patients, characterised by aggressive oncogenic traits, downregulated hormone receptor signalling, and alterations in histone methylation marks linked to loss of luminal identity. The study further demonstrated that this basal-like epigenetic signature can be detected in cell-free nucleosomes from blood, establishing a potential liquid biopsy approach for early breast cancer diagnosis. Critically, detection of this basal signature in blood was associated with prognosis, suggesting it could identify patients at heightened risk of disease relapse.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because single-cell epigenetic analyses of breast tumours have uncovered a conserved signature that could improve both diagnosis and the prediction of which patients are at heightened risk of disease relapse.
items.citation: Noa Furth, Christina Riemenschneider, Yishai Arieli et al.. Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis. Nature. 2026

items.title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors
items.summary: This study investigated how rice plants detect and respond to feeding by sucking insects, specifically focusing on the molecular signals generated during insect attack. The researchers discovered that a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein called NIB1 serves as a sensor for small cyclic nucleotide molecules produced when a salivary ribonuclease from green stink bugs digests plant RNA during feeding. When NIB1 binds these nuclease-generated products, it forms condensates in the nucleus that recruit a core immune regulator, thereby activating plant defences. The findings further suggest a mechanistic link between this insect-triggered signalling pathway and the defence signalling mediated by plant TIR proteins, which independently produce similar nuclease products as immune signals. Overall, the study reveals a conserved immune pathway in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins act as sensors of nuclease-derived second messengers to coordinate plant defence responses.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it uncovers a previously unrecognized plant immune mechanism in which an RNA-binding protein detects small-molecule signals generated by insect salivary enzymes, triggering a nuclear defense response. The findings suggest this messenger-based surveillance pathway is conserved, potentially reshaping understanding of how plants recognize and respond to herbivorous insects.
items.citation: Xiao‐Xiang Guo, Jia‐Fa Huang, Jinsong Zhao et al.. A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors. Nature. 2026

items.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
items.summary: Tidal power offers predictable renewable energy but exposes turbines to severe and variable hydrodynamic loads, driving up costs through the need for complex active pitch control systems. This study investigated whether passively flexible rubber blades, designed to deform along the chord at the trailing edge, could serve as a simpler alternative for load management. Through experimental testing under simulated tidal cycle conditions, the researchers found that flexible blades matched the total energy yield of rigid blades equipped with active pitch control. Crucially, the flexible blades also reduced high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third, with this passive regulation arising from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under loading. The results suggest that chordwise-flexible blades offer a mechanically simpler and potentially more cost-effective route to durable tidal turbine design.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because flexible rubber blades achieve energy output comparable to more complex active-control systems while substantially cutting the load fluctuations that cause wear and mechanical failure. The combination of maintained performance with reduced maintenance complexity represents a meaningful advance for practical tidal energy deployment.
items.citation: Zhehong Zhang, Junchen Tan, Eric-Carin Neba et al.. Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines. Nature. 2026

items.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
items.summary: This paper reports the discovery of an ancient trondhjemitic gneiss from the North China Craton, extending the known record of terrestrial rocks older than roughly four billion years beyond the previously unique Acasta Gneiss Complex in Canada. The researchers analyzed magmatic zircons from this rock, measuring oxygen isotope ratios and hafnium isotope compositions, which together indicate that the source material was low-temperature altered basaltic crust derived from a Hadean depleted mantle. Unlike the Acasta rocks, which formed under low-pressure conditions, this gneiss displays geochemical signatures consistent with a high-pressure origin, and thermodynamic and trace element modelling indicates that its parental magma formed through partial melting of basaltic crust at depths corresponding to pressures exceeding one and a half gigapascals along a cool thermal gradient. The researchers interpret these conditions as requiring the rapid burial of near-surface altered oceanic crust to mantle depths, most plausibly achieved through a transient subduction event approximately three and a half billion years ago. The findings suggest that both Hadean mantle depletion and early subduction-like processes were operating on Earth by this time.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it pushes evidence for subduction — a hallmark of modern-style plate tectonics — back to nearly four billion years ago, among the earliest such signatures yet proposed. The ancient rocks also imply that mantle depletion began even earlier, during the Hadean, offering rare geochemical insight into Earth's formative geological processes.
items.citation: Hangqiang Xie, Chunyan Dong, Pengchuan Li et al.. Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks. Nature. 2026

items.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
items.summary: This study investigated how human land-use change influences microplastic accumulation in free-ranging terrestrial mammals in Brazil. The researchers combined direct microplastic measurements from living animals with high-resolution GPS tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters to link individual habitat use with microplastic burdens. They found that microplastic loads in these mammals increased with greater exposure to human-modified landscapes and closer proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Notably, microplastics were also detected in the blood of animals inhabiting apparently pristine, remote habitats, indicating that direct contact with developed areas is not the only pathway to systemic microplastic contamination. The findings suggest that managing wildlife proximity to anthropogenic infrastructure could help reduce microplastic burdens in terrestrial animals amid ongoing global land-use change.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it links human-modified land use and proximity to development directly to microplastic accumulation in wild mammals, while also revealing that even animals in remote habitats are not spared, underscoring the pervasive reach of plastic pollution across landscapes.
authors: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz
items.citation: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, Arnaud Léonard Jean Desbiez, Mário Henrique Alves et al.. Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife. Nature. 2026

items.title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice
items.summary: During early mouse embryogenesis, nuclei undergo extensive epigenetic reprogramming, yet how the physical properties of the nucleus itself change during this process had remained largely unexplored. Using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation, researchers examined the mechanical properties of nuclei at the two-cell embryonic stage and discovered that nuclei become remarkably soft and deformable precisely when zygotic gene activation occurs. This transient softness results from autophagy-mediated clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope, and experimentally preventing this clearance or artificially stiffening the nucleus impairs zygotic gene activation and embryonic development. High-resolution imaging and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization revealed that nuclear deformability facilitates the accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and the coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the nuclear envelope. The findings establish that a distinct, transient physical state of the nucleus is essential for initiating the zygotic transcription program at the onset of mammalian life.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that embryos transiently adopt a physically softer nuclear state at the very start of life, and that this mechanical change in the nucleus plays a functional role in activating the embryo's own gene expression program.
items.citation: Masahito Tanaka, Rin Sakanoue, Yasuki Miyagawa et al.. Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice. Nature. 2026

items.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a previously unrecognized role for a common gut antibody in controlling the rate at which colon lining cells divide and in protecting against colorectal cancer. The findings, demonstrated in mouse models, suggest that immune factors within the gut lumen itself may directly influence epithelial cell turnover and tumor susceptibility.
items.citation: Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad et al.. Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA. Nature. 2026

items.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
items.summary: This study investigated the pre-cancerous somatic evolutionary dynamics that precede acute myeloid leukaemia, with the goal of quantifying how driver mutations accumulate and expand in blood over time. Using serial blood samples collected annually for up to a decade before leukaemia diagnosis, the researchers applied deep duplex sequencing combined with evolutionary theory to reconstruct the timing and fitness effects of key driver events. They found that initial driver mutations are typically acquired early in life, when blood remains highly polyclonal, and that these early clones grow slowly. Subsequently, the acquisition of additional driver mutations confers dramatically larger selective advantages, enabling faster-growing multi-driver clones to completely sweep through the blood compartment decades before diagnosis, a pattern strongly associated with eventual leukaemia development. The findings suggest that clonal haematopoiesis follows simple evolutionary rules that balance stochastic and deterministic processes, providing a quantitative framework for understanding cancer predisposition.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals the somatic evolutionary trajectories of blood cells in the period before acute myeloid leukaemia develops, showing that clonal dynamics follow predictable, simple evolutionary rules. Understanding these pre-diagnostic patterns could shed light on how leukaemia arises and potentially inform early detection strategies.
items.citation: Caroline J. Watson, Gladys Y. P. Poon, Hamish A J MacGregor et al.. Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia. Nature. 2026

items.title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
items.summary: This paper introduces a design framework called scale-rich metamaterials, which embeds the kind of multiscale structural heterogeneity found in real-world and biological networks—such as the brain or the Internet—into the architecture of mechanical metamaterials. Unlike conventional metamaterials that rely on periodic, homogeneous unit cells with discrete length scales, the proposed framework uses network science principles to generate structures with orders-of-magnitude variation in ligament lengths, thicknesses, and connectivity, governed by just two parameters. Through a combination of simulations and physical experiments, the authors demonstrate that these scale-rich metamaterials exhibit mechanical properties unattainable by traditional single-scale systems, including tunable elastic anisotropy, delocalized nonlinear deformation, high energy absorption, enhanced dynamic energy dissipation, and programmable elastic-wave control. The work establishes network heterogeneity as a minimal and universal basis for engineering multifunctional materials whose behavior emerges directly from structural scale diversity, while also suggesting new directions for network science research.
items.why_notable: By applying network-science principles to mechanical metamaterial design, this work introduces structural heterogeneity across multiple scales, unlocking mechanical properties that conventional single-scale systems cannot achieve.
items.citation: Csaba Both, Andrew Yen-Jong Chen, Ting-Ting Gao et al.. Scale-rich network-based metamaterials. Nature. 2026

items.title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
items.summary: The paper investigated how stalled DNA replication forks are restarted through a process called repriming carried out by the enzyme PRIMPOL, focusing on the molecular mechanisms governing its recruitment, positioning, and regulation. Using real-time single-molecule imaging in nuclear extracts that recapitulate genome maintenance, the researchers directly visualized repriming events at stalled forks. They found that PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks via a direct interaction with the replicative helicase complex CMG, which facilitates handover of newly synthesized primers to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, thereby minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis. Under near-physiological conditions this primary repriming mode operates close to CMG and does not require DNA damage checkpoint signalling, whereas PRIMPOL overexpression or checkpoint activation triggers a secondary mode in which repriming occurs far from CMG and primers are extended by polymerase δ instead. Together, these findings reveal a targeted, CMG-dependent mechanism that restricts PRIMPOL activity to stalled forks and suggest a potential strategy for inhibiting the repriming pathway.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals the molecular mechanism by which PRIMPOL restarts stalled replication forks, showing how it is recruited to the replicative helicase and hands off primers to a high-fidelity polymerase to limit error-prone DNA synthesis.
items.citation: Jinho Park, Luke D. Lynch, Elena Blanco‐Romero et al.. The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL. Nature. 2026

items.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
items.summary: This study investigated a new therapeutic strategy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, which depends on androgen receptor signaling maintained through its interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP. The researchers developed a novel class of molecules called domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs) that work by enforcing non-native interactions between specific protein domains, thereby rewiring endogenous oncogenic protein complexes rather than simply inhibiting them. Their lead compound forces proximity between the androgen receptor's ligand-binding domain and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, locking the complex in a non-productive configuration that suppresses androgen receptor-driven transcription more effectively than blocking either target alone. Mechanistically, this intervention reprograms how p300/CBP engages its substrates, eliminates specific histone acetylation marks, induces aberrant acetylation of the androgen receptor and its coactivators, and disrupts the assembly of transcriptional machinery at oncogenic enhancers. The compound demonstrated selective activity in androgen receptor-dependent cancer cells while sparing others, and produced sustained tumor regressions in multiple animal models, suggesting broad applicability of the DALTAC strategy for rewiring disease-relevant protein complexes.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it introduces a new class of molecules that force abnormal interactions between a key cancer-driving protein and its regulatory partners, achieving unusually potent and selective suppression of metastatic prostate cancer. Beyond the specific disease application, the approach is framed as a broadly applicable therapeutic strategy for rewiring oncogenic protein complexes through induced proximity.
items.citation: Jie Luo, Jianzhang Yang, Jean Ching-Yi Tien et al.. Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer. Nature. 2026

items.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
items.summary: The nuclear pore complex controls selective molecular traffic between the nucleus and cytoplasm through a permeability barrier made of intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), but the physical state of these proteins inside living cells has remained contentious. Using site-specific labelling combined with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy and molecular-dynamics simulations, the researchers investigated how FG domains behave in live cells compared to reconstituted systems. They found that FG domains display rapid, liquid-like segmental motion on nanosecond timescales in living cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro, highlighting the importance of cellular context. The transport receptor importin-β and O-linked glycosylation of FG-NUPs together act to stabilize this dynamic liquid-like network, generating a radial organization in which importin-β concentrates near the pore periphery while extended FG domains occupy the central channel to form the transport barrier. These findings reconcile previously conflicting models of FG-NUP organization and are supported by direct nanoscale imaging of importin-β localization, providing a unified framework for how intrinsically disordered proteins are tuned by their cellular environment.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals the molecular mechanisms by which nuclear pore proteins form a fluid yet selective barrier, offering a resolution to long-standing, competing models of how nuclear pores are structured and how they achieve selective transport.
items.citation: Miao Yu, Maziar Heidari, Karen Palacio‐Rodríguez et al.. Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores. Nature. 2026

items.title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals that severe drought and warming will substantially shrink the climatically suitable habitat for cactus species, raising their extinction risk. The findings highlight a major climate-driven threat to this distinctive plant group.
items.citation: Michiel Pillet, Brian Maitner, Mónica Arakaki et al.. Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti. Nature. 2026

items.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
items.summary: This paper investigated the challenge of reducing power consumption in scaled silicon electronics by exploring two-dimensional semiconductor transistors with improved gate dielectric interfaces. The researchers developed a wafer-scale, transferable single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric that can be integrated with two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides via van der Waals bonding, creating an exceptionally clean interface. This pristine interface yielded subthreshold swing approaching the fundamental thermal limit, record-low hysteresis, and stable performance for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode transistors. Using these components, the team fabricated complementary field-effect transistors whose inverters demonstrated high voltage gain, large noise margins, and subpicowatt static power consumption. The results establish single-crystal high-κ dielectrics as a compelling route to ultra-low-power operation in two-dimensional semiconductor devices.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because using a transferable single-crystal high-κ dielectric achieves high-quality interfaces with two-dimensional semiconductors, resulting in near-ideal switching behavior, low hysteresis, and ultra-low-power complementary transistors—addressing longstanding challenges in scaling next-generation low-power electronics.
