items.citation: Ni Yang, Ji Zhang, Yu-Cheng Lu et al.. Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics. Nature. 2026

items.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
items.summary: This paper addresses ongoing debates about the reliability of the first black hole shadow image of M87*, where different imaging methods and data analysis choices had produced inconsistent representations of the source's fine-scale structure, with some analyses even questioning whether the fundamental ring-like morphology was real. The challenge stems from the sparse interferometric measurements of very long baseline interferometry, which make image reconstruction an underdetermined problem highly sensitive to calibration, algorithms, and tuning parameters. The researchers developed and applied an independent imaging algorithm that avoids prescriptive morphological assumptions and relies on observables that are immune to instrument calibration errors. Their method independently reconstructed a ring-like morphology from the same dataset, unequivocally confirming the black hole shadow, with the inferred angular diameter consistent with a black hole mass in agreement with previous estimates and an inclination broadly consistent with the known jet orientation. This work strengthens confidence in the original black hole shadow detection by demonstrating that the ring morphology is robust across fundamentally different imaging approaches.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it independently confirms the black hole shadow and mass using a novel approach that sidesteps the calibration and imaging assumptions that have constrained previous analyses. The use of closure-invariant formalism combined with diffusion-based reconstruction provides a more robust, assumption-free validation of one of astronomy's landmark observations.
items.citation: Samuel Lai, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, O. Ivy Wong et al.. Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*. Nature. 2026

items.title: PCR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Strengthening Environmental Pathogen Surveillance and Public Health Preparedness Across United States Communities
items.summary: This review paper examines the role of PCR-based molecular diagnostic technologies in strengthening environmental pathogen surveillance and public health preparedness across the United States. The authors critically assess advances across multiple PCR formats, including conventional, quantitative, digital, and multiplex approaches, as well as point-of-need platforms, evaluating their application to complex environmental matrices such as wastewater, surface water, soil, and air. The review addresses key methodological considerations including assay design, sample processing, quality assurance, and computational data interpretation, alongside integration with national surveillance infrastructures such as wastewater-based epidemiology programs. The authors find that PCR technologies offer substantial advantages over conventional culture-based methods in terms of speed, sensitivity, and throughput for detecting bacterial, viral, fungal, and protozoan pathogens, with demonstrated utility for early outbreak detection and antimicrobial resistance monitoring. The review concludes by identifying current implementation challenges and highlighting opportunities to combine artificial intelligence with molecular diagnostics to further enhance surveillance capacity and public health resilience.
items.venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
items.citation: Iyanuoluwa Oluwafemi. PCR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Strengthening Environmental Pathogen Surveillance and Public Health Preparedness Across United States Communities. International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews. 2026

items.title: Policy and Governance of Disease Surveillance Systems in Nigeria: Addressing Emerging Microbial Threats
items.summary: This review examines the policies, governance structures, and operational capacity of disease surveillance systems in Nigeria as they relate to managing infectious disease threats and antimicrobial resistance. The authors critically assessed the country's Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response framework, coordinated by the national disease control agency, alongside the broader public health infrastructure responsible for outbreak detection and response. Nigeria's experience managing major outbreaks has yielded meaningful advances in workforce capacity and laboratory networks, yet the review identifies persistent weaknesses including fragmented data systems, inadequate diagnostic infrastructure at sub-national levels, insufficient funding, and poor integration of One Health principles. Promising developments noted include the launch of a national antimicrobial resistance survey and early exploration of wastewater-based epidemiology as a surveillance tool. The review concludes that although national policy frameworks are broadly sound, achieving genuine health security will require sustained investment in laboratory capacity, digital surveillance infrastructure, antibiotic stewardship, and equitable implementation of surveillance systems down to the local level.
items.citation: Nnamdi Michael Nwadiogbu, James Kodilichukwu Anekwe, Obioma Davison Mbanefo et al.. Policy and Governance of Disease Surveillance Systems in Nigeria: Addressing Emerging Microbial Threats. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive sequence analysis reveals the vast β-lactam resistome
items.summary: This study investigated the environmental reservoir of β-lactamase resistance genes, which are enzymes that confer resistance to β-lactam antibiotics and are thought to have ancient origins in environmental microorganisms. Using an integrated bioinformatics and experimental workflow applied to large-scale sequence databases, the researchers systematically identified and classified putative β-lactamase sequences across all four enzyme classes. They discovered a reservoir of putative β-lactamases vastly exceeding what is currently catalogued in existing resistance gene databases, distributed across diverse bacterial phyla and environmental ecosystems. Notably, putative β-lactamases were detected at frequencies approaching those of an essential housekeeping gene, with relative enrichment found in wastewater and plant-associated environments, though terrestrial and aquatic settings also harbored close homologs of clinically relevant variants. The findings reveal a largely unexplored and taxonomically broad β-lactamase resistome with the potential for mobilization into clinical pathogens, and the authors provide a reusable mapping tool to support future surveillance efforts.
items.citation: Sevan Gholipour, John Z. Chen, Dong‐Kyu Lee et al.. Comprehensive sequence analysis reveals the vast β-lactam resistome. Microbiome. 2026

items.title: Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host
items.summary: This study investigated whether antibiotic resistance genes detected in wastewater can serve as meaningful indicators of community-level antibiotic use, a question complicated by the complex microbial ecology of sewer systems. The researchers combined a multi-year dataset of outpatient antibiotic prescription records with intensive metagenomic sampling of a single wastewater treatment plant over the course of a year to disentangle human-derived resistance signals from in-sewer microbial dynamics. They found that resistance genes associated with Enterobacteriaceae tracked closely and contemporaneously with antibiotic usage patterns in the community, while resistance genes linked to Pseudomonadaceae showed delayed correlations of one to three months, reflecting the distinct ecological behavior of these organisms within the sewer environment. Statistical modeling further confirmed that the dynamics of Pseudomonas populations in sewage were associated with lagged use of specific antibiotic classes after controlling for sewage characteristics and seasonality. The findings demonstrate that wastewater-based surveillance can capture epidemiologically relevant antibiotic resistance signals, but only when the host bacterial ecology shaping those signals is explicitly taken into account.
items.citation: Connor Brown, MA. Rumi, Lauren F. McDaniel et al.. Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
items.summary: This review examines the use of wastewater collected from aircraft lavatories and airport facilities as a public health surveillance tool for detecting and monitoring infectious pathogens among traveling populations. The authors conducted a structured narrative review synthesizing current evidence on the scientific, methodological, and interpretive dimensions of aviation-based wastewater surveillance, with particular focus on lessons drawn from monitoring for the virus responsible for the pandemic. They find that while detection of viral RNA in aviation wastewater can provide timely, aggregate signals about pathogen circulation, the reliability of these signals depends on a complex array of factors including pathogen shedding dynamics, flight duration, sampling design, assay sensitivity, and the availability of epidemiological context. The review cautions that wastewater signals cannot be interpreted as individual-level diagnoses, evidence of transmission, or definitive attribution to specific flights or origin countries. The authors conclude that extending surveillance beyond the best-documented pathogen to cover a broader range of viruses, vaccine-preventable infections, and antimicrobial resistance markers will require pathogen-specific validation, and that the approach's public health value ultimately rests on converting technical detections into rigorously interpretable evidence within an integrated, sustainable surveillance framework.
items.citation: Vaidya SR, Pandey PG, Giri S et al.. Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.
items.summary: This paper examined wastewater surveillance as a complementary tool for monitoring *Salmonella* at the population level, addressing the limitations of traditional clinical surveillance in capturing asymptomatic or unreported infections. The researchers developed and validated a workflow involving polyethylene glycol precipitation for sample concentration, magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction, and quantitative PCR for pathogen detection. When deployed across a statewide surveillance network, the approach revealed seasonal transmission patterns and demonstrated the ability to identify outbreak activity that passive clinical surveillance missed. Notably, the wastewater signal preceded clinical case reporting by approximately one week, highlighting its potential for early warning. The authors conclude that despite challenges such as low pathogen concentrations and limited resolution at the serovar level, integrating wastewater surveillance with conventional public health systems meaningfully improves the detection and understanding of *Salmonella* dynamics.
items.citation: Kuhn KG, Shelton K, Rimal B et al.. From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.). 2027

items.title: Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.
items.summary: This study examined how the structure of urban wastewater infrastructure affects the detection and interpretation of multiple respiratory viruses through wastewater-based epidemiology, focusing on the heterogeneous sewage systems of Mumbai. Researchers collected wastewater samples across two monitoring periods from both centralised sewage treatment plants and decentralised open drains, analysing them for SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus using RT-qPCR. Centralised treatment plants produced more consistent viral signals with less short-term variability, reflecting their integration of signals across larger populations, while open drains showed greater temporal fluctuation consistent with more localised transmission dynamics. SARS-CoV-2 was reliably detected across both node types, whereas influenza detection was more sporadic and suggested seasonal patterns, with co-detection of influenza A and B subtypes observed in one monitoring period. The authors conclude that viral signal profiles reflect both pathogen-specific characteristics and the structural configuration of the sampling network, and advocate for integrated surveillance frameworks combining centralised and decentralised nodes alongside clinical validation to improve epidemiological inference.
items.citation: Shaikh A, Nikam S, Mistry N. Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.. Food and environmental virology. 2026

items.title: Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
items.summary: This study examined how a major international mass gathering event affected the infectious disease landscape in a host city by employing wastewater-based surveillance as a complement to traditional clinical monitoring. Researchers collected wastewater samples from three water reclamation facilities before, during, and after the FIFA World Cup matches held in Atlanta, testing each sample against a broad panel of respiratory and gastrointestinal pathogen targets using multiplexed qualitative PCR assays. The primary analysis found no statistically significant differences in pathogen detection between the pre-tournament and tournament periods across the facilities. A sensitivity analysis that incorporated post-tournament samples did reveal a statistically significant increase in SARS-CoV-2 detection, but this increase mirrored regional and national trends, suggesting it reflected broader community transmission rather than a tournament-specific effect. The authors conclude that qualitative multiplexed PCR panels can serve as a practical tool for population-level pathogen surveillance during mass gathering events, while acknowledging that wide confidence intervals, the absence of quantitative data, and limited post-event sampling constrain definitive conclusions.
items.citation: Raymo N, Kraft CS, Gulick D et al.. Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings
items.citation: Ahmed W, Medlicott K, Nolan M. A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings. ACS ES&T water. 2026

items.title: Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examined the application of machine learning to wastewater-based surveillance for detecting and monitoring emerging pathogens at the community level. The authors conducted a narrative review of published literature, classifying studies by their analytical role, task type, and strength of evidence, organizing methods into four layers spanning classical statistical models through deep learning and hybrid mechanistic approaches across five analytical tasks. They found that the evidence base is heavily concentrated on SARS-CoV-2 and that demonstrated early-warning performance came predominantly from simpler classical statistical methods rather than more complex machine learning approaches, with most other pathogen-task combinations remaining prospective rather than validated. Reported performance was consistently context-dependent, and broader application is constrained by data-quality problems including sampling variability, environmental noise, and population-dependent biases alongside methodological and governance barriers. The authors call for standardized collaborative frameworks, multimodal data fusion, mechanistic and digital-twin modelling with explicit uncertainty quantification, and transparent analytics to advance the field beyond its current narrow evidence base.
items.citation: Song A, Jia P, Luo J et al.. Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.. Emerging microbes & infections. 2026

items.title: Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional occupational health surveillance systems, which suffer from delayed hazard detection and poor adaptability to changing workplace conditions. The authors propose an AI-powered surveillance framework that integrates wearable devices and Internet of Things sensors to continuously collect data on both environmental factors and individual employee health metrics. Machine learning algorithms and predictive analytics are applied to these data streams to identify anomalies, recognize risk patterns, and trigger proactive interventions before hazards escalate. The system also includes a dashboard for visualizing health and safety insights, generating automated compliance documentation, and delivering recommendations to managers and workers. The authors claim the framework is scalable across industries and capable of improving workplace safety culture, reducing injuries, and enhancing employee well-being by bridging emerging technologies with occupational health practice.
items.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.citation: Cynthia Obianuju Ozobu. Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards. WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately characterizing the transmission dynamics of co-circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. The authors extended existing methods for estimating effective reproduction numbers from case count data to jointly incorporate genetic sequencing data, enabling simultaneous inference of variant-specific effective reproduction numbers and variant frequencies. Applying this framework to confirmed case and sequencing data across United States states over roughly fourteen months, they modeled structured relationships between reproduction numbers to estimate fixed variant-specific growth advantages that remain consistent across locations. The approach moves beyond analyses based solely on sequence frequency dynamics, which cannot fully capture epidemiological behavior, by linking variant prevalence directly to transmission intensity. Using this method, they estimated effective reproduction numbers and location-consistent growth advantages for multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and interest circulating in the United States during the study period.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper investigates the challenge of monitoring maritime activities by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which identifies vessels but has known vulnerabilities, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships on their own. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers developed a Pair Hidden Markov Model to align individual radio frequency detections with AIS vessel trajectories by incorporating temporal and spatial information while accounting for noise and timing discrepancies. The model was evaluated on real AIS data combined with synthetic radio frequency detections, with performance benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that compares the full model against a null model without match transitions substantially improved both association precision and the detection of vessels behaving suspiciously by suppressing their AIS signals. Despite these improvements, a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without any parameter fitting still outperformed the probabilistic model, indicating that the proposed single-detection Pair Hidden Markov Model formulation approaches but does not surpass simpler heuristic methods.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
items.summary: The paper studies the problem of detecting slope changes in multidimensional time series by fitting continuous piecewise-linear functions that share a single breakpoint, examining both a dense setting where all dimensions may change slope and a sparse setting where at most a fixed number of dimensions may do so. Despite the resulting optimization problems being nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear programs that can yield irrational solutions even for rational inputs, the authors prove that all six problem variants across three common loss functions are exactly solvable in polynomial time. Efficient algorithms are derived for the least-squares case, with the dense variant requiring operations linear in the product of dimensions and time points and the sparse variant scaling with the square of the number of dimensions. These algorithms are implemented and benchmarked on both simulated and real-world datasets spanning climate, motion tracking, and engineering sensor domains, demonstrating that they solve large instances in well under a second on a laptop. Compared to a general-purpose mixed-integer nonlinear programming solver, the proposed algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster while consistently finding exact optimal solutions on instances where the solver struggles or fails to converge within time limits.
items.citation: Apoorva Narula, Santanu S. Dey. Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigated how convolutional neural networks exploit contextual background information when classifying agricultural images, and whether the internal representations of hidden neurons can be made interpretable using a technique called Concept Induction. The researchers applied this approach across multiple agricultural datasets with varying degrees of contextual bias, examining several CNN architectures at different network depths and across different spatial patch locations within images. Quantitative visual descriptors were encoded in a knowledge graph and used as background knowledge to derive logical expressions characterizing when individual neurons activate, with these expressions then statistically validated on held-out images. The study found that neuron-feature relationships were most frequently validated at intermediate network depths, and that texture-related features such as edge, Gabor, and Tamura descriptors were most commonly linked to neuron activations. Notably, the degree of contextual bias in a dataset did not align with the rate of interpretable neuron-feature validation, suggesting that a network's behavioral reliance on background context and the semantic interpretability of its hidden neurons reflect distinct and separable aspects of CNN behavior.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world object detection systems, framing each detected bounding box decision as a hypothesis test where the null hypothesis assumes the box contains an in-distribution object. The authors identify that the null distribution of box features varies systematically with box size and border contact, motivating a conditioning strategy that compares each box only against in-distribution boxes sharing the same geometric properties, which yields distribution-free false-alarm rate bounds and reveals separations obscured by pooling across all box types. Because classification-oriented layers discard information about unknown objects, the method reads features from earlier in the network, specifically from the last backbone stage before class-specific processing. Building on these insights, the authors propose PLUM, a training-free scoring method that pools backbone features within a box and ranks their distance to in-distribution classes using the box-conditional reference set. PLUM achieves state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection performance on standard benchmarks without requiring external models or additional training.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: This paper investigates whether Redshift Space Distortions (RSD) can mimic parity violation signals in galaxy clustering statistics, specifically in the four-point correlation function (4PCF). The authors analyzed the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density using Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory to third order, incorporating wide-angle effects, tidal bias, and an arbitrary cosmological background. By expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, they demonstrated that angular momentum selection rules encoded in Wigner 3-j symbols force all parity-odd contributions from RSD to vanish when averaged over all line-of-sight orientations. This result holds both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case, up to leading-order general relativistic corrections. The finding is significant for ongoing observational searches for cosmological parity violation, as it confirms that any detected parity-odd signal in isotropic 4PCF estimators cannot be attributed to RSD as a systematic artefact.
items.citation: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.. Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of coherent detection for audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) modulation in CubeSat communications, where the severe line-of-sight dynamics of low Earth orbit typically make synchronization too difficult for practical use. The authors developed an all-digital coherent AFSK demodulator that combines a Kalman filter for carrier phase and timing synchronization with the Viterbi algorithm for maximum likelihood sequence detection, with detected bit statistics fed back to the Kalman filter to track phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift. Original mathematical analyses were derived to characterize synchronization accuracy under dynamic low Earth orbit conditions, and the system was evaluated using simulations with real CubeSat orbital parameters over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. The proposed coherent demodulator achieved a substantial improvement in bit error rate performance compared to the conventional noncoherent AFSK approach, demonstrating that coherent detection is viable even under challenging orbital dynamics.
items.citation: Rubem Vasconcelos Pacelli, Rodrigo de Lima Florindo, Felix Antreich et al.. An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infections in its intermediate snail hosts, which is critical for controlling and eliminating schistosomiasis, a neglected tropical disease. The researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of the parasite, optimizing it for a simple, single-temperature reaction, and evaluated its performance against conventional parasitological methods, standard PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two endemic countries. The assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory conditions, outperforming microscopy and matching the performance of real-time PCR, while in field settings it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR and identified infections entirely missed by parasitological examination. These results demonstrate that the assay is a sensitive, specific, and practically deployable diagnostic tool suitable for routine surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission in snail populations.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Towards point-of-care diagnostics of neglected tropical diseases using nucleic acid amplification tests.
items.summary: This paper reviewed the state of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification tests for neglected tropical diseases, a group of conditions that have historically received less diagnostic innovation than other major infectious diseases despite their considerable global burden. The authors conducted a systematic critical analysis of published studies, examining the full nucleic acid amplification workflow with an emphasis on operational feasibility and implementation barriers rather than purely analytical performance metrics. Common themes emerging from the literature included simplified extraction methods, integrated device platforms, smartphone-based result interpretation, and workflows designed to reduce dependence on cold chains and electricity. Despite these advances, the review identified persistent technical, analytical, and implementation obstacles that prevent most current developments from transitioning from proof-of-concept prototypes to genuinely field-deployable tools. The central finding is that the majority of nucleic acid amplification test developments for neglected tropical diseases do not yet meet the World Health Organization's criteria for point-of-care application in resource-limited settings, and that achieving elimination goals will require careful attention to every step from sample collection through to real-world deployment.
items.citation: Priem N, Rodriguez-Mateos P, Waweru H et al.. Towards point-of-care diagnostics of neglected tropical diseases using nucleic acid amplification tests.. Analytical and bioanalytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: A LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Specific Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in Whole Blood: Analytical Performance and Clinical Evaluation in Suspected Bloodstream Infection.
items.summary: This paper developed and evaluated a diagnostic assay combining loop-mediated isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a detection to identify *Escherichia coli* directly in whole blood, targeting the *dxs* gene. The assay was optimised and benchmarked against quantitative PCR and blood culture using both laboratory-spiked samples and clinical specimens from patients with suspected bloodstream infection. The method demonstrated complete inclusivity across tested *E. coli* isolates and full exclusivity against non-target organisms, with results readable within minutes of initiating the CRISPR detection step. Its limit of detection was modestly higher than that of quantitative PCR, and in the clinical evaluation it identified all patient samples at or above the quantitative PCR detection threshold while producing no false positives. Because bacteraemia typically involves extremely low bacterial loads, the assay's clinical sensitivity was insufficient for use as a rule-out test, but its specificity and speed make it appropriate as a rapid confirmatory tool used alongside blood culture.
items.citation: Quyen DT, Thau NS, Trung PQ et al.. A LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Specific Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in Whole Blood: Analytical Performance and Clinical Evaluation in Suspected Bloodstream Infection.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future potential of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for cancer, addressing the need for rapid, accurate testing outside centralized laboratory settings. The authors survey advances in sample preparation, nucleic acid and protein biomarker detection, and imaging modalities compatible with decentralized deployment across diverse clinical environments. Key enabling technologies evaluated include microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip platforms, nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors, and smartphone-integrated devices, alongside their limitations. The review also analyzes funding landscapes, intellectual property considerations, and regulatory frameworks that govern the translation of these technologies from research to commercial use. The authors conclude that interdisciplinary innovation and attention to equitable access are essential for integrating point-of-care molecular diagnostics into precision oncology for cancer detection, therapy selection, and treatment monitoring.
items.citation: Seemesh Bhaskar, Saurabh Umrao, Hankeun Lee et al.. Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk
items.summary: This study developed a rapid molecular detection platform for *Streptococcus agalactiae*, a major cause of bovine mastitis, by combining recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with the prokaryotic Argonaute protein PfAgo, targeting the conserved *cfb* gene. The researchers screened multiple primer pairs and guide DNAs to optimize the system, which was configured in two readout formats: a real-time fluorescence assay and a lateral flow dipstick assay. The fluorescence-based format achieved a lower detection limit than the dipstick format, and both demonstrated high analytical specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target bacteria. Field validation using bovine milk samples from multiple dairy-farming regions in China showed that both RPA-PfAgo formats detected substantially more positive samples than bacteriological culture, while achieving complete concordance with a standardized quantitative PCR assay across all samples tested. The authors conclude that this dual-readout platform offers a rapid and reliable alternative to conventional methods for on-site detection of *S. agalactiae* in dairy settings.
items.citation: Xujie Zhao, Yuying Du, Qianlei Zhu et al.. Development and Application of a Dual-Readout RPA-PfAgo System for Rapid Detection of Streptococcus agalactiae in Bovine Milk. Veterinary Sciences. 2026

items.title: Smartphone-integrated RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection system with microneedle sampling for early point-of-care diagnosis of potato late blight
items.citation: Jinbiao Zhao, Hanbo Xu, Shifang Fei et al.. Smartphone-integrated RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection system with microneedle sampling for early point-of-care diagnosis of potato late blight. Biosensors and Bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, in the context of a rapidly changing global environment. The authors synthesize current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review identifies significant surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances discussed include molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems. The authors argue that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and improving preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Molecular engineering of CRISPR/Cas12a: from activity enhancement to exponential signal amplification
items.summary: This review examines strategies to improve the detection sensitivity of CRISPR/Cas12a-based molecular diagnostics by moving beyond its inherent linear signal output limitations. Rather than coupling Cas12a with external pre-amplification techniques, which add complexity and uncertainty to clinical workflows, the authors focus on molecular engineering approaches that intrinsically enhance the system's performance. The review systematically covers methods including crRNA reprogramming, activator strand engineering, reporter probe design, and reaction environment optimization as means to improve catalytic kinetics, specificity, and signal output. Together, these strategies are argued to shift the paradigm from the conventional "one-target-one-enzyme" model toward exponential signal amplification without pre-amplification steps. The authors propose that such integrated engineering approaches enable ultrasensitive detection of both nucleic acid and non-nucleic acid targets, supporting the development of field-deployable point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Qing-Nan Li, Qi-Fan Yang, Wei-Liang Jin et al.. Molecular engineering of CRISPR/Cas12a: from activity enhancement to exponential signal amplification. Chemical Science. 2026

items.title: Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of bacterial identification methods in the context of rising antimicrobial resistance and the limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches. The authors surveyed techniques spanning classical methods such as microscopy, culture, and biochemical testing through to advanced proteomic, immunological, and molecular tools including various forms of polymerase chain reaction, whole-genome sequencing, and metagenomics. Emerging technologies such as CRISPR-based diagnostics and phage- and nanomaterial-based detection systems are also considered, alongside the integration of artificial intelligence to enhance analytical performance. The review finds that while the combination of these approaches promises improvements in accuracy, speed, and applicability across clinical, veterinary, agricultural, and environmental settings, variability in bioinformatics frameworks and algorithm-defined thresholds continues to hinder standardized implementation, particularly for whole-genome sequencing in routine laboratories. The authors conclude that technological modernization must be pursued cautiously, with standardization treated as a central priority.
items.citation: Ina Gajić, Milos Jovicevic, Dušan Kekić et al.. Evolving Approaches to Bacterial Identification: A Review of Classical and Modern Techniques. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Scan-specific k-space interpolation using deep Koopman autoencoders
items.summary: This paper developed a scan-specific deep learning method for reconstructing accelerated MRI data through nonlinear k-space interpolation. The proposed approach uses a deep Koopman autoencoder architecture comprising an encoder, a linear interpolation layer, and a decoder, trained on autocalibration signals with a combined prediction and autoencoding loss. The method was evaluated against established techniques on a large set of retrospectively undersampled brain datasets using quantitative metrics and a clinical reader study assessing image quality attributes such as sharpness, noise, and aliasing. The proposed technique outperformed both GRAPPA and RAKI on quantitative measures, demonstrated greater resilience to noise amplification, and was preferred by clinical readers over RAKI in a forced-choice evaluation. The method also showed robustness to variations in key parameters such as autocalibration signal count, kernel size, and latent space dimensionality.
items.citation: Wassim Ben Salah, Jon Cleary, Sarah McElroy et al.. Scan-specific k-space interpolation using deep Koopman autoencoders. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Extending an X-ray & Mid-Infrared diagnostic for absorption in Active Galactic Nuclei to higher redshifts using NuSTAR and XMM-Newton
items.summary: This paper investigated methods for measuring the fraction of Compton-thick active galactic nuclei, which is key to understanding supermassive black hole growth and evolution. The researchers extended an existing column density estimation technique — based on the ratio of observed X-ray to mid-infrared luminosity — from the local universe to higher redshifts, using a sample of bright AGN drawn from a hard X-ray survey catalog with a median redshift around a third. They applied X-ray spectral fitting with physically motivated models to constrain column densities and calibrate the luminosity ratio diagnostic at these greater distances. The high-redshift relationship was found to be broadly consistent with the low-redshift version, with modest parameter differences attributable to higher X-ray luminosities in the higher-redshift sample rather than genuine evolutionary change. Applying the calibrated method across the full catalog, they derived an observed Compton-thick fraction consistent with recent independent measurements from other hard X-ray surveys of the local universe.
items.citation: Ryan J. Turney, Claire L. Greenwell, David M. Alexander. Extending an X-ray & Mid-Infrared diagnostic for absorption in Active Galactic Nuclei to higher redshifts using NuSTAR and XMM-Newton. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates a specific failure mode in clinical language models where incomplete reasoning traces already contain the correct diagnosis before an answer is explicitly produced. The authors developed MamaReason, a model adapted from a large dense language model, and evaluated it on a maternal and child health benchmark consisting of paired clinical presentations. They employed an explicit-commitment extractor to identify diagnoses within failed reasoning passes, finding that the extracted commitments frequently matched the final answer produced by continuation across both reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning conditions. Crucially, simply reading the committed diagnosis from within the unfinished trace — without generating additional tokens — recovered a substantial portion of the cases restored by full continuation, suggesting that diagnostic content is often present in the trace before completion occurs. The paper argues that clinical language model evaluation must distinguish between diagnostic content already present in a reasoning trace, completion of an accepted answer, and overall paired diagnostic correctness, as these represent meaningfully different outcomes that only become separable when the same trace is examined through multiple readout strategies.
items.citation: Thanni Adewuyi, Adepoju Jeremiah Moyondafoluwa, Dorcas Amapu et al.. MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Compressible gas flow through porous media under forced pressure and fluxes: compressibility number and pressure curvature
items.summary: This paper investigates how gas compressibility shapes pressure evolution and transient behavior during flow through porous media under different types of boundary forcing. The authors analyze isothermal gas flow using the porous medium equation, nondimensionalized with a Péclet-type compressibility number that characterizes the degree of steady-state compression and allows direct comparison across inlet conditions controlling pressure, volumetric flux, or mass flux. They derive a semi-analytical perturbation series valid across all three forcing conditions and confirm it with numerical solutions spanning several orders of magnitude in the compressibility number, finding that the effective pressure-squared diffusivity transitions from boundary-condition-dependent plateau values at low compression to a power-law scaling at high compression, explained by the slowest eigenmode of the linearized system. To capture localized flow behavior, the authors introduce the pressure curvature and describe its dynamics through a nonlinear advection-diffusion-reaction equation, revealing that compression pulses migrate downstream and dissipate during relaxation, with curvature moments exposing a compressibility-dependent crossover between compression- and expansion-dominated transients. The framework is illustrated with applications to gas chromatography and underground hydrogen storage.
items.citation: A. F. Visentini, J. J. Hidalgo, M. Dentz. Compressible gas flow through porous media under forced pressure and fluxes: compressibility number and pressure curvature. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Positive Weights Do Not Certify TWFE Inference: A Design Diagnostic under Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity
items.summary: The paper examines whether positive treatment weights in two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) regressions are sufficient to guarantee valid inference under treatment-effect heterogeneity, arguing they are not. The authors develop a design-only diagnostic that quantifies the worst-case mean shift in the TWFE test statistic arising from local treatment-effect drift, expressed as a function of the discrepancy between actual and uniform treatment weights. To perform inference on this diagnostic, they propose two regular one-sided procedures—a reverse-triangle multiplier lower bound and a covariance-aware noncentral chi-squared inversion—that can either detect unsafe configurations or certify adequacy, since a debiased quadratic estimator of the shift is nonregular at zero. Applying the framework to several well-known empirical panels, they find that conventional inference remains uncertified even in cases where all treated-cell weights are positive, with the minimum-wage and property-tax applications failing certification while the castle-doctrine application passes under a restricted heterogeneity class. The diagnostic thus provides a formal basis for separating point correction, exposure uniformity, and statistically warranted certification of TWFE inference.
items.citation: Stanisław M. S. Halkiewicz. Positive Weights Do Not Certify TWFE Inference: A Design Diagnostic under Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: KnowVis: Dual-View Evaluation and Diagnosis of World-Knowledge Grounding in Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitation that text-to-image models, despite advances in visual realism and instruction following, struggle to ground implicit world knowledge, structured facts, and domain-specific commonsense in generated images. The authors developed KnowVis, a dual-view evaluation and diagnosis framework built on a hierarchical knowledge taxonomy with case-level annotations, combining two complementary benchmarks with a multimodal large language model-based visual question answering judge protocol. One benchmark supports fine-grained atomic knowledge evaluation through structured question answering, while the other examines open-ended knowledge composition using a combination of required, optional, and dynamically discovered knowledge expressions alongside human-judge collaboration. Experiments using KnowVis revealed substantial gaps in world-knowledge grounding across existing text-to-image models and demonstrated that the framework provides structured diagnostic signals capable of attributing errors to specific knowledge categories.
items.citation: Yonghang Yu, Ruoyu Wang, Haoyu Zhang et al.. KnowVis: Dual-View Evaluation and Diagnosis of World-Knowledge Grounding in Text-to-Image Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers in the Blood for Sepsis Diagnosis.
items.summary: This study addressed the critical need for early and accurate sepsis diagnosis in critically ill patients by using a multi-phase proteomics approach to discover and validate blood-based biomarkers. The researchers combined data-independent acquisition proteomics, targeted mass spectrometry verification, ELISA-based clinical confirmation, and machine learning across discovery, verification, and prospective cohorts. Three proteins — alpha-2-HS-glycoprotein, clusterin, and kallistatin — were consistently downregulated in sepsis patients and selected as candidate biomarkers. A random forest model built on this triple-biomarker panel demonstrated strong diagnostic performance in prospective testing, outperforming the conventional inflammatory markers procalcitonin and C-reactive protein. The authors conclude that this panel offers a rapid, accurate, and clinically translatable tool for early sepsis detection.
items.citation: Fan Z, Chen M, Sun Y et al.. Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers in the Blood for Sepsis Diagnosis.. Journal of proteome research. 2026

items.title: From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps
items.citation: Plata-Menchaca E, Hernández-Jiménez E. From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps. Frontiers in medical technology. 2026

items.title: Circulating calprotectin and S100A8/A9-related biomarkers for diagnosis and prognostic stratification in adult acute infection and sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether circulating calprotectin and related S100A8/A9 biomarkers can accurately diagnose acute infection and sepsis and stratify prognosis in adults. The researchers searched multiple biomedical databases and trial registries, pooling data from independent cohorts using random-effects models to estimate diagnostic and prognostic areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve, alongside bivariate analyses of sensitivity and specificity, with evidence quality assessed using established appraisal tools. Across the included cohorts, calprotectin and S100A8/A9 markers demonstrated only moderate overall diagnostic performance for both sepsis and infection-related outcomes, with considerable variability in sensitivity and specificity depending on the clinical context. Prognostic accuracy for mortality and survival was similarly moderate, and paired comparisons with other biomarkers did not establish clear superiority for calprotectin-based measures. The authors conclude that these biomarkers may serve as adjunctive indicators of host immune response in selected clinical contexts but that current evidence, rated as very low certainty, does not support their use as stand-alone diagnostic tools, universal decision thresholds, or replacements for established biomarkers and clinical evaluation.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Liao YS, Deng YP, Song JL et al.. Circulating calprotectin and S100A8/A9-related biomarkers for diagnosis and prognostic stratification in adult acute infection and sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Procalcitonin-Guided Antimicrobial Therapy: Current Evidence for Clinical Decision-Making and Practical Limitations
items.citation: Alshammari S, Alrawaili B, Alshammari R et al.. Procalcitonin-Guided Antimicrobial Therapy: Current Evidence for Clinical Decision-Making and Practical Limitations. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Procalcitonin as a Stewardship Checkpoint, Not an Antibiotic Gatekeeper: From Antibiotic Initiation to Discontinuation in Resource-Limited Hospitals.
items.summary: This paper examines the clinical role of procalcitonin as a biomarker within antimicrobial stewardship programs, with particular attention to how its utility varies depending on where it is applied along the antibiotic treatment pathway. The authors reviewed evidence on procalcitonin's performance both at the point of antibiotic initiation and during ongoing treatment, finding that its value for safely withholding antibiotics at the outset is limited, especially in patients with suspected sepsis or physiological instability. By contrast, serial procalcitonin measurements show more consistent benefit after empirical therapy has begun, supporting de-escalation, shorter treatment courses, and earlier discontinuation. The paper further argues that in resource-limited hospitals, introducing procalcitonin without the infrastructure for timely serial testing and structured antibiotic review may increase costs without meaningfully improving antibiotic use. The authors therefore propose that procalcitonin be used selectively as a reassessment checkpoint to guide discontinuation decisions in patients already receiving empirical antibiotics, rather than as a standalone gatekeeper for initiating treatment.
items.citation: Abdi DA, Yusuf AA, Hirsi AM et al.. Procalcitonin as a Stewardship Checkpoint, Not an Antibiotic Gatekeeper: From Antibiotic Initiation to Discontinuation in Resource-Limited Hospitals.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: Citrullinated Histone H3 and Myeloperoxidase are Associated with Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy (SIC) in Sepsis Patients but Fail to Predict 28-Day Mortality Among SIC Patients.
items.summary: This study investigated whether two neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-related biomarkers, citrullinated histone H3 and myeloperoxidase, could serve as clinically useful markers for sepsis-induced coagulopathy and subsequent mortality in sepsis patients. Using a single-center retrospective design, the researchers measured plasma levels of both biomarkers at hospital admission in adult sepsis patients, then assessed their association with coagulopathy occurrence and twenty-eight-day all-cause mortality. Both biomarkers were significantly elevated in patients who developed sepsis-induced coagulopathy compared to those who did not, and each independently predicted coagulopathy occurrence after adjusting for confounders, with moderate diagnostic accuracy. However, among patients who had already developed sepsis-induced coagulopathy, neither biomarker differed meaningfully between survivors and non-survivors, and neither independently predicted twenty-eight-day mortality. The findings suggest that circulating citrullinated histone H3 and myeloperoxidase reflect the inflammatory-coagulation crosstalk underlying sepsis-induced coagulopathy but lack prognostic utility for mortality once coagulopathy is established.
items.citation: Lai H, Zhong A, Liao W et al.. Citrullinated Histone H3 and Myeloperoxidase are Associated with Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy (SIC) in Sepsis Patients but Fail to Predict 28-Day Mortality Among SIC Patients.. International journal of general medicine. 2026

items.title: Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026)
items.summary: The Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction is a consensus document that updates the clinical and pathophysiological framework for defining, classifying, and diagnosing myocardial infarction. The document introduces a revised three-part clinical classification that distinguishes primary myocardial infarction arising from acute coronary pathology, secondary myocardial infarction resulting from myocardial supply-demand imbalance, and procedure-related myocardial infarction occurring as a complication of cardiac intervention or surgery. Updated diagnostic criteria incorporate cardiac troponin testing, electrocardiographic findings, and coronary or cardiac imaging, with refined thresholds for defining acute and chronic myocardial injury based on the ninety-ninth percentile upper reference limit. The classification is aligned with International Classification of Diseases coding and includes adapted diagnostic pathways for low-resource settings where biomarker testing and imaging may not be available. The document also addresses special clinical situations, implications for public health and research, and provides guidance on silent or unrecognized myocardial infarction, unstable angina, and myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries.
authors: ESC/ACC/AHA/WHF Universal Definition Document Advisory Group
items.venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
items.citation: Nicholas L. Mills, Laura Kristin Newby, Sarah J. Zaman et al.. Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026). Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2026

items.title: Quantum–Photonic Topological Intelligence for Multiscale Biomedicine: Brain Networks, Biosignals, Spatial Multi-Omics and Autonomous Therapeutics
items.summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework called Quantum–Photonic Topological Intelligence for Multiscale Biomedicine, designed to address the challenge of integrating heterogeneous biomedical data spanning multiple biological scales, including brain network dynamics, physiological signals, spatially resolved molecular measurements, and treatment response data. The authors developed a unified mathematical and conceptual architecture combining graph and simplicial representations, persistent topological descriptors, multimodal learning, hybrid quantum–photonic feature maps, and constrained therapeutic optimization across four coupled layers. The framework is entirely model-based and uses an illustrative numerical scoring scheme rather than real patient data, and explicitly does not claim empirical clinical superiority. The analysis suggests that the framework's value lies in disciplined multiscale coupling, whereby persistent topological representations, cross-modal fusion connecting electrophysiology with spatial molecular states, and governed optimization can together support constrained therapeutic decision-making. The authors call for future empirical work benchmarking the framework's components against matched datasets, prospective validation, fairness constraints, and clinically meaningful endpoints before any deployment claims are made.
items.venue: International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI)
items.citation: Murali Krishna Pasupuleti. Quantum–Photonic Topological Intelligence for Multiscale Biomedicine: Brain Networks, Biosignals, Spatial Multi-Omics and Autonomous Therapeutics. International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI). 2026

items.title: Detection of Chagas disease from the ECG: the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025
items.summary: The paper describes a machine learning challenge focused on detecting Chagas disease, a parasitic infection causing cardiomyopathy, using electrocardiogram data. Teams were invited to develop algorithms that could identify likely Chagas disease cases from a large collection of ECGs drawn from multiple Brazilian databases, framing the problem as a triage task aligned with regional serological testing capacity. The evaluation metric measured the true positive rate among the patients ranked most likely to have the disease by each algorithm, reflecting realistic clinical constraints. Key innovations included combining datasets with both weak and strong labels, data augmentation for generalizability, and development of an ensemble model that aggregated top-performing submissions. The challenge attracted a large international field of participants, and results showed that both individual top models and the ensemble approach achieved meaningful sensitivity at clinically relevant operating points, though performance varied across datasets.
items.citation: Matthew A. Reyna, Soheil Saghafi, Zuzana Koscova et al.. Detection of Chagas disease from the ECG: the George B. Moody PhysioNet Challenge 2025. Physiological Measurement. 2026

items.title: Objective Bayes Factor Based Model Selection for Zero-Inflated Microbiome Count Data Under Jeffreys Prior
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of selecting appropriate statistical models for microbiome count data, which is characterized by excess zeros and overdispersion arising from the complex relationships between microbial communities and disease, diet, genetics, and environmental factors. The authors developed a Bayes factor approach for model selection among negative binomial, Poisson, zero-inflated negative binomial, and zero-inflated Poisson distributions, using non-informative Jeffreys prior to maintain objectivity. The proposed method was evaluated through simulation studies and real data analysis, where it was compared against traditional model selection criteria including the Akaike information criterion and Vuong's test. The Bayes factor approach was found to outperform these conventional methods in both settings, suggesting it provides more reliable discrimination between competing count data models for microbiome applications. The authors also released a dedicated R package to make the methodology accessible for broader use in Bayesian model selection for zero-inflated microbiome data.
items.citation: Paramahansa Pramanik, Arnab K. Maity. Objective Bayes Factor Based Model Selection for Zero-Inflated Microbiome Count Data Under Jeffreys Prior. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research. 2026

items.title: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and the epitranscriptome: Advances in mapping native RNA landscapes
items.summary: This review examines nanopore direct RNA sequencing as a tool for studying the transcriptome and epitranscriptome, focusing on its capacity to analyze native RNA molecules without reverse transcription or amplification. The authors outline the biophysical principles of the technology and trace its development, comparing it against short-read RNA sequencing, long-read cDNA sequencing, and conventional RNA modification mapping approaches. A key emphasis is placed on the technology's ability to simultaneously capture RNA modifications, full-length transcript structures, alternative splicing, and poly-adenylation tail features within single molecules, offering an integrated regulatory view unavailable to competing methods. The review also surveys optimized experimental workflows for diverse RNA biotypes, state-of-the-art computational algorithms for modification detection and isoform quantification, and analytical pipelines for integrating multiple regulatory layers, while stressing the importance of benchmarking and orthogonal validation. Emerging applications discussed include resolving complex transcriptomes, characterizing coordinated epitranscriptomic regulation, identifying disease-associated RNA signatures, and future deployment in precision medicine and broader biological research.
items.citation: Tianyuan Zhang, Jia Li, Chao Tang et al.. Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and the epitranscriptome: Advances in mapping native RNA landscapes. iMeta. 2026

items.title: Benchmarking AI Agents for Addressing Scientific Challenges Across Scales
items.summary: This paper addresses the gap between the growing use of AI agents for scientific discovery and the lack of realistic benchmarks for evaluating their capabilities. The authors developed SciAgentArena, a benchmark comprising approximately two hundred tasks drawn from real-world scientific research scenarios across multiple domains, featuring stepwise verification and an interactive environment compatible with diverse AI agents. Evaluating current agents with this framework revealed that they perform reasonably well on structured data-analysis workflows with clear task definitions and evaluation criteria, but struggle with generating novel insights, sustaining self-directed exploration, and tackling open-ended research questions. The study also characterizes recurring failure modes and identifies directions for improving agent reliability, autonomy, and scientific reasoning. Overall, SciAgentArena is proposed as a practical framework for tracking progress in AI agents for science and guiding the development of more capable future systems.
items.citation: Tianyu Liu, A F Wang, Antonia Panescu et al.. Benchmarking AI Agents for Addressing Scientific Challenges Across Scales. arXiv (Cornell University). 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of monitoring maritime activity by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which provides vessel identification but has known vulnerabilities including intentional manipulation, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships on their own. Following a structured data science methodology, the authors developed a Pair Hidden Markov Model to align individual radio frequency detections with AIS vessel trajectories by jointly modeling temporal and spatial information along with noise and timing discrepancies. The approach was evaluated on real AIS data combined with synthetic radio frequency detections, benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baselines, and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and the spatial distance between the two data sources. A log-odds formulation that contrasts the full matching model against a null model substantially improved precision and the ability to detect vessels behaving covertly, though a simple time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without any model fitting still outperformed the probabilistic approach. The study concludes that the single-detection Pair Hidden Markov Model formulation approaches but does not surpass the hand-designed baseline, while identifying remaining biases that future work would need to address.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: This paper investigates whether recent hints of non-standard cosmological expansion are accompanied by modifications to how gravity behaves, going beyond a simple dark energy equation-of-state analysis. The authors perform a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density and two gravitational response functions governing matter clustering and lensing, using a combination of CMB, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation, supernova, and large-scale structure data. A persistent feature emerges in the dark energy density at intermediate redshifts, corresponding to a crossing of the phantom divide, and this feature is robust across different data combinations and whether or not gravitational modifications are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response functions show suggestive but less significant enhancements over a similar redshift range, though including large-scale structure data shifts the lensing response toward values below the standard expectation. The authors conclude that current departures from the standard cosmological model are most clearly manifested in the expansion history, while correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics remain possible but await confirmation from next-generation surveys.
items.citation: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri. Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigates how convolutional neural networks exploit background contextual information when classifying agricultural images, and whether a technique called Concept Induction can reveal what hidden neurons represent when processing such context-dominated patches. The researchers applied this approach across five agricultural datasets exhibiting varying degrees of contextual bias, examining four CNN architectures at multiple network depths and patch locations, with image descriptors encoded in a knowledge graph serving as background knowledge for deriving logical characterizations of neuron activations. They found that roughly a quarter of tested neuron-feature pairs were statistically validated, with validation occurring most frequently at intermediate network depths and being most strongly associated with edge, Gabor, and Tamura texture features. Notably, the degree of contextual bias in a dataset did not predict how interpretable its hidden-neuron activations were, as a moderately biased dataset yielded the highest validation rate while the most biased dataset yielded the lowest. The authors conclude that behavioral context dependence and the semantic interpretability of hidden neurons reflect distinct aspects of CNN behavior, and that Concept Induction offers a complementary lens for understanding bias beyond classification accuracy alone.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
items.summary: This paper introduces KELP, a Lagrangian particle tracking tool designed to follow virtual particles through ocean model velocity fields in order to study transport pathways, connectivity, and dispersion. The software supports unstructured ocean meshes with triangular, quadrilateral, and mixed elements, as well as HEALPix equal-area grids used by kilometre-scale digital twin ocean models, and computes both two- and three-dimensional trajectories. A central design goal is compatibility with coding agents driven by language models, and the paper demonstrates that structured task instructions called skills substantially improved the completeness of study setups generated by multiple language models. KELP's results were validated against two independent trackers and trajectories computed on HEALPix grids were shown to converge toward those on the native model mesh as pixel resolution increased, supporting the use of HEALPix output for ensemble Lagrangian statistics when the original mesh is unavailable. The tool demonstrated practical scalability through a multi-decade simulation tracking millions of particles in the Beaufort Gyre and a stress test involving tens of billions of particles on a high-resolution HEALPix mesh.
items.citation: Ivan Kuznetsov, Alexey Androsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin et al.. KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world object detection scenarios, framing each detected bounding box decision as a hypothesis test where the null hypothesis assumes the box contains an in-distribution object. The authors identify that the null distribution over box scores varies meaningfully with box size and contact with image borders, and that conventional approaches obscure this by pooling all boxes together. To exploit this structure, they propose PLUM, a training-free scoring method that extracts features from the last backbone stage before class-specific layers, then ranks a box's distance to in-distribution classes only against boxes sharing the same size and border-contact properties. This conditioning provides distribution-free false-alarm rate bounds per box stratum and preserves feature information that class-specific layers would otherwise discard. The method achieves leading out-of-distribution detection performance on standard benchmarks without requiring external models or additional training.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
items.summary: The paper investigates numerical instability problems that arise when computing divergences between categorical distributions that are nearly identical. Building on prior work identifying similar issues in softmax and soft cross-entropy operations, the authors demonstrate that forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence, generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence, Monte Carlo KL estimates, and entropy all suffer from rounding and cancellation errors under these conditions, affecting both forward computations and gradient calculations. These instabilities have practical consequences in machine learning workflows that rely on divergences as optimization objectives, including knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal optimization methods. The authors derive numerically stable reformulations for each case and provide concrete implementations validated through property-based testing.
items.citation: Brandon Amos. On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.
items.summary: This study examined the diagnostic performance of three approaches for evaluating bloodstream infections in a setting with high antimicrobial resistance burden: a commercial syndromic multiplex PCR panel, metagenomic next-generation sequencing performed directly from positive blood cultures, and conventional phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing. The researchers retrospectively compared these methods across a large series of positive blood-culture episodes from patients at a tertiary-care center. Metagenomic sequencing recovered the full set of organisms identified by routine culture more completely than the multiplex panel and detected off-panel carbapenem resistance genes, particularly an oxacillinase variant in *Acinetobacter baumannii*, that accounted for false-susceptible results on the targeted panel. Neither platform demonstrated statistically significant superiority for predicting meropenem or ceftriaxone resistance, and broader genomic detection did not consistently translate into improved phenotypic resistance prediction. The authors conclude that syndromic panels and metagenomic sequencing have complementary strengths in organism and resistance-mechanism coverage, while phenotypic susceptibility testing remains indispensable for definitive clinical guidance.
items.citation: Nitayanon P, Phoonthong S, Peizner MT et al.. Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Pathogen identification and resistance gene expression tests using ASTar remnant bacterial suspension in gram-negative contrived positive blood cultures.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether remnant bacterial suspension produced during routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing on the ASTar System could be repurposed for simultaneous pathogen identification and resistance gene detection, thereby streamlining diagnostic workflows for bloodstream infections. Gram-negative bacterial strains from multiple curated reference collections were contrived into blood culture bottles, processed through the ASTar System, and the remnant suspensions were analyzed using mass spectrometry for identification and lateral flow assays for detection of clinically important resistance mechanisms including extended-spectrum beta-lactamases and carbapenemases. All samples yielded high-confidence mass spectrometry identification scores, and lateral flow assay results showed complete or near-complete agreement with reference isolate characterization for all targeted resistance markers. Reflex testing workflows triggered by ASTar phenotypic results did not compromise lateral flow assay performance, and the approach could deliver identification and resistance detection results within approximately one to two hours of instrument initiation. The authors conclude that this integrated approach reduces duplicate sample handling, may enable earlier susceptibility reporting compared to current fragmented workflows, and offers potential cost savings relative to commercial multiplex polymerase chain reaction platforms.
items.citation: Gupta V, Myers M, Niklasson I et al.. Pathogen identification and resistance gene expression tests using ASTar remnant bacterial suspension in gram-negative contrived positive blood cultures.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: From empirical to targeted therapy: A comprehensive review of clinical microbiological diagnostics for urinary tract infections.
items.summary: This review examines the full clinical microbiological diagnostic workflow for urinary tract infections, a globally prevalent bacterial infection increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance and high recurrence.
