The authors systematically describe the sequential steps from specimen collection and traditional culture-based methods through modern identification technologies such as mass spectrometry and multilocus sequence typing. They also survey the range of antimicrobial susceptibility testing approaches, from broth microdilution and automated systems to molecular methods including multiplex polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing for genotypic resistance detection. The review argues that combining conventional phenotypic testing with rapid molecular diagnostics creates a practical clinical framework for accelerating the shift from empirical to targeted antibiotic therapy. The authors conclude that integrating genotypic and phenotypic data, alongside systematic diagnostic pipelines, strengthens antimicrobial stewardship programs and supports precision medicine in managing urinary tract infections amid rising multidrug resistance.
items.citation: Kim JA, Kim JH. From empirical to targeted therapy: A comprehensive review of clinical microbiological diagnostics for urinary tract infections.. Investigative and clinical urology. 2026

items.title: Endolysins for precision antimicrobial therapy and rapid bacterial detection: translational challenges and future directions.
items.summary: This review examines bacteriophage-derived endolysins as dual-purpose tools to address the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance, covering both their therapeutic potential and their utility in rapid bacterial detection. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how these peptidoglycan-degrading enzymes achieve bacteriolytic activity with high target specificity, and how derived structural domains such as cell wall-binding domains and receptor-binding proteins can serve as precise recognition molecules in clinical and food safety diagnostics. The review identifies key translational obstacles, including difficulties in protein expression, stability, formulation, and large-scale production, with particular emphasis on how the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria restricts endolysin access to its peptidoglycan target. Recent progress in protein engineering, membrane-permeabilization strategies, and novel delivery systems is discussed as promising means of overcoming these barriers. The authors conclude that engineered endolysins hold considerable future promise as precision antimicrobials and diagnostic agents against resistant bacterial pathogens, provided remaining translational challenges can be resolved.
items.citation: Khan FM, Zourob M. Endolysins for precision antimicrobial therapy and rapid bacterial detection: translational challenges and future directions.. Frontiers in pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside
items.citation: Mugisha N, Fawaz L, Noureddine R et al.. Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside. Health science reports. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study examined whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antimicrobial stewardship and patient outcomes compared to conventional antibiotic susceptibility testing alone. Conducted at a hospital in Pakistan, the study enrolled adult patients with suspected bacterial infections and measured outcomes including time to effective therapy, antibiotic appropriateness, hospital length of stay, and mortality. The integrated approach dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and to initiation of effective therapy, and substantially increased the proportion of patients receiving appropriate antibiotics while reducing broad-spectrum antibiotic use. These improvements were accompanied by shorter hospital stays and lower mortality rates in patients managed with the integrated strategy. The AI model showed strong discriminative performance, and genotypic and phenotypic resistance profiles showed substantial concordance, supporting the potential of this combined approach as a scalable, cost-effective strategy for combating antimicrobial resistance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Distributional Policy Evaluation for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects, Social Equity and Climate-Transition Governance
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental limitation in climate policy evaluation: relying on average treatment effects can obscure how the burdens and benefits of climate-transition policies are distributed across vulnerable populations, carbon-dependent workers, and low-income households. The authors develop a comprehensive framework called D-PECT that integrates heterogeneous treatment effects, quantile and distributional methods, doubly robust causal learning, and equity-sensitive welfare optimization alongside emissions effectiveness and governance quality indicators. The framework is formalized through potential-outcome equations, dynamic transition-state models, and a constrained social-welfare optimization with a risk-adjusted master objective. Using a pedagogical numerical demonstration, the authors show that an adaptive, targeted policy package scores notably higher on an integrated resilience metric than an untargeted benchmark, and that policy rankings can reverse entirely when the evaluation objective shifts from average welfare to lower-tail protection. The paper concludes that compensation schemes gain credibility when tied to estimated exposure and treatment response rather than income alone, and offers the framework as a tool for governments and institutions seeking climate action that is causally rigorous, distributionally transparent, and institutionally governable.
items.venue: International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI)
items.citation: Murali Krishna Pasupuleti. Distributional Policy Evaluation for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects, Social Equity and Climate-Transition Governance. International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI). 2026

items.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated whether internalized reasoning models and externalized agent-based frameworks represent competing or complementary approaches to complex medical reasoning tasks. The researchers developed MedicalAgentsBench, a curated benchmark of challenging clinical questions drawn from multiple medical datasets using difficulty-aware selection and contamination screening. They systematically evaluated a range of internalized reasoning models, standard base models, and externalized multi-agent scaffolding methods across this benchmark. The key finding is that both approaches independently improve performance and their benefits are additive, with the best results achieved by combining agent workflows on top of an internalized reasoning model. Additionally, Pareto analysis revealed that this combined approach dominates on the cost-performance frontier, while lightweight optimization on less expensive models provides a viable path for resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Yanjun Shao, Xiangru Tang, Jiwoong Sohn et al.. MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks. Patterns. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how multiomics approaches—including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling—generate deep insights into disease mechanisms, while AI methods such as deep learning extract meaningful patterns from these complex biological datasets. The paper covers applications across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The review highlights disease areas such as oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions as illustrative contexts where these combined approaches show particular promise. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges, including data harmonization across disparate omics streams, reproducibility concerns, and the need to address algorithmic biases, while arguing that the convergence of these technologies heralds a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
items.citation: Avina Vongpradith, Regina-Mae Villanueva Dominguez, Lorainne Tudor Car et al.. Global burden of enteric infectious diseases, diarrhoeal diseases, and corresponding aetiologies, 1990–2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023. The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Generative AI-enabled clinical decision support system in primary care: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial
items.summary: This study investigated whether a large language model integrated into an electronic medical record system could improve clinical outcomes in real-world primary care settings in Kenya. Using a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial design, clinical officers at primary care facilities were assigned to either use the LLM-assisted decision support tool or standard electronic medical records, with the primary outcome being expert-adjudicated treatment failure within fourteen days of patient enrollment. Nearly ten thousand patients were enrolled across the two arms, making this one of the larger real-world trials of generative AI clinical decision support in a low-resource context. Treatment failure rates were similar between the intervention and control groups, with the difference not reaching statistical significance, and no safety signals were identified. The investigators concluded that while LLM assistance appeared safe, it did not significantly reduce treatment failures, and any clinical benefit, if it exists, is likely to be modest.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Vaishnavi Menon et al.. Generative AI-enabled clinical decision support system in primary care: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial-laden PerOssal beads display in vitro inhibition and killing of extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria associated with conflict wounds in Ukraine
items.summary: This study investigated the potential of locally delivered antimicrobials to combat extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria commonly found in conflict-related wounds, particularly open fractures from the war in Ukraine. The researchers tested antimicrobial-laden PerOssal hydroxyapatite and calcium sulphate beads against clinical bacterial isolates using zone-of-inhibition testing and time-kill analysis. The bacterial isolates showed resistance to multiple standard antimicrobials including gentamicin, tobramycin, and ciprofloxacin at concentrations exceeding established susceptibility breakpoints, and beads loaded with single agents such as gentamicin or cefazolin showed only weak inhibitory activity. However, beads combining gentamicin with rifampicin achieved consistent broad-spectrum bacterial inhibition and killing, and co-amoxiclav-loaded beads also inhibited all tested strains. The findings suggest that local antimicrobial delivery via these beads may help reduce infection risk in heavily contaminated open fractures when surgical wound excision is delayed, with potential applications in both conflict and civilian disaster settings, though in vivo validation is still needed.
items.citation: Henry Adam Claireaux, Edward J. A. Douglas, Scott J C Pallett et al.. Antimicrobial-laden PerOssal beads display in vitro inhibition and killing of extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria associated with conflict wounds in Ukraine. Bone and Joint Research. 2026

items.title: Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass
items.summary: This paper investigated the suitability of a commercially available, back-illuminated CMOS image sensor for use in space-based soft X-ray observatories. The researchers measured the quantum efficiency of the sensor across the soft X-ray bandpass using a synchrotron beamline facility, supplementing these measurements with microscopy of the sensor's physical layer structure to constrain a quantum efficiency model. The sensor was found to achieve quantum efficiency in the range of roughly ten to forty percent across the tested energy band. The results affirm this low-cost sensor's potential for deployment in affordable X-ray observatories, while also identifying design improvements — specifically the removal of microlenses and the use of deeper silicon depletion layers — that would enhance performance in future commercial X-ray CMOS sensors.
items.citation: Casey T. DeRoo, Mallory Weber, Carson Bantz et al.. Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Deterministic ECDSA on secp256k1: the RFC 6979 assumption, a counterexample, and the state of deployed implementations
items.summary: This paper examines the security foundations of RFC 6979, the standard for deterministic ECDSA nonce generation, which derives the signing nonce by keying HMAC-DRBG with the private signing key. The authors isolate the precise security assumption required, which they call A*, showing it is distinct from and not equivalent to standard pseudorandom function security or auxiliary-input PRF security, and they construct explicit counterexamples demonstrating these separations in both directions. They prove that A* follows tightly from the discrete logarithm problem when an ideal compression function is assumed and a randomized signing oracle is available, and they show that using a nonce key independent of the private key would eliminate the assumption entirely. An empirical audit of secp256k1 implementations reveals that the vast majority sign deterministically without added entropy, and that a deviation from the specification present in an early version of libsecp256k1 persists in several actively used cryptocurrency libraries. Additional findings include quantitative bounds on how close the HMAC input block is to uniformly distributed across several standard curves, unconditional bounds on the Fourier coefficients of the low-R grinding nonce set, and test vectors for an undertested branch of the nonce generation procedure.
items.citation: Ilia Prosianoi. Deterministic ECDSA on secp256k1: the RFC 6979 assumption, a counterexample, and the state of deployed implementations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Convergence rate of observables in the Marcus-Lushnikov process toward Smoluchowski with singular homogeneous kernels
items.summary: The paper studies how well the Marcus-Lushnikov stochastic particle system approximates the deterministic Smoluchowski coagulation equation when the coagulation kernel is singular at the origin, specifically for the family of kernels that blow up as particle size approaches zero. For regular mean-field systems, weak errors for smooth observables of the empirical measure are generically expected to be of order one over the number of particles, and the central question is whether this favorable scaling survives when the kernel singularity creates analytical difficulties near zero cluster size. The authors prove that the weak error of order one over particle number is indeed preserved on finite time intervals for a suitable class of nonlinear functionals of the empirical measure. The key insight is that the singularity is self-regularizing: small clusters coagulate at very high rates, causing rapid escape from the dangerous region near zero and generating exponential moments in the singular variable. To make this precise, the authors develop a Wasserstein-type distance adapted to the singular variable together with weighted total variation estimates that allow them to control derivatives of the Smoluchowski flow.
items.citation: R{é}mi Catellier, Sebastian Baudelet-Aponte Garcia. Convergence rate of observables in the Marcus-Lushnikov process toward Smoluchowski with singular homogeneous kernels. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantized resistance limitations for graphene p-n junction devices
items.summary: This paper investigated the feasibility of using graphene p-n junction devices to achieve quantized Hall resistance values beyond those readily available from standard epitaxial graphene. The researchers examined multiple device geometries — rectangular, Corbino, and triangular — by developing an automated Landauer-Büttiker solver in Python to map the relationship between device topology and effective resistance, since this mapping is mathematically degenerate and not straightforwardly invertible. The computational approach was validated against cryogenic multi-terminal transport measurements and circuit simulations. By applying Shannon entropy analysis to quantify the diversity of accessible resistance states, the study found that rectangular checkerboard configurations offer the greatest topological complexity and range of tunable outputs, while Corbino geometries are severely limited in the resistance values they can produce.
items.citation: Tamar M. Padwa, DaVonne Henry, Dominick S. Scaletta et al.. Quantized resistance limitations for graphene p-n junction devices. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023
items.summary: This study investigates the evolving surface magnetic field and starspot configuration of the young solar analogue V889 Her using Zeeman-Doppler imaging over a multi-year observational campaign. Spectropolarimetric observations were obtained with the SOFIN instrument at the Nordic Optical Telescope, and differential rotation parameters previously reported for this star were tested within the imaging framework. The analysis reveals significant temporal changes in the radial magnetic field near the rotational pole, including a full polarity reversal around 2021, alongside a persistently strong azimuthal field component at high latitudes. Abrupt reconfigurations of the spot distribution were detected on timescales of approximately one week in 2018, confirming earlier reports of rapid surface evolution that complicate differential rotation measurements. The observations favor solar-type differential rotation, and no clear link could be established between the long-term spot activity and the observed changes in large-scale magnetic field topology.
items.citation: Thomas Hackman, Jyri J. Lehtinen, Oleg Kochukhov et al.. Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Kronecker Approximations of Covariance Matrices for Solving Inverse Problems
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of handling large prior covariance matrices in Bayesian inverse problems, which arise when recovering unknown parameters from indirect or noisy observations. The authors developed approximations of large covariance matrices using structured Kronecker-Toeplitz products, exploiting the Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block structure of covariance kernels to create compact representations that are substantially cheaper to store and invert than the full matrices. These approximations were incorporated as prior covariance surrogates within generalized hybrid iterative methods for solving Bayesian inverse problems. The proposed Kronecker-Toeplitz approximation was shown to achieve lower relative approximation error than existing matrix approximation approaches, with rapid error decay as rank increases, and enables efficient matrix-vector products. The practical utility of the method was demonstrated through applications to two-dimensional seismic tomography reconstruction.
items.citation: Srijon Sarkar, Julianne Chung. Kronecker Approximations of Covariance Matrices for Solving Inverse Problems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Why Sensors Fail in Biological Samples: Fouling, Blocking, Matrix Effects and Prevention Solutions
items.summary: This review paper examines why sensors and biosensors fail when deployed in complex biological fluids such as blood, serum, plasma, and sweat, focusing on the interconnected problems of surface fouling, interface blocking, and matrix interference. The authors provide a mechanistic analysis of how phenomena including protein adsorption, nonspecific binding, ionic strength variations, pH fluctuations, and electroactive interferents degrade sensor performance, leading to signal drift, reduced sensitivity, false-positive responses, and shortened operational lifetimes. The review systematically compares how these failure modes affect different sensing platforms, including electrochemical, optical, capacitive, potentiometric, and wearable biosensors, as well as field-effect transistors. A substantial portion of the work catalogues practical mitigation strategies already applied in real sensing systems, spanning antifouling surface coatings, zwitterionic and hydrogel interfaces, blocking agents, membrane engineering, microfluidic sample pre-treatment, and artificial intelligence-assisted drift correction. The paper ultimately synthesizes advances across materials science, surface chemistry, and signal processing to offer guidance for developing more stable, reliable biosensors suitable for point-of-care biomarker analysis.
items.citation: Nikola Lenar, Beata Paczosa‐Bator. Why Sensors Fail in Biological Samples: Fouling, Blocking, Matrix Effects and Prevention Solutions. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Transforming Diagnostic Precision in Periodontology Through Lab-on-a-Chip Technology: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: This scoping review examined the state of evidence for lab-on-a-chip and microfluidic technologies as point-of-care diagnostic tools for periodontal and peri-implant disease, addressing the limitation that conventional periodontal diagnostics reflects past damage rather than active disease. Following established scoping review methodology, the authors searched multiple electronic databases and screened records for studies involving biosensor platforms, microfluidic systems, or lab-on-a-chip devices targeting periodontal tissues or relevant biomarkers. A small subset of identified records met inclusion criteria, revealing that saliva was the predominant sample matrix and that platforms ranged from paper-based microfluidics to electrochemical biosensors and PCR chips, most targeting key periodontal pathogens or inflammatory markers such as matrix metalloproteinase-8 and interleukin-1 beta. The review found that clinical diagnostic accuracy was rarely reported, validation was predominantly conducted under controlled laboratory rather than clinical conditions, and the majority of devices remained at the prototype stage. The authors conclude that while these technologies demonstrate analytical promise, widespread clinical adoption requires multicentric clinical validation, standardized fabrication protocols, and clearer regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Manoj M, Jaison J, Varghese J. Transforming Diagnostic Precision in Periodontology Through Lab-on-a-Chip Technology: A Scoping Review.. International journal of dentistry. 2026

items.title: Microfluidic Biosensors for the Detection of Foodborne Pathogens: A Comprehensive Review.
items.summary: This review examines the current state of microfluidic biosensors designed to detect foodborne pathogens in complex food matrices. The authors systematically compare these platforms across multiple dimensions, including substrate materials, fabrication approaches, sample handling strategies, and detection modalities spanning optical, electrochemical, and nucleic-acid-based readouts. While published studies show that rapid pathogen detection is achievable in controlled settings, the review highlights that reported performance metrics are rarely comparable across studies due to inconsistent reporting of matrices, enrichment steps, and assay conditions. The authors identify key translational barriers including reproducible manufacturing, reagent stability, and the lack of integrated sample-to-answer workflows validated in authentic food environments. They conclude that emerging approaches such as CRISPR-based assays and AI-assisted interpretation are promising but require rigorous direct comparison and independent validation, and that future work must address matrix-specific performance, multi-site robustness, usability, cost, and regulatory compliance before commercial deployment can be justified.
items.citation: Mao W, Zhang L. Microfluidic Biosensors for the Detection of Foodborne Pathogens: A Comprehensive Review.. Food science & nutrition. 2026

items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review paper examines the state of wearable and implantable microfluidic systems and their pathway toward clinical use in personalized medicine. The authors argue that existing literature treats materials chemistry and device fabrication in isolation, and so they construct a unified, translation-focused framework spanning foundational biomaterials, fabrication techniques, and diagnostic performance benchmarking through to closed-loop theranostic platforms that combine sensing with autonomous therapy. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence across sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular signal decoding, and on-device decision-making, which together enable a shift from passive health monitoring toward adaptive therapeutic intervention. The review critically identifies socio-technical barriers to clinical translation, particularly how heterogeneity in biofluid data and disparities in population baselines can propagate algorithmic bias into deployed systems. The authors conclude that robust hardware interfaces, standardized validation benchmarks, and alignment with regulatory frameworks are necessary prerequisites for equitable and responsible deployment of these technologies in digital health.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Toward self-driving laboratory 2.0 for chemistry and materials discovery
items.summary: This review examines the evolution of self-driving laboratories (SDLs) — autonomous platforms that design, execute, and analyze scientific experiments with minimal human input — and proposes a framework for a next-generation architecture termed SDL 2.0. The authors identify key limitations of earlier SDL systems, including narrow scope, poor interoperability, and dependence on human-curated heuristics, and use these shortcomings to motivate a more ambitious vision. The review surveys recent advances in modular hardware, AI-driven decision-making approaches such as Bayesian optimization and large language models, and orchestration software that integrates scheduling, data management, and safety protocols. From these developments, the authors derive six defining characteristics for SDL 2.0 — interoperable, collaborative, generalizable, orchestrated, safe, and creative — envisioning globally networked platforms that enable reproducible and accelerated discovery in chemistry and materials science. The paper ultimately argues that embedding modularity, AI reasoning, and community-driven standards into SDL infrastructure will not only transform how experiments are conducted but also broaden participation in and access to advanced scientific research.
items.citation: Heeseung Lee, Hyuk Jun Yoo, Hye Su Jang et al.. Toward self-driving laboratory 2.0 for chemistry and materials discovery. Materials Horizons. 2026

items.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
items.summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma presents a paradox in which cancer cells thrive despite a dense, poorly vascularized stroma that should limit nutrient delivery. This study investigated how cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) supply essential lipids, including cholesterol, to pancreatic cancer cells within this challenging microenvironment. The researchers discovered that cancer cells form synapse-like contacts with CAFs, triggering calcium influx through Orai channels in the fibroblasts, which activates the phospholipid scramblase ANO6 and causes phosphatidylserine exposure on CAF membranes, thereby initiating trogocytosis—a process by which cancer cells bite off and internalize fragments of CAF plasma membranes loaded with lipids acquired from blood-borne particles. This ANO6-dependent phosphatidylserine externalization additionally enables CAFs to suppress cytotoxic T cell activity through trogocytosis, linking the same molecular mechanism to both metabolic support and immune evasion. Blocking ANO6 impaired tumor growth by disrupting cholesterol delivery to cancer cells and reduced immunosuppression, identifying ANO6 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
items.citation: Charline Ogier, Charles Solomon Akino Mercy, Elena Bondarenko et al.. ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression. Nature Cancer. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: This review examines the development of ferrite-based nanomaterials for biomedical applications, tracing their evolution from basic magnetic contrast agents into multifunctional therapeutic platforms. The authors critically analyze how atomic-level engineering approaches, including cation distribution, defect modulation, and morphological anisotropy, can be used to tune magnetic, catalytic, and heating properties in spinel and hexagonal ferrite systems. Beyond established uses in magnetic resonance imaging and drug delivery, the review highlights emerging applications such as viscosity-independent magnetic hyperthermia, reactive oxygen species-driven antimicrobial therapy, and magnetic tissue engineering. A central focus is the translational gap between laboratory performance and clinical use, with the authors identifying key barriers including discrepancies between colloidal and intracellular heating efficiency, protein corona complexity, and challenges in scalable, regulatory-compliant manufacturing. The review concludes by proposing a roadmap that integrates artificial intelligence-driven material discovery and green chemistry to advance next-generation magnetotheranostic systems for precision medicine.
items.citation: Pramod D. Mhase, Varsha C. Pujari, Akash V. Fulari et al.. Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with attention to both European and global frameworks. The authors analyze how the acellular nature of extracellular vesicles causes them to fit imperfectly into existing regulatory categories, including a recent European guideline clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside advanced therapy medicinal product definitions, while other jurisdictions such as the United States regulate them as drugs and biological products under distinct criteria. By critically reviewing regulatory, technical, safety, and ethical considerations across multiple regions, the paper identifies key operational challenges including inconsistent classification criteria, undefined critical quality attributes, and unresolved comparability standards that complicate cross-regional clinical development. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle products can be advanced within existing medicinal product frameworks provided regulatory tools are applied consistently and current ambiguities are systematically addressed. The review is intended to support dialogue among international regulatory agencies and scientific societies to promote methodological convergence and move extracellular vesicle therapies toward safe and internationally credible clinical application.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)/polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): current and future trends
items.summary: This review examines polycystic ovary syndrome, described as the most common endocrinologic disorder affecting women, with particular focus on the gaps in understanding that have complicated diagnosis and management. The authors synthesize current knowledge of the disease's pathophysiology from a translational perspective, covering proposed mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. The paper evaluates existing diagnostic criteria and current treatment strategies, while also addressing the long-term health consequences associated with the condition. The authors conclude by identifying future research directions and highlighting areas where scientific understanding remains insufficient for this frequently overlooked disorder.
items.citation: Jessica L. Chan, Irene Masini, Margareta Danuta Pisarska. Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)/polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): current and future trends. Journal of Clinical Investigation. 2026

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of deploying brain-to-text speech neuroprostheses in real-world settings, where current systems rely on computationally intensive language models that produce high and variable inference latencies. The authors developed FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end decoding framework that repurposes automatic speech recognition model architectures to translate intracortical neural activity directly into text with greater efficiency. When evaluated on publicly available data from a neuroprosthesis user, the framework achieved low word error rates and, crucially, ran successfully on a commercially available mobile device at speeds far exceeding real-time demands. The system also demonstrated the ability to adapt to neural signal drift across recording sessions through fine-tuning, and gradient-based saliency maps revealed that the neural features driving decoding align with established physiological knowledge. These results collectively demonstrate that portable, low-latency brain-to-text communication is achievable outside of laboratory infrastructure.
items.citation: Jonathan D. McCart, Pranav I. Deevi, Mehdi Azabou et al.. FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency
items.summary: This paper investigates how the placement and penetration level of grid-forming inverters within a power network affect frequency stability, distinguishing between local bus-level and aggregate system-wide frequency metrics. Using an exhaustive search across all possible assignments of synchronous generators and droop-controlled grid-forming inverters in the IEEE 39-bus test system, the authors evaluated frequency nadir and rate of change of frequency under load disturbances applied at every eligible bus. The results show that at a fixed grid-forming inverter penetration level, placement choices alone produce substantial variation in worst-case local frequency nadir and maximum local rate of change of frequency. Critically, aggregate frequency assessment dramatically underrepresents this variation, masking nearly all of the placement-dependent differences visible in local frequency metrics. The authors conclude that relying solely on aggregate frequency measures may conceal both beneficial and harmful effects of inverter placement on local frequency performance.
items.citation: Fatma Alfailkawi, Marena Trujillo, Bri-Mathias Hodge. Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
items.summary: This paper investigates whether boson sampling machines can be used to model the time evolution of complex nonlinear dynamical systems relevant to fluid dynamics. The researchers extended the existing scattershot boson sampling framework by incorporating higher photon number components — a scheme they call bright scattershot boson sampling — which overcomes scaling limitations by making use of all randomly generated input photon number distributions rather than discarding them. Using a digital twin of the proposed architecture, they demonstrated that the photonic approach accurately reproduces the temporal dynamics of both a Lorenz-type model of two-dimensional thermally driven convection and a higher-dimensional model of global atmospheric circulation. The scheme proved resilient to substantial photon losses and outperformed both coherent light implementations and a classical reservoir-computing model of equivalent query complexity in terms of prediction horizon. These findings suggest that near-term, noisy intermediate-scale photonic quantum devices hold practical promise for simulating real-world complex systems.
items.citation: Robert Schade, Shailendra K. Rathor, Tim J. Bartley et al.. Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
items.summary: The paper addresses the quantum marginal problem—determining whether a set of local reduced states is consistent with some global quantum state—specifically for qubit systems. The authors establish a mathematical connection between qubit representability and the well-developed representability theory of fermionic systems by encoding each qubit as a single fermion distributed across two orbitals. Through this mapping, they prove that valid qubit marginals correspond to an exposed face of the set of representable fermionic reduced density matrices, characterized by the vanishing of site-occupation variance, allowing the full hierarchy of fermionic representability conditions to transfer directly to qubits. Testing these conditions on frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings demonstrates that low-level positivity conditions are either exact at a known analytical point or accurate to within a fraction of a percent near criticality. Beyond ground-state physics, the authors argue that their framework can also be applied to mitigate measurement errors on qubit-based quantum hardware.
items.citation: David A. Mazziotti. Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tessa: Encoding Classical Data Across an Entire Quantum Processor
items.summary: This paper introduces Tessa, a hardware-aware encoding scheme designed to store classical data across an entire quantum processor by distributing address and data qubits in a checkerboard pattern across the device's coupling graph. The approach extends prior methods by ensuring that neighboring data qubits share only a subset of address qubits, which eliminates the need for SWAP gates or routing when the native coupling graph is used, though the scheme generalizes to any bipartite coupling graph. The number of measurement shots required for readout scales with the local coupling degree of the device rather than the full system size. The scheme was experimentally validated on real quantum hardware, successfully encoding and decoding large numbers of real values representing diverse data types including images, audio, genetic sequences, and protein sequences.
items.citation: Daniel Bultrini. Tessa: Encoding Classical Data Across an Entire Quantum Processor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Toward On-Device Markerless 6DoF Tracking of a Physical Manipulative on a Mixed-Reality Headset: A Preliminary Study
items.summary: This paper investigates markerless six-degree-of-freedom tracking of a physical LEGO airplane manipulative for use in a mixed-reality educational application running on a standalone headset. The researchers developed a pipeline using a compact YOLO model trained on synthetically rendered images to predict keypoints from the physical object, which are then passed to a perspective-n-point solver to estimate the object's pose. Evaluations on synthetic validation images showed that cropping the input around the object of interest substantially improved detection rates and keypoint performance compared to using uncropped images. On-device testing demonstrated that the system could maintain a high display frame rate at a tracking frequency of two Hz, and a qualitative demonstration confirmed that virtual overlays aligned with the physical airplane following manual rotation. The authors acknowledge that quantitative pose accuracy on real headset footage remains to be assessed in future work.
items.citation: Guangxi Feng, Philip Yasskin, Wei Yan. Toward On-Device Markerless 6DoF Tracking of a Physical Manipulative on a Mixed-Reality Headset: A Preliminary Study. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Detection of Salmonella Typhimurium using a nanoflower-mediated horseradish peroxidase-linked antibody signal system combined with microfluidic sensors.
items.summary: This paper developed a colorimetric biosensor for detecting the foodborne pathogen Salmonella typhimurium by combining aptamer-based recognition with enzyme-mediated signal amplification. The researchers synthesized three-dimensional nanoflower-shaped organic-inorganic nanocomposites using a one-step method, incorporating horseradish peroxidase-labeled secondary antibodies and Salmonella-specific aptamers into the material as signal labels within a sandwich-type sensing architecture. In the presence of hydrogen peroxide, the horseradish peroxidase oxidizes a colorless substrate into a colored product, enabling visual colorimetric detection, and the system was further integrated with a microfluidic device to simplify operation. The biosensor achieved a broad linear detection range and an exceptionally low detection limit, while also demonstrating good selectivity, reproducibility, and stability. The authors conclude that this platform has strong potential for pathogen detection and on-site rapid screening applications.
items.citation: Yu Y, Zhou H, Bu S et al.. Detection of Salmonella Typhimurium using a nanoflower-mediated horseradish peroxidase-linked antibody signal system combined with microfluidic sensors.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper investigated the rapid detection of *Acinetobacter baumannii* and its carbapenem resistance genes directly in clinical respiratory samples, addressing the limitations of conventional diagnostic methods that are slow and infrastructure-dependent. The researchers developed oligonucleotide-functionalized gold nanoparticle biosensors targeting a conserved region of the *nucAb* gene for species identification and two key carbapenem resistance genes, *bla*OXA-23 and *bla*NDM, without requiring DNA purification or amplification. The biosensors produced visible colorimetric results within thirty minutes and demonstrated a detection limit sufficient for clinically relevant bacterial loads. Notably, the *bla*NDM biosensor also detected resistance gene variants across multiple other clinically important Gram-negative pathogens, including *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Escherichia coli*, and *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. The authors propose these biosensors as rapid, economical tools to support early clinical decision-making and antimicrobial resistance surveillance.
items.citation: Chalana A, Gupta V, Sharma P et al.. Rapid visual and direct detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem resistance by oligoDNA-gold nanoparticles biosensor in clinical samples.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.
items.summary: The paper describes the development of an electrochemical biosensor platform called SHIELD, designed to detect viable foodborne pathogens with high sensitivity and specificity. The system addresses a key challenge in food safety diagnostics: distinguishing living bacteria from dead ones, which can otherwise generate false-positive signals. To achieve this, the platform combines Propidium Monoazide pretreatment to chemically block DNA from dead cells, isothermal amplification to generate abundant target sequences, and Argonaute-guided cleavage of dual-labeled electrochemical probes, with unreacted probes removed via magnetic separation to produce a clean signal-on readout. By operating in solution rather than on a surface-immobilized format, the design avoids reproducibility problems common to traditional biosensors. The resulting platform demonstrated the ability to detect viable Salmonella typhimurium at extremely low concentrations within a rapid timeframe, suggesting broad applicability for sensitive screening of foodborne pathogens.
items.citation: Qiao J, Bai B, Zhang Y et al.. SHIELD: An Argonaute-powered immobilization-free homogeneous electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive viable pathogen detection.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.
items.summary: The paper describes the development of a photoelectrochemical biosensor designed to detect a specific gene fragment from *Legionella pneumophila*, the pathogen responsible for Legionnaires' disease. The biosensor was constructed using a perylene-based compound as a photoactive material to generate a strong initial photocurrent, with gold nanoparticles electrodeposited on the electrode surface to anchor a DNA probe strand. Upon hybridization with the target gene sequence, a cobalt porphyrin compound intercalated into the resulting DNA duplex and quenched the photocurrent signal, enabling quantitative detection. The sensor achieved a wide linear detection range and an exceptionally low detection limit in the femtomolar range, demonstrating high sensitivity. The authors propose this platform as a promising tool for practical screening of *Legionella pneumophila* in respiratory specimens with high bacterial loads.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Zhang F, Lu L, Li S et al.. Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.. Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review
items.citation: Yang T, Ling Y, Zhang E et al.. Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Cross-validated SPR/SERS dual-mode fiber biosensor for rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in foods.
items.summary: This paper developed a portable fiber-optic biosensor that simultaneously uses surface plasmon resonance and surface-enhanced Raman scattering to detect the foodborne pathogen Salmonella Typhimurium in food samples. The sensing platform employs sea-urchin-shaped gold/silver nanoparticles conjugated with bacteriophage-based recognition probes, which form sandwich complexes on tapered optical fibers coated with a complementary phage capture layer, allowing both detection modalities to be read from a single binding event. The SPR channel provided a wide linear detection range extending from low to high bacterial concentrations with a very low detection limit, while the SERS channel offered a similarly broad range, and the entire workflow was completed within about half an hour. The biosensor was validated against fish, vegetable, and milk matrices, demonstrating good accuracy and resistance to matrix interference. Critically, the two independent signal outputs serve as mutual cross-verification, substantially reducing false-positive results and improving overall detection reliability for field-deployable food safety applications.
items.citation: Zhu S, Su Y, Wang Y et al.. Cross-validated SPR/SERS dual-mode fiber biosensor for rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in foods.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Efficient generation of epitope-targeted antibodies with Germinal
items.citation: Luis Santiago Mille, Claudia L. Driscoll, John N. Wang et al.. Efficient generation of epitope-targeted antibodies with Germinal. Nature Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape
items.summary: The paper investigated the evolutionary dynamics of affinity maturation in germinal centers, where B cells undergo Darwinian selection to produce increasingly potent antibodies. The researchers developed an experimental evolution model by replaying over one hundred monoclonal germinal center reactions and used deep mutational scanning to assign affinity values to individual cells, constructing a quantified affinity landscape. They found that germinal centers achieve predictable evolutionary outcomes through noisy but persistent selection, with the exploration of sequence space heavily constrained by somatic hypermutation biases. By inferring a fitness landscape that quantitatively reproduces the affinity maturation trajectory, they demonstrated that previously observed features such as tolerance for low-affinity lineages and rapid affinity plateauing are likely artifacts of survivorship bias rather than true properties of the selection process. These findings clarify how germinal center evolution is shaped by both selective pressures and mutational constraints, while cautioning that observational biases can fundamentally distort interpretations of B cell affinity progression over time.
items.citation: William S. DeWitt, Ashni A. Vora, Tatsuya Araki et al.. Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape. Cell. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: This review examines the development of ferrite-based nanomaterials as multifunctional biomedical platforms, tracing their evolution from basic magnetic contrast agents to sophisticated systems capable of actively modulating biological microenvironments. The authors survey how atomic-level engineering strategies—including cation distribution, defect modulation, and morphological anisotropy—can be used to tune magnetic, catalytic, and thermal properties in both spinel and hexagonal ferrite structures. Applications discussed span established uses in MRI and drug delivery as well as emerging areas such as viscosity-independent magnetic hyperthermia, reactive oxygen species-mediated antimicrobial therapy, and magnetic tissue engineering. The review critically identifies key barriers preventing clinical translation, including discrepancies between colloidal and intracellular heating efficiency, protein corona complexity, and the difficulty of achieving scalable, GMP-compliant synthesis. The authors conclude by proposing a development roadmap that integrates artificial intelligence-driven material discovery and green chemistry to advance next-generation magnetotheranostic systems for precision medicine.
items.citation: Pramod D. Mhase, Varsha C. Pujari, Akash V. Fulari et al.. Recent Advances in Ferrite‐Based Materials for Biomedical Applications: A Comprehensive Review. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future trajectory of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for cancer, addressing the need for rapid, accessible testing outside centralized laboratory settings. The authors survey a broad range of enabling technologies, including microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip platforms, nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors, and smartphone-integrated devices, alongside advances in sample preparation and detection of nucleic acid and protein biomarkers. Clinical requirements are illustrated through case studies drawn from diverse oncology settings, grounding the technological discussion in real-world diagnostic scenarios. The review also analyzes funding landscapes, intellectual property considerations, and regulatory frameworks that govern the translation of these technologies from research to commercial use. The authors conclude that interdisciplinary innovation, equitable access, and integration with precision medicine will be central to establishing point-of-care molecular diagnostics as transformative tools for cancer detection, therapy selection, and treatment monitoring.
items.citation: Seemesh Bhaskar, Saurabh Umrao, Hankeun Lee et al.. Point of care molecular cancer diagnostics. Lab on a Chip. 2026

items.title: Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses
items.summary: This paper investigated how hedgehog merbecoviruses — relatives of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus circulating in European and Asian hedgehogs — gain entry into host cells. Using cell-based assays, pseudotype experiments with a vesicular stomatitis virus reporter system, and protein binding assays, the researchers identified aminopeptidase N (APN) as the functional entry receptor for these viruses. They found that spike protein-mediated infectivity was enhanced at temperatures matching the hedgehog's physiological body temperature rather than the standard mammalian temperature, and a broad screen of mammalian APN orthologues revealed restricted cross-species receptor usage, with human APN unable to support infection. Electron cryomicroscopy showed that the glycoprotein–receptor interface is structurally distinct from previously characterized coronavirus spike–APN interactions, providing a molecular explanation for the observed species barrier. These findings clarify the receptor biology of hedgehog merbecoviruses and contribute to assessments of their potential for zoonotic emergence.
items.citation: Min Jin, Victoria A. Jefferson, Zhe Zhao et al.. Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses. Nature Microbiology. 2026

items.title: A multimodal adaptive optical microscope for in vivo imaging from molecules to organisms
items.summary: This paper presents MOSAIC, a reconfigurable multimodal microscope designed to address the challenge of studying biological systems across vastly different spatial and temporal scales within complex native environments. The instrument integrates multiple advanced imaging modalities — including light-sheet, label-free, super-resolution, and multiphoton microscopy — all augmented with adaptive optics to correct for sample-induced aberrations. The authors demonstrate that MOSAIC enables noninvasive imaging of subcellular dynamics in cultured cells and live multicellular organisms, nanoscale mapping of molecular architectures across large expanded tissue samples, and structural and functional neural imaging in live mice. By allowing correlative studies across biological scales within the same specimen, MOSAIC overcomes the typical limitation of single-purpose microscopes that sacrifice versatility for performance. The platform is presented as an integrated solution for broad biological investigation spanning molecules to whole organisms.
items.citation: Tian-ming Fu B, Gaoxiang Liu, Daniel Edward Milkie et al.. A multimodal adaptive optical microscope for in vivo imaging from molecules to organisms. Nature Methods. 2026

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: This paper investigates the challenge of monitoring maritime vessels by fusing two complementary data sources: the Automatic Identification System, which provides vessel identification but has known vulnerabilities, and space-based radio frequency observations, which detect vessel activity independently but cannot identify ships on their own. Following a structured data science methodology, the researchers developed and applied a Pair Hidden Markov Model to align individual radio frequency detections with AIS vessel trajectories by jointly modeling temporal and spatial information along with noise and timing discrepancies. The approach was evaluated on real AIS data combined with synthetic radio frequency detections, benchmarked against nearest-neighbor baselines, and analyzed for systematic biases related to trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity, and spatial separation. A log-odds scoring variant that compares the full matching model against a null model substantially improved both pairing precision and the ability to detect vessels behaving suspiciously, though both metrics remained below those of a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline that requires no parameter fitting. The study concludes that this single-detection Pair Hidden Markov Model formulation closely approaches but does not surpass the hand-designed baseline, highlighting remaining biases and directions for further refinement.
items.citation: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.. Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
items.summary: The paper studies the problem of detecting slope changes in multidimensional time series by fitting continuous piecewise-linear functions that share a single breakpoint, examining both a dense setting where all dimensions may change slope and a sparse setting where at most a fixed number of dimensions may do so. Despite the resulting optimization problems being nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear programs that can even yield irrational solutions for rational inputs, the authors prove that all six problem variants across three common loss functions are exactly solvable in polynomial time. They derive efficient algorithms for the least-squares case with explicit operation counts that scale jointly in the number of dimensions and time points, and implement these for empirical evaluation. Testing on simulated data and three real-world datasets covering climate, motion tracking, and industrial sensor domains, the algorithms handle very large instances in well under a second on standard hardware. Compared to a general-purpose mixed-integer nonlinear programming solver, the proposed algorithms are faster by several orders of magnitude, while the solver frequently fails to find near-optimal solutions within a generous time limit on larger instances.
items.citation: Apoorva Narula, Santanu S. Dey. Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: This paper investigated whether a technique called Concept Induction can reveal what convolutional neural network hidden layers actually represent when networks exploit contextual background information rather than target objects to classify agricultural images. The researchers applied this approach across five agricultural datasets with varying degrees of contextual bias, examining four CNN architectures at different network depths and multiple image patch locations, encoding quantitative image descriptors into a knowledge graph to derive logical expressions characterizing neuron activations. They found that a substantial minority of tested neuron-feature pairs were validated, with intermediate network depths showing the highest validation rates and texture-related features such as edge, Gabor, and Tamura descriptors being most frequently validated. Importantly, the degree of contextual bias in a dataset did not predict how interpretable the corresponding hidden neurons were, suggesting that a network's behavioral reliance on background context and the semantic interpretability of its internal representations are distinct phenomena. The authors conclude that Concept Induction can usefully complement existing patch-based methods for detecting contextual bias by providing insight into what hidden neurons encode.
items.citation: Abhilekha Dalal, Avishek Das, Samatha Ereshi Akkamahadevi. Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of detecting out-of-distribution objects in real-world deployment of object detectors by framing each detected bounding box decision as a hypothesis test. The authors identify that the null distribution of in-distribution boxes varies systematically with box size and border contact, factors the detector already observes, and argue that boxes should only be compared against in-distribution boxes sharing these same characteristics. Building on this insight, they propose reading features from before the classification layers, since later layers optimized for known classes discard information that distinguishes unknown objects. The resulting method, PLUM, is a training-free scoring approach that pools features from the last backbone stage within a box and measures their distance to in-distribution classes conditioned on box size and border contact, achieving leading out-of-distribution detection performance on standard benchmarks without requiring external models.
items.citation: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang. Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: This paper investigates whether Redshift Space Distortions (RSD), including leading-order general relativistic corrections, can mimic parity violation in measurements of the galaxy four-point correlation function (4PCF). The authors analyzed the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density to third order using Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory, incorporating tidal bias, wide-angle effects through a local line-of-sight definition, and an arbitrary cosmological background. By expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, they demonstrated that angular momentum selection rules encoded in Wigner 3-j symbols force all parity-odd contributions from RSD to vanish upon averaging over all line-of-sight orientations, in both the plane-parallel and full wide-angle cases. This finding holds for the isotropic 4PCF estimator and extends prior trispectrum results to a more general setting. The result is significant for large-scale structure analyses because it supports the interpretation that any detected parity-violation signal in the isotropic 4PCF cannot be attributed to RSD as a systematic artifact.
items.citation: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.. Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of coherent demodulation for audio frequency-shift keying signals used in CubeSat communications, where the severe line-of-sight dynamics of low Earth orbit typically make coherent detection impractical due to synchronization degradation. The authors developed an all-digital coherent demodulator that combines a Kalman filter for carrier phase and timing synchronization with the Viterbi algorithm for maximum likelihood sequence detection, with detected bit statistics fed back to estimate phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift. Original mathematical analyses were derived to characterize synchronization accuracy under realistic low Earth orbit conditions, and the system was evaluated using simulated real CubeSat orbits over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. The proposed coherent demodulator achieves a substantial gain in bit error rate performance compared to conventional noncoherent AFSK demodulation, demonstrating that coherent detection can be made viable even under intense orbital dynamics.
items.citation: Rubem Vasconcelos Pacelli, Rodrigo de Lima Florindo, Felix Antreich et al.. An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications. arXiv. 2026
